docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Windows EDR · v1.29.1

No log lake.No cloud.No blind trust.

Plasma keeps the telemetry on the box, answers questions with a 121M on-device model, and makes every response named, journaled, and reversible. The endpoint can explain itself — without shipping its diary anywhere.

Get started Download v1.29.1 Agent-native operation 94.6% rollup coverage 13 reversible actions 25 baseline rules 1051 tests Signed MSI + SHA256SUMS SENSORS Everything stays on the box

Sysmon, WHIDS gene rules, identity Event Log API, an ETW tap, persistence probes, canaries and DTrace — normalised into one strict JSONL contract.

ON-DEVICE A 121M model that refuses

Frozen neuralOS instance picks from a closed menu of probes and says unknown when it is — no cloud round-trip, no hallucinated answer.

ORCHESTRATION neuralOSd in front

An optional local orchestrator with 20 typed probes, a refusal gate and a signed envelope. The model proposes; the operator applies. Read the guide.

RESPONSE Reversible by construction

Plan-gated actions with single-use approvals, a hash-chained provenance ledger, a kill switch and undo for every change.

PREVENTION Off until you arm it

enforce contains in seconds; prevent configures AppLocker, firewall egress, ASR, LSA, CFA, Network Protection and the driver blocklist. Dry-run first, journaled, rollbackable — no Plasma kernel driver.

Detects always. Contains only when armed. Blocks only through Microsoft's own enforcement points.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
# 1. download the current release binary
#    https://github.com/DrOlu/plasma/releases/latest

# 2. install (intelligent mode choice: FULL or MINIMAL)
.\plasma-<version>-windows-x64.exe install

# 3. verify
plasma health
plasma identity pull --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl --since 60
plasma watch once

# 4. optional: see what prevention would do (nothing is applied)
plasma enforce run
plasma prevent status
plasma prevent posture
plasma query --kind alert --min-score 0.7 --since 24h

Every command prints JSON and uses meaningful exit codes, so it composes with Task Scheduler, cron or another agent.

docs.title: Why it's different
docs.text:
Commercial EDR ships every event to a central lake and asks you to trust the vendor's console. SIEM does the same one layer up. Plasma starts from the opposite question: what can one machine answer about itself, honestly, without sending its diary anywhere?

Every other EDR / SIEM Plasma Streams events to a vendor cloud Normalizes them on the box into one local JSONL contract Central lake required for correlation A desk pulls bounded tails and correlates only when asked Model in the cloud decides A 121M on-device model picks from a closed menu of probes Response is a vendor API call Response is named, allowlisted and dry-run first; containment is policy-gated; prevention uses Windows enforcement points "Trust us" Manifest digests, SHA256SUMS, pinned signer thumbprints, and a refusal gate

docs.title: The layers
docs.text:
SENSORS            Sysmon · WHIDS gene rules · Security-log identity ·
                   ETW tap · deep persistence probe · canary tokens · memory scan
EXTENSIONS         plugin sensors · detectors · responders (signed process ABI)
        │
        ▼  one strict event contract (events.jsonl, on the box)
ON-DEVICE BRAIN    frozen neuralOS instance — 10 probes, refuse-if-unknown
        │
        ▼  optional: local model + refusal gate + 20-probe menu
ORCHESTRATOR       neuralOSd — plan/apply/undo over the same typed tools
        │
        ▼  pull-based answers over WinRM/SSM, never a standing server
DESK               status · ask · query · tree · summarize · case ·
                   drift · chains · coverage · fleet ·
                   watch + alerts · plan-gated response (actuate)
        │
        ▼  measured, policy-gated, journaled
PROTECTION         enforce (snapshot + kill at 9+, approval for the rest) ·
                   prevent (AppLocker, egress, ASR, LSA, CFA, Network Protection) ·
                   intercept (NTFS ACL, firewall, agent gateway)

docs.title: Estate-wide correlation
docs.text:
The estate edge ledger is the standing counterpart to fleet cases: hosts ship hash-sealed counts, the desk merges and correlates them, and no event diary moves.

Finding Score Rule estate_user_fanout 9 one account on many hosts, with a source address shared across at least two estate_user_fanout 7 same-name pattern without a shared source — verify estate_source_fanout 9 one source address across many hosts estate_stale_host 8 ledger older than --max-age estate_hash_fanout 8 the same file hash on many hosts estate_new_host_edge 7 user/host pair absent from the baseline 
plasma estate sync --inventory inventory.json --out-dir C:\PlasmaEstate --loop
plasma estate findings --ledger C:\PlasmaEstate\estate.json

See Estate edge ledger.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
Plasma plugins are bounded external processes with a signed manifest and an NDJSON contract — the same pattern already used for Sysmon, WHIDS, the ETW tap and DTrace. They can be written in any language and installed without rebuilding Plasma.

Kind What it contributes Command Sensor PlasmaEvents from an app, log or agent plasma plugin run Detector Findings over a bounded event tail plasma plugin run Responder Named actions with preview/apply/rollback plasma plugin act Exporter Reserved for plugin-driven outbound sinks —

The core validates every record, stamps the source, quarantines garbage and keeps ownership of the event store and the response plan gate. Plugins never write events.jsonl directly and never get a shell.

plasma plugin new acme --kind sensor --out C:\build
plasma plugin keygen --out keys
plasma plugin sign --plugin C:\build\acme --key keys\plugin-private.pem
plasma plugin install C:\build\acme --pubkey keys\plugin-public.pem --enable
plasma plugin run acme --max-events 100

Inbound adapters bring other systems in: plasma ingest jsonl|evtx|webhook. Outbound adapters push bounded batches: plasma export webhook|syslog. See Plugins for the manifest, protocol, lifecycle, security model and schemas.

docs.title: What's new in 1.29.1
docs.text:
• Remote ledger integrity. estate sync verifies the SHA-256 of every ledger returned by a host before accepting it; a corrupted reply becomes a recorded host failure, not a merged finding.
  • Atomic findings. findings.json is replaced atomically, like estate.json and the per-host ledgers, so a reader never sees a half-written cycle.

docs.title: What's new in 1.29.0
docs.text:
• Estate edge ledger. Each host reduces its own store to a small hash-sealed count ledger — users, sources, user>process pairs and hashes, never command lines or file paths. The desk replaces the newest ledger per host, merges and correlates.
  • Continuous sync. plasma estate sync pulls in parallel over WinRM or files, writes estate.json and findings.json, survives a failed host, and runs on a cadence with --loop.
  • Five cross-host findings. User fan-out (9 when a shared source links the appearances, 7 for a same-name pattern), source fan-out, shared file hashes, stale hosts and new host edges against a baseline.
  • Bounded at scale. 200 users and 256 KiB per host ledger; 5,000 identities on the desk. A 1,000-host, 10,000-identity estate merges and correlates in seconds. SHA-256 integrity on every ledger.

docs.title: What's new in 1.28.1
docs.text: • Responder arguments from a file. plasma plugin act --args-file avoids Windows native-argument quoting when an action takes a path.

docs.title: What's new in 1.28.0
docs.text:
• Plugin ABI. Sensors, detectors, responders and exporters run as bounded external processes with signed manifests and an NDJSON contract. Validation, quarantine, dedupe and the store stay core-owned.
  • Plan-gated responders. plugin act previews exact argv; apply needs the plan id and a reason, checks the kill switch and journals the rollback.
  • Two-way integration. ingest covers JSONL, Event Log and HMAC webhooks; export covers webhook and syslog with a capped spool.
  • Signed and scaffolded. Ed25519 keygen/sign/verify, pinned keys and plugin new.

docs.title: What's new in 1.27.7
docs.text:
• TTPForge-driven coverage. Masqueraded system binaries, PowerShell WebClient/Invoke-WebRequest downloads, WMI reconnaissance over 4104, and wmic query reconnaissance.
  • Query self-match fixed. plasma query --contains no longer returns the query process itself.

docs.title: What's new in 1.27.1
docs.text: • Calibrated on a real estate. Routine Windows servicing no longer reads as critical: children of signed service hosts are damped, and the critical band starts at 9.5.

docs.title: What's new in 1.27.0
docs.text:
• Profiles, not a lake. Each host keeps a compact behaviour baseline: counts and robust statistics, never event rows or full command lines. Profiles carry an integrity hash and merge into an estate baseline.
  • Explainable anomaly scores. plasma anomaly score fuses rarity, first-seen keys, daily-volume z-scores and optional estate rarity; every result names the counts behind it. Cold profiles return no score.
  • Causal traces. plasma anomaly trace rebuilds PID/PPID trees on one host and scores them by edge rarity. RDP/SMB hops start a new tree.
  • Estate pulls only profiles. plasma fleet profiles builds on the endpoint and moves kilobytes, not telemetry.

docs.title: What's new in 1.26.6
docs.text: • Chain precision, again. schtasks /delete (cleanup) no longer counts as persistence — only /create does — and events spawned by Plasma's own binaries are excluded from the persistence step.

docs.title: What's new in 1.26.5
docs.text: • One fewer chain false positive. A read-only Get-ScheduledTask query no longer completes persistence_after_privilege; the step now requires schtasks.

docs.title: What's new in 1.26.4
docs.text:
• Rules that actually reach the alert log. The three new detection rules were raised to criticality 6 after estate testing showed WHIDS silently dropping anything at or below its forwarding threshold of 5.
  • Validation guard. plasma detect validate now warns when a gene's criticality is at or below that threshold.

docs.title: What's new in 1.26.3
docs.text:
• Encoded PowerShell coverage. Plasma Encoded Cmd now covers the -e alias as well as -enc, -ec and -encodedcommand, with a base64 guard.
  • More Atomic-driven coverage. New low/medium rules for sensitive-path deletion, attrib +h, and Explorer file-extension/hidden-file registry changes.
  • Less Sigma noise. PowerShell's __PSScriptPolicyTest temp file is suppressed at info/0.2 instead of firing high-criticality public-folder/SharePoint rules.
  • Better chains. persistence_after_privilege now recognises sc.exe create and reg add ...\Run, in addition to scheduled tasks and services.
  • Atomic smoke suite. sensors/atomic-smoke.json, tests/test_atomic_fixes.py and docs/atomic-smoke.md add a six-case release-validation subset.

docs.title: What's new in 1.26.2
docs.text:
• Boot-time enforcement. PlasmaWatch, PlasmaWhidsWatchdog and PlasmaCanaryShield now carry both an AtStartup trigger and StartWhenAvailable. A reboot or missed timer run no longer waits for the next interval.
  • Bounded task runs. Restart-on-failure, non-overlapping execution and execution time limits stop a hung sweep from wedging the schedule.
  • Health drift detection. plasma health reports present Plasma tasks that lack an AtStartup trigger.

docs.title: What's new in 1.26.1
docs.text: • Architecture diagram polish. Removed overlapping labels and rerouted the WinRM, optional API and SIEM links in the enterprise illustration; PDFs regenerated. No runtime behavior change.

docs.title: What's new in 1.26.0
docs.text:
• Named-pipe canaries. canary pipe deploy|list|remove|serve|install|uninstall adds decoy pipes. The SYSTEM listener gets the connecting client PID with GetNamedPipeClientProcessId, verifies it, refuses protected/trusted processes, and kills. Enumeration alone is not a connection.
  • Proper architecture diagram. The enterprise deployment page now uses a real SVG illustration instead of ASCII art.
  • Enterprise guide expanded with pipe-canary rollout, scanner caveats and disarm steps.
  • 943 tests, full suite and -W error pass.

docs.title: What's new in 1.25.0
docs.text:
• Active canary shield. File and registry canaries can now kill the process that writes or deletes them. A narrow Sysmon include feeds a one-minute SYSTEM sweep; the sweep verifies the live PID and image, refuses protected/trusted processes, then kills and journals.
  • No read false positives. Merely opening or reading a canary does not trigger. Explorer, Plasma, Defender and common backup/system processes are skipped; the boundary is explicit.
  • Registry canaries. canary registry deploy|list|remove adds decoy registry keys watched by the same narrow RegistryEvent include.
  • Enterprise deployment guide. A new AD-domain installation, configuration, GPO/SCCM/Intune, fleet, canary-shield and operations guide.
  • 933 tests, full suite and -W error pass.

docs.title: What's new in 1.24.1
docs.text:
• Structured refusal for ACL intercept. intercept apply on an ACL rule with no matching canary now returns a JSON refusal instead of a traceback.
  • Structured refusal for bad summaries. summarize --since with an invalid duration returns a JSON query error instead of a traceback.
  • 921 tests, full suite and -W error pass.

docs.title: What's new in 1.24.0
docs.text:
• Opt-in Defender controls. prevent cfa, prevent network and prevent driver-blocklist now preview, apply, verify and roll back with the same plan gate as AppLocker and ASR. WDAC stays read-only.
  • Rollback that proves itself. The previous value is captured at apply time and rollback verifies the restored value, not just the command exit.
  • Detection regression suite. plasma detect test runs deterministic hit/miss cases for phishing, brute force, Kerberos spray, privilege to persistence, account creation and injection.
  • Hardened network fetches. Every download is HTTPS-only, with no embedded credentials or control characters.
  • True read-only MCP reads. get_case renders in memory and no longer writes a report file.
  • 919 tests, full suite and -W error pass.

docs.title: What's new in 1.23.0
docs.text:
• Typed investigation. plasma query is a closed local query language; plasma tree follows explicit PID lineage; plasma summarize produces a bounded digest for agent context.
  • Case workspace. plasma case collects selected events and findings, records operator notes, renders a report and seals the artifacts with a hash manifest. case verify detects later changes.
  • Triggered memory triage. plasma memory triage scans only PIDs selected by injection- or credential-shaped alerts.
  • Identity coverage. Account creation/enable/reset, group membership, explicit credentials, special privileges and directory access now normalize into the event contract, with parent PID retained on 4688.
  • Detection harness. plasma detect validate|diff|replay compiles rule regexes, compares rule sets and replays chains over a capture.
  • Honest posture. health now accounts for blind spots and canary tamper; prevent posture reads WDAC, Controlled Folder Access, Network Protection and the vulnerable driver blocklist.
  • Agent surface. Eight new typed MCP tools, including query_events, get_process_tree, get_summary, get_case and simulate_policy.
  • 900 tests, full suite and -W error pass.

docs.title: What's new in 1.21.0
docs.text:
• Interception phases 0-3. plasma intercept adds shadow rule evaluation, NTFS canary protection, an MCP tool-call gateway and a native ACL/firewall policy broker.
  • Plan-gated and reversible. Every apply is dry-run first, single-use, payload-bound, journaled and reversible. No kernel driver.
  • Estate-verified on WS1 and WS2: canary write denial and rollback, firewall apply/rollback, shadow matches and an MCP INTERCEPTED response.
  • 833 tests, full suite and -W error pass.

docs.title: What's new in 1.20.1
docs.text:
• Root help matches the feature set. plasma --help now names canary files and native DNS/HTTP tokens in the intro, not just "canary decoys".
  • No behavior change; this is a help/documentation patch on top of 1.20.0.

docs.title: What's new in 1.20.0
docs.text:
• Native canary tokens. File canaries now use randomized, believable documents; DNS tokens are observed through a narrow Sysmon EID 22 include; HTTP tokens use a loopback-first local collector. No Docker, no cloud.
  • One evidence path. DNS/HTTP hits become source="canary" alerts, watch surfaces them, fleet correlates them, and enforcement maps them to approval-gated isolation.
  • Canary accounts are in the sweep. Configure canary.accounts and every watch sweep checks 4624/4625/4771/4776 with deduplication.
  • Field-verified on WS1 and WS2: file deploy/verify/tamper, a real Sysmon EID 22 query, an HTTP collector hit, watch findings, and a real 4625 on a disabled canary account.
  • 823 tests, full suite and -W error pass, ruff check clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.19.3
docs.text:
• MSI upgrades converge the running node. The package now runs install --force --rotate, which swaps bin\plasma.exe and restarts the registered tasks after staging the new version. Before this, an MSI upgrade updated the files and config but left the service on the old binary.
  • Rotation is all-or-nothing. A failed canonical swap returns exit 4 with the rotation detail instead of reporting a successful install.
  • Verified on WS2: silent MSI install exits 0, bin\plasma.exe --version and /healthz both report 1.19.3.
  • 788 tests, full suite and -W error pass, ruff check clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.19.2
docs.text:
• The MSI is now Authenticode-signed in the release workflow, using the same PFX and timestamp as the exe. SHA256SUMS covers the signed MSI.
  • The MSI is built with -arch x64, so it installs under C:\Program Files\Plasma instead of Program Files (x86).
  • Verified on WS2: silent MSI install exits 0, the installed exe and /healthz report 1.19.2.
  • 786 tests, full suite and -W error pass, ruff check clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.19.1
docs.text:
• HTTP boundary hardened. Parsed command paths replace text scanning, read-only covers every mutating command, the default key is loopback-only, TLS handshakes run in worker threads, request desync is blocked, output is read under a hard byte cap, and mutations fail closed when auditing fails.
  • Response and prevention hardened. Kill switch covers undo and prevention, approvals re-check policy and are atomic, protected paths/processes/tasks are canonicalized, plans are identity- and time-bound, capture failure gates automatic kills, and prevention rollback is plan-gated and verified.
  • Collection and data hardened. Tap/observatory redaction, identity failure reporting, malformed WHIDS/watch rows skipped, content-aware dedupe, trace/MSI validation, deep persistence parsing, BOM-safe stores, canary/fleet/health/Sigma/notify/FIM fixes.
  • Install/update hardened. Dry-run is read-only, operator config is preserved, Sysmon and updates require valid signatures, ring/hold/promote logic is fixed, rotation/rollback/locking is robust, prerelease ordering is correct.
  • Agent trust hardened. Policy type validation, fail-closed tenants, ledger truncation detection, terminal denials and single-use approvals.
  • 785 tests, full suite and -W error pass, ruff check clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.19.0
docs.text:
• Every command has a detailed help page. plasma <command> --help includes a description, working examples, notes, safety, output and related commands. -h works everywhere.
  • plasma help is the discovery command. No topic prints the grouped command map and the dry-run → plan → apply workflow; a topic prints one detailed page.
  • plasma help --json is the machine catalog. Schema plasma.help/1 lists every command path, usage, argument, default, choice, example, safety class and see-also. One topic narrows it.
  • The HTTP API carries the same metadata. /v1/commands rows include summary, description, examples and safety; help --json is runnable through /v1/exec.

docs.title: What's new in 1.18.0
docs.text:
• Measured self-update. plasma update auto checks the latest release and applies it through the existing SHA256 + Authenticode + install + rotate path. Signed releases only.
  • PlasmaUpdate daily SYSTEM task with a random minute inside the 02:00–05:00 maintenance window. --no-autoupdate disables it.
  • Ring-aware: broad waits 24 hours; canary updates immediately; rollback never auto-updates. The kill switch pauses updates.
  • Previous binary kept. plasma rollback still restores it; the canonical plasma.exe is rotated and PlasmaServe is restarted after a successful update.
  • update-journal.jsonl and update-state.json record every attempt.
  • 731 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.17.1
docs.text:
• Critical process-guard fix. _g_process wrapped the Get-CimInstance assignment in parentheses, so PowerShell emitted the whole CIM object as a formatted table. The guard compared table text to PROTECTED_PROCESSES, and kill_process on LSASS, CSRSS, SERVICES, WINLOGON, WHIDS or Sysmon minted a dry-run plan instead of refusing. The assignment is now bare and the guard refuses as designed.
  • 716 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.17.0
docs.text:
• Measured protection is armed by default. Automatic containment is limited to snapshot + kill_process at score 9+, with a 2-action per-run cap and a 30-minute cooldown. The snapshot is written before the kill.
  • Everything else stays human-approved. Host isolation, quarantine, disabling users, removing admins, stopping services, credential rotation, task/Run-key/WMI removal and IP blocking require approval.
  • PlasmaWatch drives the sweep. A SYSTEM task runs watch once --enforce every 5 minutes. --no-autoprotect installs the old dry-run posture and removes the task.
  • Protected components stay protected in code. WinRM, RDP, WHIDS, Sysmon, LSASS, BFE, MpsSvc, Administrator, SYSTEM and service accounts are refused; isolation keeps RDP/WinRM open.
  • New plasma protect commands: status, arm, disarm, protected.
  • 715 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.16.3
docs.text:
• Command-tree type metadata. /v1/commands now reports type (int, str, or null) for every option and positional. The OpenAPI Option and Positional schemas require the field.
  • 698 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.16.2
docs.text:
• Serve hardening. Serialized argparse validation, byte-safe API-key comparison, 411 for missing Content-Length, socket timeouts, broken-pipe handling, UTF-8 child I/O, stdin=DEVNULL, and process-tree kill on timeout.
  • Audit reliability and redaction. Serialized audit appends, a 30 s lock timeout, failed-write logging, and redaction of --prompt values and credential-shaped argv items.
  • Command tree completeness. /v1/commands returns a separate root and 127 commands, each with positionals as well as options. The OpenAPI schemas describe both.
  • Explicit lifecycles. plasma/lifecycle.py names the serve request, plan, approval, enforcement, prevention, WHIDS, FIM, canary, drift, identity-schedule, capture, fleet, kill-switch, tenant and ring machines, with pure classifiers used by the modules.
  • 698 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.16.1
docs.text:
• OpenAPI 3.1 for plasma serve. GET /openapi.json publishes the spec; GET /docs serves a self-contained HTML reference. Both are unauthenticated. The spec covers the four API routes, both auth schemes and the error envelopes.
  • 674 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.16.0
docs.text:
• plasma serve — the full CLI over HTTP. POST /v1/exec takes an argv list and runs it through the real parser, so every command, flag and default is available exactly as it is on the command line. GET /v1/commands returns the full command tree.
  • API-key auth, read-only mode, TLS, audit and hard timeouts. The default bind is loopback and non-loopback binds refuse the default key; --api-key-file or PLASMA_SERVE_API_KEY overrides it. --read-only refuses every mutating command. Every call lands in <root>/serve/audit.jsonl.
  • 667 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.15.9
docs.text:
• observe canary filters server-side. The collector pulled every 4624/4625 for seven days and timed out at 240 s on a busy DC. It now uses a FilterXPath on TargetUserName, so only canary logons cross the wire.
  • 639 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.15.8
docs.text:
• Observatory collectors get 240 s. observe edges and observe canary exceeded the 90 s limit on a busy domain controller.
  • Fleet pull ships in the frozen exe. pywinrm is now collected by PyInstaller, so plasma fleet scan works from the single-file binary.
  • Terminal approvals leave the queue. control approvals list hides approval_invalid, denied and expired rows; the ledger keeps history.
  • 638 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.15.7
docs.text:
• remove_run_key accepts the canonical registry spelling. The allowlist regex was case-sensitive and expected SOFTWARE; the real key is Software, so every HKCU:\Software\...\Run target was refused. The regex is now case-insensitive.
  • 637 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.15.6
docs.text:
• WHIDS storm_first_ts alerts validate. The strict contract carries the timestamp WHIDS writes on storm alerts. WS1 parses 24,965/24,965 events; WS2 90,724/90,724.
  • 636 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.15.5
docs.text:
• WHIDS storm_count alerts validate. The strict contract carries the integer storm_count WHIDS writes on storm alerts. WS1 now parses 24,874/24,874 events; WS2 89,603/89,603.
  • 635 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.15.4
docs.text:
• Long command lines validate. Encoded PowerShell can exceed 8 KiB; cmdline now allows 32 KiB.
  • WHIDS storm alerts validate. The strict contract carries the boolean storm field WHIDS writes on storm alerts.
  • 634 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.15.3
docs.text:
• WHIDS suppressed alerts validate. The strict event contract now carries the suppressed reason WHIDS writes on suppressed alerts.
  • dest_ip accepts workstation names and IPv6 zone IDs. 4776 NTLM events put the calling machine in dest_ip; IPv6 may carry %zone. A 10,000-event sample from each host now validates with zero failures.
  • 633 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.15.2
docs.text:
• DTrace events validate. The strict event contract now accepts source="dtrace", kind="trace", event_id=0 and action="observed". The estate drill had been counting every DTrace row as a parse failure: 1,419/22,818 events on WS1 and 765/77,950 on WS2.
  • Persistence chains read the command line. description matchers now also search cmdline, so a real 4688 net user /add followed by schtasks fires persistence_after_privilege. Findings carry the matched command line as evidence.
  • Snapshot and remove-admin survive domain controllers. The Administrators lookup uses net localgroup Administrators instead of Get-LocalGroupMember -Group 'Administrators', which fails with “group not found” or Win32 error 1789 on some hosts. The same fix covers observatory.sketch.
  • 631 tests, full suite green, ruff clean.

docs.title: What's new in 1.15.1
docs.text:
• Security and state-machine hardening — failed actions are journaled as failed, locks cover the whole operation, the kill switch fails closed, MCP defaults to read-only scopes, update tag pinning works, and manifest verification rejects path traversal.
  • Section-injection predicate fixed — NtMapViewOfSection takes (SectionHandle, ProcessHandle, ...); the script filtered arg0, so it fired on every section map. It now filters arg1. Negative control on WS2: 12 rows/5 s before, 0 after.
  • Telemetry provenance — coverage now derives a third axis from the shipped Sysmon config: live, partial, dormant or unknown per rule and technique. Weighted coverage counts only rules that can actually fire.
  • The dormant rules are live — the config now enables DriverLoad (6), unsigned ImageLoad (7), LSASS ProcessAccess (10) and PipeEvent (17/18), so the LSASS, unsigned-driver and named-pipe rules are no longer inventory. sysmon_config is a health check.
  • Injection depth — four new DTrace scripts (hijack, hollow, section, remote write) and four chains, covering the primitives that leave no RWX flip or no new thread on their own.
  • 259-rule Sigma corpus — the Windows/Sysmon SigmaHQ tree converted, curated and vendored (168 techniques, DRL 1.1, provenance pinned). Coverage moves to 94.6 rollup / 89.2 exact / 85.9 weighted; the blind set is down to input capture (T1056, T1056.001).
  • Capture before containment — enforce writes a host snapshot before the first automatic kill, so the response does not delete the evidence the detection produced.
  • Prevention, two tiers — plasma enforce turns watch findings into policy-gated, reversible containment (injection → kill the accessing process, canary → isolation for approval). plasma prevent configures the Windows enforcement points: AppLocker, firewall egress default-deny, Defender ASR and LSA protection. Off by default, dry-run first, journaled and rollbackable.
  • Full identity plane — 4624/4625 logons, 4768/4769/4770/4771 Kerberos, 4776 NTLM and 4688 process lineage with creator, parent and command line.
  • Coverage provenance — evidence class derived from rule shape, so substr-only techniques are labelled keyword-only. 94.6 rollup / 89.2 exact / 85.9 weighted; blind spots T1056, T1056.001.
  • Sigma, FIM, Sysmon gaps — Sigma→gene conversion, critical-file integrity, and LSASS access / unsigned driver / named-pipe rules.
  • PyYAML is a feature dependency — only sigma convert asks for it.
  • 605 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.9.5
docs.text:
• One handle test, both scripts — inject-rwx now uses the same low-word comparison as inject-remote-thread, so self-RWX can never be misclassified by a 64-bit literal quirk.
  • APC chain — cross-process RWX followed by an APC from the same image inside 30 s forms injection_apc_chain at score 9. inject-apc itself is documented as high-volume.
  • README corrected — WHIDS is detect-only (report); containment is the separate, plan-gated response plane.
  • 492 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.9.4
docs.text:
• Injection precision — inject-rwx now matches RWX with modifier bits and records whether the caller targeted itself or another process. Self-RWX (JIT) scores 5; cross-process RWX scores 8, and only that can satisfy injection_chain.
  • APC coverage — inject-apc witnesses NtQueueApcThread, NtQueueApcThreadEx and NtQueueApcThreadEx2.
  • Positive controls on WS1 and WS2 for self/cross-process RWX, remote threads and APC queueing. 488 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.9.3
docs.text:
• Kernel-boundary injection evidence (T1055) — two reviewed DTrace scripts witness the RWX permission flip (inject-rwx) and thread creation in another process (inject-remote-thread); injection_chain binds both to the same image at score 9.
  • Field-verified on WS1 and WS2 (DTrace Sun D 1.13.1). Coverage stays 91.7% rollup / 75.0% exact / 83.3% weighted; blind spots T1056, T1056.001, T1112.

484 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.9.2
docs.text:
• DTrace descriptions redacted — trace rows can carry command-line detail; the normalized description now passes through the same credential redactor as WHIDS alerts.

475 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.9.1
docs.text:
• ACL hardening fixed for existing installs — 1.9.0 applied an inheritable (OI)(CI) ACE recursively with /T, which left existing files with an inherit-only ACE (empty effective DACL) and Windows refused to execute them. The installer now adds explicit Full Control to every existing child after setting the root inheritance. This also restores nodes upgraded to 1.9.0.
  • 475 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.9.0 — security review
docs.text:
A focused secure-code review of the agent and desk surfaces.

  • MCP context is server-authoritative — _meta tenant/scopes were a self-asserted claim. Tenant and scopes now come from PLASMA_TENANT / PLASMA_SCOPES; trusting client _meta requires an explicit PLASMA_TRUST_CLIENT_META=1. Read tools are tenant-filtered, the health tool checks local-host ownership, and isolate_host is local-only.
  • Approval/allow-list fixes — an explicit allow list can no longer bypass assist/supervised approval. Non-integer approval ids and oversized/malformed JSON-RPC requests are refused without crashing the server.
  • DTrace MSI verification — the downloaded Microsoft MSI must carry a valid Microsoft Authenticode signature before msiexec runs.
  • Notification secrets — webhooks must be HTTPS; Telegram tokens are redacted from error strings.
  • Filesystem — the installer restricts %ProgramData%\Plasma to SYSTEM + Administrators (well-known SIDs), protecting policy, kill-switch, approvals, ledger and events from inherited ProgramData permissions.
  • Fleet transport — WinRM endpoints must be HTTPS unless allow_insecure_winrm: true is set for a controlled lab.
  • Response hardening — isolation also allows outbound RDP/WinRM responses, loopback/broadcast block targets are refused, the current user is protected from disable/rotate, and gene-rule domains are escaped and validated against rule injection.

474 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.8.7
docs.text:
• PowerShell policy-test scratch files are suppressed — every PowerShell start deletes a __PSScriptPolicyTest_*.ps1 file in Temp. That produced fleet shared_hash findings on every host pair (identical content) and a stream of low-value File-Delete alerts. Both are now recognised as PowerShell housekeeping.

454 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.8.6
docs.text:
• Fleet reads a bounded tail over WinRM — the previous base64 read returned the whole events store; a large store exceeded the WinRM envelope and the host answered HTTP 400. The pull now reads only the last ~1 MB (enough for the 200-row cap), then falls back to line mode.

452 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.8.5
docs.text:
• Pull clears the watch backlog counter — after whids pull, the next watch sweep no longer reports the same alert rows as "unpulled".
  • Legacy storm summaries are covered — inverted first/last timestamps from 1.8.3 are normalised before coverage checks, so old storms do not spawn duplicates.

452 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.8.4
docs.text:
• Storm windows are time-ordered — alert files are scanned by path, so a storm spanning rotated logs could record first_ts after last_ts. Groups are sorted before sampling and summarising.

451 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.8.3
docs.text:
• Alert-storm coalescing — a process repeating the same Tcpip service key write 17k times no longer stores 17k rows. whids pull keeps a few samples plus one summary (count, first/last timestamp, max score), and re-pulling is idempotent. watch collapses identical findings into one line with an occurrence count.
  • Why it matters — the signal (one agent looping on a privileged key) stays visible; the diary and the alert budget do not drown in it.

450 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.8.2
docs.text:
• Windows service-path suppression widened — ADFS and Microsoft.NET service binaries also update their service keys during normal operation. They are now suppressed alongside System32/SysWOW64; C:\Windows\Temp, Tasks and Debug are explicitly excluded, and LOLBins keep full score.

448 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.8.1
docs.text:
A short follow-up from the live estate run of 1.8.0.

  • Service-registry false-positive storm fixed — Windows' own service binaries (dns.exe, lsass.exe, DFSRs.exe, AD WebServices) produced 401 criticality-8 alerts on one server during normal servicing. They are now suppressed by System32/SysWOW64 path evidence; reg.exe, sc.exe and PowerShell keep the full score.
  • Fleet shared-hash noise fixed — cmd.exe/powershell.exe hashes are identical on every Windows host and no longer become score-8 cross-host findings. User-path hashes still do.
  • Watch first sweep no longer floods — a fresh install/upgrade starts at the current end of the alert log; only new criticality-8+ alerts are surfaced. Compressed/archived logs are excluded from counts.
  • Run-key suppression narrowed — a Microsoft-signed LOLBin writing a Run key is the technique, not a benign installer.

447 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.8.0
docs.text:
This is the production-hardening release, driven by a full re-test on the Windows estate.

  • WHIDS init hang, root-caused — an oversized Dumps tree inside the install directory made WHIDS' startup ACL reset exceed the SCM timeout. Detect-only nodes now ship with dump hooks off; whids prune and the watchdog move legacy trees out of the install path, not delete them file by file.
  • Watch surfaces lone critical alerts — a criticality-8+ WHIDS alert is reported on the next sweep, with per-file offsets that survive log rotation. Previously only the 25-row growth counter was visible.
  • Fleet false positives cut — lateral movement now requires network logons (type=3/10) and reports linked only when the source address is another host in the case; shared domains/IPs need at least one scored row.
  • Chain user binding — a brute-force burst must end in a success for the same user; another user's success no longer completes the story.
  • Response safety — the kill switch now blocks CLI and playbook applies, rotated credentials are redacted from the journal, quarantine is hash-pinned and refuses protected paths, WMI undo restores bindings by name, isolation verifies management allows before blocking, and the journal is locked, fsynced and id-safe.
  • Collector edge cases — empty stores are no longer "ok", deep persistence no longer flags unsigned Windows binaries, and identity drops malformed domains/timestamps.

440 tests pass (21 skipped).

docs.title: What's new in 1.7.2
docs.text:
• Implicit state machines formalised — update phases, approvals, actuate plans, playbook plans, undo, tenant ownership, rings, canaries and the service lifecycle now have explicit states and single-use transitions.
  • No plan or approval reuse — reusing an actuate/playbook plan or an approval is refused; undo requires its own dry-run.
  • Atomic writes — binary rotation recovers from an interrupted rename; canary manifests are written atomically and deduped.
  • Exclusive tenant ownership — a host belongs to one tenant.

See State machines.

docs.title: What's new in 1.7.0
docs.text:
Plasma is now agent-native, not just agent-adjacent:

  • Capability contract — 20 typed tools with scopes, risk tiers, preconditions and JSON schemas. Unknown tools and extra arguments are refused before anything runs.
  • Deterministic policy engine — assist / supervised / autonomous tiers, deny lists, blast-radius and rate limits. The model never authorises.
  • Provenance ledger — every decision and action is appended to a hash-chained log with harness, model, prompt digest, arguments, policy digest, approval and outcome. plasma control audit verify.
  • Approval queue — high/critical actions return an approval id; a human approves or denies, and the approval is single-use.
  • Kill switch — global and per-host, blocks actions but not reads.
  • MCP server — plasma mcp serve exposes the typed tools over stdio to any harness.
  • Compliance evidence — CBN, NDPA, PCI DSS and ISO 27001 control matrices generated from real state.
  • Assurance — CycloneDX SBOM, safety case and redacted support bundle.
  • Deployment rings — canary/broad assignment and one-command rollback.
  • Safety evals — plasma eval run covers tier behaviour, injections, blast radius, rate limits and refusals.

Read Agent-native operation and the Control plane.

docs.title: What's new in 1.6.x
docs.text:
• Self-healing WHIDS — plasma whids ensure force-stops a hung StartPending and restarts the sensor. The installer registers PlasmaWhidsWatchdog as a SYSTEM task that runs it every two minutes; every action is logged. Crashes are already covered by SCM failure actions; this covers the hang.
  • DTrace provisioning without winget — trace provision downloads the official Microsoft package directly (winget is absent on Server 2022 by default), enables bcdedit /set dtrace on, and is idempotent. Readiness is capability-based: installed + enabled is ready.
  • Trace rows are estate-consistent — the reviewed scripts emit tid, which works across the DTrace builds on Windows Server; pid is not portable between them.
  • Installer convergence — updates re-stage the WHIDS config, rules, binary and Sysmon config from the bundle, and roll back the config once if a new one cannot start.
  • Gene alerts keep their technique — WHIDS 1.7 omits the ATTACK block; Plasma maps the rule name to its technique on ingest.

Prefer a visual tour? Open the one-page overview.

docs.title: What you get in 1.4.0
docs.text:
• Story detection — deterministic chain rules (phish spawn, brute-force success, persistence-after-privilege) that fire on sequences, not single events, and run inside every watch sweep.
  • Honest ATT&CK coverage — 91.9% with parent rollup, 64.7% fidelity-weighted (keyword-only evidence derived and discounted), and the blind spots named out loud.
  • Deep persistence probe — every auto-start location with Authenticode status and a surfaced suspect heuristic; no driver, no service.
  • Signed updates — update apply refuses any binary whose Authenticode signer does not match thumbprints pinned inside the installed exe.
  • Playbooks — contain-user, isolate-box: fixed sequences applied as one plan-gated unit, aborting on the first failure, reversible last-first.
  • Store hygiene — store rotate|compact|stats keeps the diary bounded.
  • Interception — typed rules compiled into NTFS ACLs, Windows Firewall rules and the MCP tool-call gateway; plan-gated and reversible.
  • Canaries and tokens — randomized, believable decoy documents (score 10 on modification/deletion), DNS hostname tokens observed through a narrow Sysmon EID 22 include (score 8), HTTP .url tokens served by a loopback-first local collector (score 8), and configured canary accounts (score 10). All hits land in the same source="canary" event path.
  • MSI + GPO — an enterprise package that provisions a node silently through Group Policy.
  • DTrace, on demand — reviewed, bounded kernel/syscall tracing where the host supports it, normalized into the same event contract.

docs.title: Doctrine
docs.text:
1. Read-only by default. Collectors read. Manual actions require --apply --plan <id> from a seen dry-run.
  2. Containment is armed but narrow; prevention is audit-first. enforce is limited to snapshot + kill_process at score 9+, with isolation and every other action behind approval. prevent does nothing until you apply a plan. Both are policy-gated and journaled.
  3. Deterministic. Detection is written rules and written chains. The model selects probes; it never decides guilt and never runs commands.
  4. Bounded. Every collector has a time window, a row cap and a size cap.
  5. Local. Events never leave the host by default. The desk pulls what it needs.
  6. Reversible. Every applied action or prevention control carries a journal entry and an undo recipe — where something cannot be undone, the CLI says so up front.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:

  • Operating an estate? Operations and Fleet.

docs.title: Agent-native operation
docs.text:
Plasma is designed to be driven by an agent harness — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or a customer's own orchestrator — without giving that harness arbitrary execution.

The rule is simple: the model may investigate and propose; the policy engine decides; the ledger remembers. Autonomy is a policy setting, not a property of the model.

docs.title: The capability contract
docs.text:
Every action is a typed tool with a scope, a risk tier and a JSON schema. Unknown tools and unexpected arguments are refused before anything runs.

Tool Risk Scope In MCP read_events read events:read executes list_findings read events:read executes get_health read health:read executes read_policy read policy:read executes list_approvals read approvals:read executes audit_tail read audit:read executes query_events read events:read executes get_process_tree read events:read executes get_summary read events:read executes get_case read events:read executes get_coverage read events:read executes get_blind_spots read health:read executes get_enforcement_posture read health:read executes simulate_policy read policy:read executes scan_memory medium response:memory dry-run plan deploy_canary medium response:canary dry-run plan contain_user high response:identity dry-run plan isolate_host critical response:network dry-run plan quarantine_file high response:file dry-run plan kill_process critical response:process dry-run plan

Mutating tools are dry-run-only in the MCP surface. The agent receives a plan, a risk tier and (when required) an approval reference. Applying the action stays behind the CLI's plan/approval gate. A hallucinating or prompt-injected model cannot change a host through the tool API.

Canary token creation, collection and hit review are available through the CLI and the authenticated HTTP API (/v1/exec); the MCP deploy_canary tool remains a dry-run plan. Token creation is a local write, not a host change, and canary serve is classified long-running so the HTTP API refuses to start it.

Intercept rules at point: agent_tool_call are evaluated before policy and handlers. A denied call returns INTERCEPTED with the rule id and an audit ledger entry; a shadow rule is audited but allowed. This is the synchronous gateway that lets an operator stop a class of agent action without relying on the model to comply.

docs.title: Autonomy tiers
docs.text:
Set the node's posture with plasma control policy set --autonomy ….

Tier Read tools Low / medium High Critical assist allowed approval approval approval supervised (default) allowed allowed approval approval autonomous allowed allowed allowed approval unless allow_critical

Start at supervised. Move to autonomous only after the eval suite and a purple-team drill pass in that estate.

docs.title: Policy
docs.text:
The policy is a local JSON file (policy.json under the Plasma root). The model never edits it.

{
  "version": 1,
  "autonomy": "supervised",
  "allow": [],
  "deny": ["kill_process"],
  "require_approval": {"high": true, "critical": true},
  "allow_critical": false,
  "max_actions_per_minute": 30,
  "max_hosts_per_action": 1
}

plasma control policy show
plasma control policy set --autonomy supervised --deny kill_process
plasma control policy set --max-actions 20 --max-hosts 1

The policy check is deterministic and runs before every tool call: deny list, scopes, blast radius, rate limit, risk tier, autonomy tier.

docs.title: Approvals
docs.text:
A high-risk call returns a structured refusal with an approval_id:

{
  "ok": false,
  "code": "APPROVAL_REQUIRED",
  "approval_id": 42,
  "tool": "isolate_host",
  "args_sha256": "…",
  "risk": "critical"
}

A human reviews and decides:

plasma control approvals list
plasma control approvals approve 42 --approver ciso --note "confirmed beacon"
plasma control approvals deny 42 --approver ciso --note "false positive"

The approval is bound to the action and the argument hash and can be used once. The agent re-calls the tool with "approval_id": 42; the dry-run plan is then returned and recorded.

docs.title: Provenance ledger
docs.text:
Every decision and action is appended to a hash-chained JSONL ledger before the result is returned to the harness:

{
  "seq": 42,
  "ts": "2026-11-13T19:00:00Z",
  "tenant": "default",
  "kind": "action",
  "agent": "claude-code",
  "model": "…",
  "prompt_sha256": "…",
  "tool": "isolate_host",
  "args": {"host": "WS1"},
  "args_sha256": "…",
  "risk": "critical",
  "decision": "approval_required",
  "policy_sha256": "…",
  "prev": "…",
  "hash": "…"
}

plasma control audit tail --last 20
plasma control audit verify      # exit 2 if the chain is broken

This is the answer to "why did the agent do that?" — harness, model, prompt digest, arguments, policy digest, approval and outcome, in one chain.

docs.title: Kill switch
docs.text:
plasma control killswitch status
plasma control killswitch on --reason "incident drill"
plasma control killswitch on --host WS1 --reason "quarantine"
plasma control killswitch off

Reads remain available; every mutating tool is blocked while the switch is engaged.

docs.title: Trusted context (security)
docs.text:
_meta in an MCP request is supplied by the connecting harness and is not an authorization source. Tenant and scopes come from the server environment:

Variable Meaning PLASMA_TENANT authoritative tenant (default default) PLASMA_SCOPES comma-separated scopes; default * PLASMA_TRUST_CLIENT_META set 1 only for a controlled harness that may claim tenant/scopes in _meta

Read tools are tenant-filtered (events by host ownership, ledger and approvals by tenant). isolate_host is local-only and refuses a claimed remote host. Mutating tools still follow the policy/approval gate and the kill switch.

docs.title: Multi-tenant isolation
docs.text:
plasma control tenants add acme --name "Acme Bank" --host WS9 --host WS10
plasma control tenants list

Ledger rows carry the tenant, and policy checks can scope an agent to one tenant. default cannot be removed.

docs.title: MCP server
docs.text:
Plasma speaks MCP over stdio, so any harness can discover and call the tools.

Register it with Claude Code (bin name varies by release):

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "plasma": {
      "command": "C:\\ProgramData\\Plasma\\bin\\plasma-1.5.0-windows-x64.exe",
      "args": ["mcp", "serve", "--root", "C:\\ProgramData\\Plasma"]
    }
  }
}

Minimal session:

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize"}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_events","arguments":{"limit":20}}}

docs.title: Safety evals
docs.text:
plasma eval run

The suite covers read/action separation, tier behaviour, deny lists, scopes, blast radius, rate limits, kill switch, unknown tools, extra arguments, and prompt-injection strings in arguments. It exits 2 on any failure.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The model never authorises action; it only chooses among typed tools.
  • Telemetry is untrusted data. A filename cannot change policy.
  • No arbitrary shell is exposed through MCP.
  • Mutating tools are dry-run in MCP; execution is a separate human gate.
  • Autonomous critical action should be enabled only with allow_critical after an estate-specific drill.

docs.title: Assurance
docs.text: Autonomy raises the burden of proof. These artifacts are the minimum a security-conscious buyer should ask for, and the minimum Plasma should produce on every release.

docs.title: SBOM
docs.text:
plasma assurance sbom --out sbom.json

CycloneDX 1.5. Includes Plasma (MIT), the bundled WHIDS payload (AGPL-3.0), pydantic, pydantic-core, the optional pywinrm dependency and the frozen neuralOS engine/model entry. Use it for vendor-risk review and dependency tracking.

docs.title: Safety case
docs.text:
plasma assurance safety-case --out safety-case.md

States the claim, the controls, the eval result and the known limits:

  • typed tools with scopes and risk tiers;
  • dry-run-only mutating tools in MCP;
  • high/critical approval;
  • blast-radius and rate limits;
  • hash-chained provenance;
  • kill switch;
  • no arbitrary shell;
  • eval suite passing.

docs.title: Support bundle
docs.text:
plasma assurance support-bundle --out support.zip

A redacted diagnostic archive: config, policy, kill switch, tenants, rings, ledger tail, ledger verification, health, coverage and system facts. It excludes passwords, API tokens and event content beyond the ledger tail.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text:
plasma eval run

Safety scenarios, not detection tests. Exit 2 on any failure. Run it in CI and before raising an estate's autonomy tier.

docs.title: Third-party notices
docs.text:
plasma assurance notices

Plasma is MIT. The bundled WHIDS payload is AGPL-3.0. If you modify and distribute WHIDS, comply with the AGPL; get counsel before OEM packaging.

docs.title: What to ask from the vendor
docs.text:
• SBOM for the release you are running.
  • Pen-test report or a current assessment.
  • Safety case and eval results.
  • DPA, SLA, support model and escalation path.
  • Cyber-liability insurance.
  • A documented rollback and incident drill.
  • Proof that data stays on the estate.

docs.title: Atomic Red Team smoke test
docs.text:
This is the release-validation subset for the detection content that the Atomic Red Team estate run exercises. It is deliberately small: six high-value Windows techniques, one expected Plasma rule each.

The machine-readable suite is sensors/atomic-smoke.json. The unit test tests/test_atomic_fixes.py verifies that every expected rule still exists.

docs.text: Technique Atomic test Expected rule T1059.001 PowerShell Command Execution (a538de64-1c74-46ed-aa60-b995ed302598) Plasma Encoded Cmd T1053.005 Scheduled task Local (42f53695-ad4a-4546-abb6-7d837f644a71) Plasma Scheduled Task Create T1543.003 Service Installation CMD (981e2942-e433-44e9-afc1-8c957a1496b6) Plasma Service Registry Persistence T1547.001 Reg Key Run (e55be3fd-3521-4610-9d1a-e210e42dcf05) Plasma Run Key Persistence T1136.001 Create a new user in a command prompt (6657864e-0323-4206-9344-ac9cd7265a4f) Plasma Net Account Add T1140 Certutil Rename and Decode (71abc534-3c05-4d0c-80f7-cbe93cb2aa94) Plasma File Delete by LOLBin

docs.title: Run it on a lab endpoint
docs.text:
1. Install Atomic Red Team and the Invoke-AtomicRedTeam module on the endpoint.
  2. Point PathToAtomicsFolder at a local clone.
  3. For each case run the test, let WHIDS flush, then pull and query:
Invoke-AtomicTest T1059.001 -TestGuids a538de64-1c74-46ed-aa60-b995ed302598 `
  -PathToAtomicsFolder C:\AtomicRedTeam\atomic-red-team-master\atomics `

plasma whids pull
plasma query --kind alert --since 10m --max-rows 2000

  2. Run the cleanup command for every test:
Invoke-AtomicTest T1059.001 -TestGuids a538de64-1c74-46ed-aa60-b995ed302598 `

  -Confirm:$false

docs.title: Acceptance
docs.text:
• All six expected rules fire on their matching test.
  • No destructive atomics are used in this smoke suite.
  • Test tasks, services, local users and Run-key values are removed afterwards.
  • plasma health returns ok.

The wider 24-technique estate run and its gaps are recorded in the release notes. Discovery-only atomics are intentionally not part of this smoke suite.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: The canonical history lives in CHANGELOG.md. Highlights by release:

docs.title: 1.29.1 — 2026-11-24
docs.text:
• Remote ledger integrity. estate sync verifies the SHA-256 of every ledger returned by a host before accepting it; a corrupted reply is recorded as a host failure instead of being merged.
  • Atomic findings. findings.json is replaced atomically, like estate.json and per-host ledgers.
  • 1051 tests collected; full suite, ruff and bandit (0 medium/high) pass.

docs.title: 1.29.0 — 2026-11-24
docs.text:
• Estate edge ledger. plasma estate build reduces a bounded window to a small hash-sealed count ledger: users, first/last seen, bounded sources, logon types, user>process pairs and hashes. No command lines, file paths or event rows leave the host.
  • Merge and correlate. estate merge keeps the newest ledger per host and signs the estate view; estate findings raises user fan-out (9 with a shared source, 7 for a same-name pattern), source fan-out, shared file hashes, stale hosts and new host edges against a baseline.
  • Continuous sync. estate sync pulls one ledger per host in parallel over WinRM or files, saves hosts/<name>.json, estate.json and findings.json, records per-host failures without aborting, and supports --loop --interval.
  • Bounded and verified. 200 users, 10 sources per user, 200 process pairs and 256 KiB per host ledger; 5,000 identities on the desk. SHA-256 integrity is verified on load, merge and status.
  • Scale tested. A 1,000-host, 10,000-identity merge and correlation completes in seconds and stays under the estate byte bound.
  • 1051 tests collected; full suite, ruff and bandit (0 medium/high) pass.

docs.title: 1.28.1 — 2026-11-22
docs.text:
• Responder args from a file. plasma plugin act --args-file reads the JSON argument object from disk, avoiding Windows native-argument quoting when the action takes paths.
  • 1036 tests collected; full suite, ruff and bandit (0 medium/high) pass.

docs.title: 1.28.0 — 2026-11-22
docs.text:
• Plugin ABI. Four plugin kinds — sensor, detector, responder, exporter — as bounded external processes with a signed manifest, NDJSON contract, per-record validation, quarantine and dedupe. Plugins never write the store directly.
  • Sensor and detector host. plasma plugin run streams events or findings with a hard timeout, line cap, event cap and stderr log; ten invalid records stop the run.
  • Responder actions. plugin act previews exact argv and returns a plan id; apply requires that id and a reason, checks the kill switch and the plugin's enabled state, verifies, journals and supports undo. Paths are checked against declared roots.
  • Ingest and export. JSONL, Windows Event Log and HMAC webhook ingest; batched webhook and syslog export with bounded spooling on failure.
  • Signing and scaffolding. Ed25519 keygen/sign/verify, pinned trust keys, and plugin new for all three plugin kinds.
  • Docs and schemas. docs/plugin-api.md plus manifest and envelope JSON schemas.
  • 1035 tests collected; full suite, ruff and bandit (0 medium/high) pass.

docs.title: 1.27.7 — 2026-11-22
docs.text:

docs.text:

docs.title: 1.23.0 — 2026-11-20
docs.text:

docs.title: 1.22.0 — 2026-11-20

  • JIT noise control. Managed .NET shellcode false positives are suppressed from the alert stream and reported as a count.
  • Bundled and bounded. 64-bit and 32-bit scanners are fetched into the Windows payload; targeted PID/name scans are the default, --all is explicit.

docs.title: 1.20.0 — 2026-11-19
docs.text:

docs.title: 1.19.3 — 2026-11-18
docs.text:
MSI upgrades now converge the running node.

  • install --rotate. The MSI custom action passes --rotate, so after staging the new version the installer swaps bin\plasma.exe and restarts the registered tasks. Previously the package copied a versioned sibling and updated config.json, but the running node kept executing the old canonical binary — an MSI upgrade from 1.19.1 to 1.19.2 left /healthz reporting 1.19.1.
  • Rotation is all-or-nothing. A failed canonical swap returns exit 4 with the rotation detail instead of reporting a successful install.
  • Verified on WS2: silent MSI install exits 0, bin\plasma.exe --version and /healthz both report 1.19.3.

docs.title: 1.19.2 — 2026-11-18
docs.text:
Enterprise MSI packaging.

  • The MSI is Authenticode-signed in the release workflow, using the same PFX and timestamp as the exe; SHA256SUMS covers the signed MSI.
  • The MSI is built with -arch x64, so it installs under C:\Program Files\Plasma instead of Program Files (x86).

docs.title: 1.19.1 — 2026-11-18
docs.text:
Holistic security and correctness review.

  • Response/prevention: kill switch covers undo and prevention, approval queue re-checks policy and is atomic, protected paths/processes/tasks are hardened, plans are identity- and time-bound, capture failure gates automatic kills, prevention rollback is plan-gated and verified.
  • Collection/data: tap/observatory/drift redaction, identity failure reporting, malformed WHIDS/watch rows skipped, content-aware dedupe, trace validation/MSI hardening, deep persistence parsing, BOM-safe store, canary/fleet/health/Sigma/notify/FIM fixes.
  • Install/update: dry-run is read-only, operator config is preserved, Sysmon and updates require valid signatures, ring/hold/promote logic fixed, rotation/rollback/locking hardened, prerelease ordering fixed.
  • Agent trust: policy type validation, fail-closed tenants, ledger truncation checkpoint, terminal denials and single-use approvals.
  • 785 tests collected; full suite and -W error pass; ruff check clean.

docs.title: 1.19.0 — 2026-11-18
docs.text:
Agent-oriented help for every command.

docs.title: 1.18.6 — 2026-11-18
docs.text:
Manual administrator updates can clear SYSTEM-owned stale processes.

  • Escalate the cleanup to SYSTEM when needed. A remote Administrator token often cannot terminate SYSTEM-owned serve processes (Access is denied), which left the old API image on port 9999 after a manual update auto. If any plasma process survives the direct kill and the updater is not already SYSTEM, it registers a one-shot SYSTEM task to finish the cleanup, waits, and removes the task. The normal PlasmaUpdate path is already SYSTEM and skips the escalation.
  • 743 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff error-level checks clean.

docs.title: 1.18.5 — 2026-11-18
docs.text:
Serve-process cleanup that works on hardened hosts.

  • Identify lingering plasma processes by image name. WS1 hides CommandLine and ExecutablePath from WMI, so the command-line match used in 1.18.4 found nothing and the old serve process kept port 9999. The updater now walks its own ancestor chain and stops every other plasma* process before rotation. All of them are restarted by _start_tasks (or by their normal schedule), and the update process cannot kill itself.
  • 742 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff error-level checks clean.

docs.title: 1.18.4 — 2026-11-18
docs.text:
Ring selection and serve restart fixes found on the live estate.

  • An explicit host ring now wins. A host assigned to canary was still compared against the configured default (broad) and skipped by the PlasmaUpdate task. update auto now derives the ring from the host's assignment, falling back to config.json only when the host is unassigned.
  • Restarting PlasmaServe actually restarts the API. PyInstaller's one-file bootloader re-execs itself as a child; schtasks /end killed the parent but left the child holding port 9999, so /healthz kept reporting the old version. The updater now stops lingering serve processes before rotation so the restarted task binds and serves the new binary.
  • 742 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff error-level checks clean.

docs.title: 1.18.3 — 2026-11-18
docs.text:
Manual update apply shares the hardened rotation path.

  • update apply now quiesces and restarts the scheduled tasks with the same rotate_running helper as update auto, so the manual path cannot hit the in-use-image failure that prompted 1.18.2.
  • 738 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff error-level checks clean.

docs.title: 1.18.2 — 2026-11-18
docs.text:
Self-update rotation reliability on Windows.

  • The tasks holding the binary are quiesced around the swap. PlasmaServe, PlasmaWatch, PlasmaWhidsWatchdog and PlasmaIdentityPull stop before rotation and restart afterwards; a serve-launched update skips PlasmaServe so it cannot kill itself.
  • Retries and stale-backup recovery. A locked image is retried five times, a stale .old backup is preserved under a unique name, a read-only attribute is cleared first, and a failed swap restores the previous binary. PlasmaServe restarts after the update, so /healthz reports the new version.
  • 737 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff error-level checks clean.

docs.title: 1.18.1 — 2026-11-18
docs.text:
Self-update install robustness.

  • A locked staged exe no longer aborts the install. The installer skips the sys.executable copy when the bytes already match and tolerates a locked destination; the updater's rotation is authoritative.
  • 731 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff clean.

docs.title: 1.18.0 — 2026-11-18
docs.text:
Measured self-update.

  • plasma update auto checks the latest release and applies it through the existing SHA256 + Authenticode + install + rotate path. Signed releases only.
  • PlasmaUpdate daily SYSTEM task with a random minute inside the 02:00–05:00 maintenance window. --no-autoupdate disables it.
  • Ring-aware: broad waits 24 hours; canary updates immediately; rollback never auto-updates.
  • Kill-switch aware; one update at a time; previous binary kept.
  • Canonical plasma.exe rotated and PlasmaServe restarted after a successful update.

  • 731 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff clean.

docs.title: 1.17.1 — 2026-11-17
docs.text:
Critical process-guard fix.

  • Protected process names were not matched. _g_process wrapped the Get-CimInstance assignment in parentheses, so PowerShell emitted the whole CIM object as a formatted table. The guard compared table text to PROTECTED_PROCESSES, and kill_process on LSASS, CSRSS, SERVICES, WINLOGON, WHIDS or Sysmon minted a dry-run plan instead of refusing. The assignment is now bare and the guard refuses as designed.
  • 716 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff clean.

docs.title: 1.17.0 — 2026-11-17
docs.text:
Measured protection is armed by default.

  • Automatic containment is on, but narrow. Default policy: enabled: true, mode: "enforce", min_score: 9, allowed_actions: ["snapshot", "kill_process"], 2 actions per run, 30-minute cooldown. Snapshot is written before the kill.
  • Everything else stays human-approved. Isolation, quarantine, disabling users, removing admins, stopping services, credential rotation, task/Run-key/WMI removal and IP blocking require approval.
  • PlasmaWatch drives the sweep. A SYSTEM task runs watch once --enforce every 5 minutes. --no-autoprotect installs the old dry-run posture and removes the task.
  • Protected components stay protected in code. WinRM, RDP, WHIDS, Sysmon, LSASS, BFE, MpsSvc, Administrator, SYSTEM and service accounts are refused. Isolation keeps RDP/WinRM open.
  • Upgrades migrate the old default; custom blocks are preserved.
  • New plasma protect commands: status, arm, disarm, protected.
  • 715 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff clean.

docs.title: 1.16.3 — 2026-11-17
docs.text:
Command-tree type metadata.

  • Options and positionals carry their argparse type. /v1/commands now reports type (int, str, or null) for every option and positional. The OpenAPI Option and Positional schemas require the field.
  • 698 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff clean.

docs.title: 1.16.2 — 2026-11-17
docs.text:
Serve hardening, command-tree completeness and explicit lifecycles.

  • Serve concurrency and edge cases. Argparse validation is serialized; API keys are compared as bytes; a missing Content-Length returns 411; the handler has a socket timeout; broken pipes are ignored; child processes get UTF-8 I/O, stdin=DEVNULL, and a process-tree kill on timeout.
  • Audit reliability and redaction. Audit appends are serialized and use a 30 s lock timeout; failed writes are logged. --prompt values and credential-shaped argv items are redacted.
  • Command tree completeness. /v1/commands returns a separate root and 127 commands, each with positionals as well as options. The OpenAPI schemas describe both.
  • Explicit lifecycles. plasma/lifecycle.py names the serve request, plan, approval, enforcement, prevention, WHIDS, FIM, canary, drift, identity-schedule, capture, fleet, kill-switch, tenant and ring machines, with pure classifiers used by the modules.
  • 698 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff clean.

docs.title: 1.16.1 — 2026-11-17
docs.text:
OpenAPI 3.1 for plasma serve.

  • GET /openapi.json publishes an OpenAPI 3.1 document covering the four API routes, both auth schemes, the request/response envelopes and the error responses. No auth required.
  • GET /docs serves a self-contained HTML reference that renders the spec; no CDN, no external dependency.
  • plasma/openapi.py is the single source of truth; info.version tracks the package version, and a unit test asserts the spec paths and the server routes do not drift apart.
  • 674 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff clean.

docs.title: 1.16.0 — 2026-11-17
docs.text:
plasma serve: the full CLI over an authenticated HTTP API.

  • One endpoint, the whole CLI. POST /v1/exec takes an argv list and runs it through the real parser, so every command, flag and default is available exactly as it is on the command line. GET /v1/commands returns the full command tree with options, mutating flags and long-running markers.
  • API-key auth. Bearer token or X-API-Key; the default is plasmaplasma for lab use, and --api-key-file or PLASMA_SERVE_API_KEY overrides it.
  • Read-only mode. --read-only refuses every command that changes host or Plasma state, including any --apply.
  • Bounded execution. Each call runs in a child process with a hard timeout, a 1 MiB request cap and an 8 MiB output cap.
  • Audit. Every call is appended to <root>/serve/audit.jsonl.
  • TLS. --tls-cert and --tls-key wrap the listener in HTTPS.
  • 667 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff clean.

docs.title: 1.15.9 — 2026-11-17
docs.text:
Canary collector performance.

  • observe canary filters server-side. The collector pulled every 4624/4625 for seven days and timed out at 240 s on a busy DC. It now uses a FilterXPath on TargetUserName, so only canary logons cross the wire.
  • 639 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff clean.

docs.title: 1.15.8 — 2026-11-17
docs.text:

  • Fleet pull ships in the frozen exe. pywinrm is now a build dependency and is collected by PyInstaller, so plasma fleet scan works from the single-file binary, not only from a Python desk install.

  • 638 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff clean.

docs.title: 1.15.7 — 2026-11-17
docs.text:
Run-key allowlist fix from the deep drill.

  • remove_run_key accepts the canonical registry spelling. The allowlist regex was case-sensitive and expected SOFTWARE; the real key is Software, so every HKCU:\Software\...\Run target was refused. The regex is now case-insensitive.
  • 637 tests collected; full suite passes; ruff clean.

docs.title: 1.15.6 — 2026-11-17

Final WHIDS storm field.

docs.title: 1.15.5 — 2026-11-17

docs.title: 1.15.0 — 2026-11-15
docs.text:
Holistic security and state-machine review.

  • Failed actions are no longer reported as applied. actuate now checks the payload exit code, journals mode: failed with a failure reason, and still allows undo of a partially applied action. Playbook undo marks the whole reversal failed instead of claiming success.
  • Locks cover the whole operation. A shared agentstate.lock uses a PID token and a 300 s stale window; the old 30 s window let a second process steal the actuate journal lock during a 60 s apply. State machines, ledger, prevention, enforcement, rings, killswitch and policy writes use it.
  • Kill switch fails closed. A corrupt killswitch.json now reports the switch engaged instead of silently disabling containment.
  • MCP is least-privilege by default. A harness that does not declare PLASMA_SCOPES gets read-only scopes, not *. Policy evaluation with no scopes denies instead of inheriting a wildcard.
  • Update pinning works. download_and_verify honours the requested tag (it silently installed latest before), matches the SHA256SUMS line to the actual exe asset, and update apply --tag exposes it.
  • Path and quoting hardening. Manifest verification rejects .. paths; the WHIDS watchdog task escapes single quotes; DTrace validation catches whitespace-separated system (; AppLocker allow paths reject control characters; WMI capture and removal use the same bounded set.
  • Enforcement approvals are single-use and policy-checked. Pending requests are deduplicated, consumed on approval, and re-checked against the current allowlist.

Killing the injecting process destroys the in-memory artifact the detection exists to surface; the journal records capture: applied|failed|skipped. docs.title: 1.12.0 — 2026-11-15
docs.text:
Prevention, in two honest tiers.

  • Tier 0 — plasma enforce: watch findings become policy-gated, reversible containment. Injection findings and chain detections kill the accessing process; a tripped canary queues host isolation for approval. Off by default and dry-run unless enabled + mode: enforce are set. Score floor, per-run cap, cooldown, action allowlist, approval queue, kill switch and a decision journal. watch once --enforce wires it to a sweep.
  • Tier 1 — plasma prevent: AppLocker (audit by default), firewall egress default-deny with a mandatory allowlist, Defender ASR rules and LSA protection. Every control is dry-run first, plan-gated, verified, journaled and rollbackable by id.
  • Still no kernel driver. Inline blocking at the file/process/network boundary is delegated to Microsoft's signed enforcement points; Plasma owns the policy, evidence and rollback. This is a deliberate limit, documented in docs/prevention.md.
  • Findings now carry structured entities (pid, user, path, technique) so enforcement acts on data instead of re-parsing text.

Consistency and claim corrections.

  • injection_apc_chain (score 9, 30 s) escalates a cross-process RWX flip followed by an APC from the same image. inject-apc is documented as high-volume and is not chained on its own.

docs.title: 1.9.4 — 2026-11-14
docs.text:
Injection evidence precision, with positive controls on both hosts.

  • inject-rwx matches RWX with modifier bits (arg3 & 0xff == 0x40) and records whether the caller targeted itself or another process. Self-RWX scores 5 (JIT warm-up); cross-process RWX scores 8.
  • injection_chain requires a cross-process RWX row ("self": 0), so a process warming up its own JIT pages can never satisfy the first step.
  • inject-remote-thread compares only the low 32 bits of the target handle, avoiding an untyped 64-bit literal; inject-apc covers the NtQueueApcThread family, including NtQueueApcThreadEx2.
  • Positive controls on WS1 and WS2: local RWX produced self=1 score 5; VirtualProtectEx on a scratch notepad produced self=0 score 8; CreateRemoteThread produced a remote-thread row; QueueUserAPC produced an NtQueueApcThreadEx2 row. All three scripts compile and pass trace selftest on both hosts.

docs.title: Help and discovery
docs.text:
Every command has a detailed help page with a description, working examples, notes, a safety classification and related commands. This is the surface an orchestrating agent should use instead of guessing flags.

plasma --help                      # root overview + agent workflow
plasma help                        # command map, grouped
plasma help control approvals approve
plasma prevent asr --help          # argparse syntax + examples
plasma help --json                 # complete machine-readable catalog
plasma help actuate apply --json   # one command as JSON

plasma help --json returns schema plasma.help/1: every command path, summary, full description, usage, arguments (required, default, choices), examples, safety class, output and related commands. The same help metadata is included in GET /v1/commands on the HTTP API; an agent can also run POST /v1/exec {"argv": ["help", "--json"]}.

docs.title: help
docs.text:
plasma help [topic ...] [--json]

With no topic, prints the grouped command map and the dry-run → plan → apply workflow. With a topic, prints the same detailed page as plasma <topic> --help. --json returns the catalog, or one command when a topic is supplied. An unknown topic exits 1 with a structured error.

docs.title: install
docs.text:
plasma install [--dry-run] [--force] [--root PATH] [--skip-whids]
              [--skip-sysmon-check] [--require-whids] [--rotate]

Intelligent installer: verifies the payload manifest, decides FULL/MINIMAL, installs Sysmon when possible, provisions WHIDS, writes config.json, flips the current junction, and reports the decision. --require-whids makes a degraded decision fail with exit 3. --rotate (used by the MSI) swaps bin\plasma.exe and restarts the registered tasks after staging, so the running node matches the package; a failed rotation exits 4.

The installer registers PlasmaWatch and PlasmaWhidsWatchdog with both an AtStartup trigger and StartWhenAvailable; PlasmaCanaryShield gets the same pair when armed. A reboot or a missed timer run is picked up immediately. PlasmaUpdate deliberately stays on its daily maintenance window. health reports any present Plasma task that lacks an AtStartup trigger.

docs.title: health / status / probe / ask
docs.text:
plasma health [--root PATH]
plasma status [--events FILE]
plasma probe --tool NAME --events FILE
plasma ask --prompt "..." --events FILE

health = checks + verdict, including whether present Plasma tasks carry an AtStartup trigger. status = bundle identity + probe menu. probe/ask = run one named probe, or let the on-device model choose one. Refusals are structured, never guesses.

docs.title: identity
docs.text:
plasma identity pull --events FILE [--host NAME] [--since MINUTES]
                     [--ids LIST] [--max-events N]

Reads the Security channel through the Event Log API, UTC-normalized, deduped and bounded (--max-events, default 2000).

Event Kind What it gives you 4624 / 4625 auth logon success / failure, type, source, workstation 4768 / 4769 / 4770 / 4771 auth Kerberos TGT, service ticket, renewal, pre-auth failure (KDC only — zero on a member server, reported as zero) 4776 auth NTLM credential validation 4688 process process creation with creator subject, parent image and command line (when audit policy records it)

--ids takes a comma list from that set and is allowlisted: anything else is rejected before PowerShell is invoked.

docs.title: whids
docs.text:
plasma whids pull    --root DIR --out FILE
plasma whids push    --events FILE [--min-confidence N] [--max-indicators N] [--apply] [--reason TEXT]
plasma whids status  --root DIR --events FILE
plasma whids diagnose [--root DIR]
plasma whids ensure  [--root DIR] [--wait SECONDS]

push is dry-run by default; --apply replaces plasma-iocs.gen atomically. Default confidence is 8 on the gene 0–10 scale.

ensure is the watchdog body: Running is a no-op; a hung StartPending is force-stopped and restarted; a stopped service is started. Actions are appended to logs/whids-watchdog.log. The installer registers PlasmaWhidsWatchdog (SYSTEM, every 2 minutes) to run it.
