docs.title: canary
docs.text:
plasma canary deploy [--dir PATH] [--randomize|--no-randomize] [--subdir NAME]
plasma canary verify
plasma canary status
plasma canary token create --kind dns --domain SUFFIX [--out PATH]
plasma canary token create --kind http --base-url URL [--out PATH] [--name NAME]
plasma canary token list
plasma canary token remove ID [--delete-artifact]
plasma canary serve [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port 8088] [--max-requests N]
plasma canary collect [--since MINUTES] [--max-events N]
plasma canary hits [--last N]
plasma canary sysmon [--domain SUFFIX...] [--apply]
plasma canary registry deploy [--hive HKCU|HKLM] [--count N]
plasma canary registry list
plasma canary registry remove ID
plasma canary shield status
plasma canary shield install [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]
plasma canary shield uninstall [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]
plasma canary shield sweep [--since-minutes N] [--apply --reason TEXT] [--max-kills N]
plasma canary pipe deploy [--count N]
plasma canary pipe list
plasma canary pipe remove ID
plasma canary pipe serve [--apply --reason TEXT] [--max-kills N] [--max-connections N]
plasma canary pipe install [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]
plasma canary pipe uninstall [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]
plasma canary pipe status

File canaries are realistic decoys with randomized subdirectories and names by default; the body never identifies itself. verify reports missing or modified files at score 10. DNS tokens are unique hostnames matched from Sysmon EID 22; canary sysmon --apply writes a narrow DnsQuery include and hot-reloads it. HTTP tokens are .url shortcuts served by the local collector; hits are written to <root>/canary-hits.jsonl. watch (or canary collect) turns DNS/HTTP hits into source="canary" event-store alerts, deduplicated across sweeps.

Registry canaries are decoy keys under Software\PlasmaDecoy in HKCU or HKLM. canary shield install adds only the recorded canary basenames and registry fragments to a narrow Sysmon FileCreate/FileDelete/ RegistryEvent include, then registers a one-minute SYSTEM task. The sweep verifies the live PID/image, refuses protected/trusted processes, kills a process that creates/deletes/registry-writes a canary, and journals the decision. Reads do not trigger; a pure in-place overwrite is detected by canary verify as a hash change without process attribution.

Named-pipe canaries are decoy pipes. canary pipe install registers a SYSTEM listener at boot; a client that connects is identified by PID and killed after the same protected/trusted checks. Enumeration alone is not a connection and is not killed. Decisions are written to <root>/canary-pipe-journal.jsonl; canary pipe status reports live connection and kill counters while the task runs. The listener is user-mode, not a driver.

docs.title: intercept
docs.text:
plasma intercept status
plasma intercept rules list
plasma intercept rules add --file FILE
plasma intercept rules remove RULE_ID
plasma intercept evaluate [--events FILE] [--max-rows N] [--out FILE]
plasma intercept apply RULE_ID [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]
plasma intercept protect-canary [--prefix PATH] [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]
plasma intercept rollback --id ID [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]

Deterministic policy at native gates. evaluate is the shadow phase: it reports would_block without changing the host. protect-canary adds an NTFS deny/audit ACL to the canary manifest. apply brokers acl and firewall rules. The MCP tool-call gateway evaluates agent_tool_call rules before policy and handlers. Every apply is dry-run first, plan-gated, payload-bound, journaled and reversible.

acl rollback restores the prior SDDL; firewall rollback removes the named rule. AppLocker and ASR remain under plasma prevent.

docs.title: memory
docs.text:
plasma memory scan --pid PID...
plasma memory scan --pname NAME...
plasma memory scan --all [--timeout SECONDS]
plasma memory scan ... [--deep] [--dump] [--scanner 64|32]
plasma memory triage [--since-minutes N] [--min-score S] [--max-targets N] [--no-deep]
plasma memory status
plasma memory list

Bounded, on-demand HollowsHunter/PE-sieve scan for hollowed or replaced PEs, reflective DLLs, shellcode, code patches and IAT hooks. The scanner is SHA-256 pinned and refuses a mismatched binary. Findings become source="memory" alerts. --dump is explicit, local and refused with --all; no dumps are produced by default. Managed .NET JIT shellcode observations are suppressed from the alert stream. triage scans only PIDs selected by injection- or credential-shaped alerts in the recent window.

Exit 0 = clean, 2 = findings, 1 = input/tool error.

docs.text:
plasma query [--spec JSON|FILE] [FILTERS] [--since 1h] [--count-by FIELD] [--out FILE]
plasma tree [--pid PID | --process NAME] [--depth N] [--max-rows N]
plasma summarize [--since 1h] [--limit N] [--rare-max N]

plasma case open NAME [--host H] [--title TEXT] [--note TEXT]
plasma case list
plasma case add NAME [FILTERS] [--spec JSON|FILE]
plasma case note NAME TEXT
plasma case timeline NAME
plasma case report NAME [--out FILE]
plasma case seal NAME
plasma case verify NAME

plasma detect validate --rules FILE
plasma detect test [--cases FILE]
plasma detect diff --old FILE --new FILE
plasma detect replay --events FILE [--rules FILE] [--max-rows N]

Typed, bounded investigation over the local JSONL store. query refuses unknown fields; tree uses only explicit pid/ppid edges; summarize returns a capped digest. A case collects selected rows and notes, renders a report and seals every artifact with SHA-256. detect compiles rule regexes, compares rule sets and replays chains over a capture. See Investigation.

docs.title: estate
docs.text:
plasma estate build    --events FILE [--out FILE] [--window MIN] [--max-rows N] [--host NAME] [--role ROLE]
plasma estate merge    (--ledgers FILE... | --dir DIR) --out FILE [--max-age MIN]

docs.title: actuate / playbook
docs.text:
plasma actuate apply <action> [--target T] --reason TEXT [--apply --plan ID]
plasma actuate undo  --id ID [--apply]
plasma actuate journal [--last N]
plasma actuate apply --list
plasma playbook list
plasma playbook apply <name> [--target T] --reason TEXT [--apply --plan ID]
plasma playbook undo  --id ID [--apply]

docs.title: enforce
docs.text:
plasma enforce run [--root DIR] [--apply | --dry-run]
plasma enforce status
plasma enforce pending
plasma enforce approve --id ID [--apply]

Tier 0 prevention: findings become allowlisted, reversible containment. Armed by default but narrow: snapshot + kill_process at score 9+, a 2-action per-run cap and a 30-minute cooldown; isolation and every other action require approval. The policy still gates each action. The installer registers PlasmaWatch, which runs plasma watch once --enforce at boot and every 5 minutes.

docs.title: protect
docs.text:
plasma protect status
plasma protect protected
plasma protect arm [--apply-prevention --reason TEXT]
plasma protect disarm [--reason TEXT]

Inspect or change the measured posture. arm writes the measured enforcement block; disarm sets enabled: false and mode: "dry-run". protected lists the services, processes, accounts and paths the response layer refuses to touch.

docs.title: prevent
docs.text:
plasma prevent status
plasma prevent posture
plasma prevent cfa [--mode off|audit|block] [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]
plasma prevent network [--mode off|audit|block] [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]
plasma prevent driver-blocklist [--off] [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]
plasma prevent applocker [--mode audit|enforce] [--allow-path P]... [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]
plasma prevent egress --allow IP[:PORT]... [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]
plasma prevent asr --ids GUID[,GUID] [--action Audit|Enabled|Disabled] [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]
plasma prevent lsa [--off] [--apply --plan ID --reason TEXT]
plasma prevent rollback --id ID [--apply]

Tier 1 prevention through Windows enforcement points. Every control is dry-run first, plan-gated, verified, journaled and undoable by id. AppLocker defaults to audit; egress requires an explicit allowlist; ASR needs Defender; LSA takes effect after a reboot. posture is read-only and reports WDAC, Controlled Folder Access, Network Protection, the vulnerable driver blocklist, ASR counts and tamper protection. cfa, network and driver-blocklist are opt-in, plan-gated and rollbackable; WDAC stays read-only.

docs.title: update
docs.text:
plasma update check [--repo OWNER/NAME] [--token-env VAR]
plasma update apply [--bin PATH] [--root PATH] [--allow-unsigned]
plasma update auto [--root PATH] [--ring canary|broad|rollback]
                   [--check-only] [--force] [--allow-unsigned] [--no-notify]

Anonymous against the public repo; signature-pinned. update auto is the measured self-update path: it respects the deployment ring, the 02:00–05:00 maintenance window, the 24-hour canary hold, the kill switch and one-at-a- time locking. The installer registers PlasmaUpdate to run it daily; --no-autoupdate disables it.

docs.text:
plasma control policy show|set
plasma control approvals list|approve|deny
plasma control audit tail|verify
plasma control killswitch status|on|off
plasma control tenants list|add|remove

policy set accepts --autonomy assist|supervised|autonomous, --deny, --allow, --max-actions, --max-hosts and --allow-critical. audit verify exits 2 if the hash chain is broken. Approvals are single-use and bound to the tool and argument hash.

docs.title: mcp
docs.text:
plasma mcp serve [--root PATH]

MCP over stdio. Twenty typed tools; mutating tools return a dry-run plan and approval reference, never an execution. See Agent-native operation.

docs.title: serve
docs.text:
plasma serve [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port 9999] [--api-key KEY]
             [--api-key-file FILE] [--root PATH] [--read-only]
             [--tls-cert FILE --tls-key FILE] [--timeout SECONDS]
             [--max-body BYTES] [--max-output BYTES] [--no-audit] [--quiet]

The full CLI over an authenticated HTTP API. POST /v1/exec takes an argv list and runs it through the real parser; GET /v1/commands returns the command tree. The default bind is loopback; a non-loopback bind refuses the known default key plasmaplasma unless --allow-insecure-default-key is set. Use --api-key-file or PLASMA_SERVE_API_KEY in production. --read-only refuses every mutating command. Every call is written to <root>/serve/audit.jsonl. See HTTP API.

docs.title: Compliance evidence
docs.text:
plasma evidence export turns the node's real state into an auditor-readable control matrix. It does not certify anything; it produces the evidence a human auditor can verify.

plasma evidence export --framework cbn ndpa pci iso27001 --out evidence.json

Outputs:

  • evidence.json — machine-readable controls, statuses and evidence.
  • evidence.md — the same matrix as Markdown.

docs.title: What is measured
docs.text: Input Evidence Event store rows, kinds, hosts, first/last UTC timestamp Coverage rollup / exact / weighted percentages and blind spots Policy autonomy tier, deny list, blast radius, rate limit Ledger hash-chain verification, rows, pending approvals Kill switch global and per-host state Tenants configured tenants and host assignment Response chains, canaries, plan-gated action tools

docs.title: Frameworks
docs.text:
• CBN — policy, asset visibility, monitoring, incident response, least privilege, third-party/agent governance, data residency, resilience.
  • NDPA — minimisation, safeguards, breach detection, accountability, local processing, retention.
  • PCI DSS v4.0 — audit logging, record contents, review, retention, time sync, change detection, incident response.
  • ISO 27001:2022 — logging, monitoring, incident management, assessment, configuration management, privileged access.

Each control is marked met, partial or gap. Gaps are shown, not hidden.

docs.title: Honest caveats
docs.text:
• Evidence is only as good as the deployed configuration and the ledger.
  • A control marked met means the mechanism exists and has evidence; it is not an audit opinion.
  • Some controls depend on organisational policy outside Plasma (training, supplier contracts, business continuity).
  • Coverage is the shipped-rule view: 94.6% rollup, 89.2% exact and 85.9% fidelity-weighted, with the two remaining blind spots named (T1056, T1056.001).
  • Have counsel map the output to the current CBN/NDPA/PCI/ISO requirements before submitting it to a regulator.

docs.title: The lake-less model
docs.text:
A traditional EDR/SIEM moves raw events to a central store, then queries there. Plasma inverts the direction: the box keeps its own diary, and the desk asks questions when there is a reason to.

        ┌──────────────────────────── one Windows host ───────────────────────────┐
        │  Sysmon ─┐                                                              │
        │  WHIDS  ─┼─► normalizers ─► data\events.jsonl   (one strict contract)   │
        │  identity┘                        │                                     │
        │  canary files/tokens ─────────────┤                                     │
        │  memory scan (on demand) ─────────┤                                     │
        │  ETW tap (on demand)              ▼                                     │
        │                       frozen neuralOS instance                          │
        │                       (menu of 10 probes, refuses unknowns)             │
        └───────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                        │  pull over WinRM / SSM
                                        ▼
        desk: status · ask · health · watch · drift · chains · coverage
              fleet pull/correlate/report · actuate (plan-gated)

Nothing streams to a server. There is no collector daemon of Plasma's own, no cloud dependency, and no standing network path except the management channel you already have (WinRM 5985 or SSM). Canary tokens follow the same rule: DNS queries are read from the local Sysmon channel, and HTTP tokens are served by a loopback-first local collector.

docs.title: The event contract
docs.text:
Every sensor output is rewritten into the same row shape before it reaches the store. One shape means every later layer — the brain, chains, fleet, drift — speaks one language.

{
  "ts": "2026-11-12T10:01:30.000Z",
  "host": "EC2AMAZ-8NK9FUP",
  "source": "plasma",
  "kind": "auth",
  "event_id": 4625,
  "severity": "medium",
  "score": 0.5,
  "action": "logged",
  "user": "CORP\\bob",
  "process": "svchost.exe",
  "pid": 812,
  "dest_ip": "203.0.113.9",
  "description": "logon FAILED type=3 from=203.0.113.9 workstation=WS12"
}

Rules the contract enforces:

  • ts is UTC. Collectors convert at the source (ToUniversalTime()); offset-less rows are treated as UTC on read. Mixed local/UTC timestamps would silently break cross-host correlation — this is tested.
  • Machine accounts ($) and empty users are dropped from identity rows.
  • Scores are 0–10 at the finding layer (severity maps to it); raw Plasma scores are 0–1 and multiplied by ten where a rule expects the WHIDS criticality scale.
  • Deduplication by content hash on append; repeated pulls are free.

docs.title: Sensors vs. probes
docs.text:
Terms used consistently in this documentation:

Term Meaning Sensor A collector that produces events (Sysmon, WHIDS, identity pull, ETW tap) Probe A read-only question over existing data (the 10-instance menu, coverage, chains, deep persistence) Finding A scored statement about risk, produced by a rule, chain, drift comparison, or fleet correlation Action A named, reversible mutation of the host (actuate) Playbook A named sequence of actions applied as one plan-gated unit Enforcement A policy that maps findings to allowlisted actions automatically (enforce) Prevention control A Windows enforcement point configured by Plasma: AppLocker, firewall egress, Defender ASR, LSA protection (prevent)

docs.title: Plugins are processes
docs.text:
A plugin is not imported into Plasma. It is an external process with a manifest, a bounded output stream and a declared kind — the same shape as the Sysmon and WHIDS integrations. That choice is deliberate:

  • a plugin crash, hang or memory bug cannot take down watch, serve or the CLI;
  • the core validates every record and owns the append, so a plugin cannot forge another source or corrupt the store;
  • a signed manifest and payload hash are checked before install;
  • limits (line size, event count, timeout) are enforced by the host, not trusted from the plugin.

The record contract is newline-delimited JSON with v, type and either an event or finding object. See Plugins for the manifest, envelope, lifecycle and security model.

docs.title: The on-device brain
docs.text:
Plasma embeds a frozen neuralOS instance: a 121M-parameter, ~35 MB, 2-bit-quantized tool-calling model plus a fixed menu of probes.

  • The model selects a probe and fills its arguments. It cannot invent a probe, run shell, or read raw logs directly — every answer comes back through the probe's typed schema.
  • If a request matches nothing on the menu, the refusal gate returns a refusal instead of guessing.
  • The model is never in the detection path and never in the response path.

This is deliberate: a tiny model that routes to validated tools is an auditable system; a large model that answers freely is not.

docs.title: Determinism and evidence
docs.text:
Plasma's promise is not "clever", it is explainable:

  • Detection = written rules with technique IDs and fixed scores.
  • Chains = written sequences with fixed gap windows.
  • Correlations = fixed score tables (lateral hop 9, shared hash 8, …).
  • Response = a named action, rendered as the exact payload before it runs.

Every finding can be traced to the rule or correlation that produced it, and every state change is in the journal.

docs.title: Control plane
docs.text:
The control plane is deliberately small: policy, approvals, provenance, kill switch, tenants, rings and rollback. It is CLI-first and JSON-out, so an agent or a human can drive it. There are no dashboards to maintain.

All commands accept --root; the default is C:\ProgramData\Plasma on Windows and ~/.plasma elsewhere.

docs.text:
plasma control policy show
plasma control policy set --autonomy assist|supervised|autonomous
plasma control policy set --deny kill_process --deny isolate_host
plasma control policy set --allow deploy_canary
plasma control policy set --max-actions 20 --max-hosts 1
plasma control policy set --allow-critical      # autonomous only

The policy is written to policy.json and checked before every tool call.

docs.text:
plasma control approvals list [--limit N]
plasma control approvals approve <id> [--approver NAME] [--note TEXT]
plasma control approvals deny <id> [--approver NAME] [--note TEXT]

plasma control audit verify

plasma control killswitch off [--host WS1]

docs.title: Tenants
docs.text:
plasma control tenants list
plasma control tenants add acme --name "Acme Bank" --host WS9 --host WS10
plasma control tenants remove acme

Tenants scope hosts and tag ledger rows for MSSP separation.

docs.title: Deployment rings
docs.text:
plasma ring status
plasma ring assign WS1 --ring canary
plasma ring promote canary

update apply --ring canary refuses a host that is not in that ring. Rings are local facts; an agent can read them but should not assign them.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
plasma rollback [--bin PATH]

Restores the previous canonical binary (<bin>.old) and keeps the failed one as <bin>.failed.

docs.title: Evidence and assurance
docs.text:
plasma evidence export --framework cbn ndpa pci iso27001 --out evidence.json
plasma assurance sbom --out sbom.json
plasma assurance safety-case --out safety-case.md
plasma assurance support-bundle --out support.zip
plasma assurance notices
plasma eval run
  • evidence export writes JSON and a Markdown control matrix.
  • assurance sbom writes a CycloneDX 1.5 document.
  • safety-case embeds the eval result and the known limits.
  • support-bundle contains policy, ledger tail, health, coverage and system facts; it contains no passwords or API tokens.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 success / clean 1 input or data error 2 refused, approval needed, or verification failed 3 execution failure

docs.title: Deployment at scale (MSI + GPO)
docs.text:
Plasma ships two artifacts per release:

Artifact Use plasma-<version>-windows-x64.exe single-file installer for a console operator plasma-<version>-windows-x64.msi MSI for GPO / enterprise deployment

The MSI installs the exe into C:\Program Files\Plasma\ and runs plasma install --force --root "<PLASMA_ROOT>" --rotate as a deferred, elevated custom action — so a GPO deployment provisions Sysmon/WHIDS and the event store without anyone at the console. --rotate swaps the canonical bin\plasma.exe and restarts the registered tasks, so an upgrade leaves the running node reporting the package version rather than the previous release.

docs.title: Silent install
docs.text:
msiexec /i plasma-1.4.0-windows-x64.msi /qn

Custom data root (e.g. a larger volume):

msiexec /i plasma-1.4.0-windows-x64.msi /qn PLASMA_ROOT="D:\Plasma"

Diagnostic log:

msiexec /i plasma-1.4.0-windows-x64.msi /qn /l*v C:\Windows\Temp\plasma-msi.log

Requirements: Windows x64, local administrator, ~200 MB disk. Internet is optional — with it, the installer provisions Sysmon automatically; without it the node installs in MINIMAL mode (identity + ETW tap).

docs.title: Group Policy deployment
docs.text:
1. Put the MSI on a share the computer accounts can read, e.g. \\fileserver\software\plasma\plasma-1.4.0-windows-x64.msi.
  2. Group Policy Management → create/edit a GPO for the target OU → Computer Configuration → Policies → Software Settings → Software installation.
  3. New → Package…, choose the MSI from the UNC path, select Assigned, click OK.
  4. To change the data root per OU, deploy a transform (.mst) that sets the public property PLASMA_ROOT, and add it in the package's Modifications tab.
  5. Force policy refresh and reboot: gpupdate /force, then gpresult /h to confirm the assignment.

The package upgrades in place: a newer release carries the same UpgradeCode and replaces the previous version (MajorUpgrade).

Uninstall behavior: removing the MSI deletes the installed exe only. It deliberately leaves Sysmon, WHIDS and C:\ProgramData\Plasma alone — silently stripping an EDR's sensors is an operational decision, not an uninstaller default. Remove those explicitly if required.

docs.title: Verifying a deployed node
docs.text:
plasma health
plasma canary deploy          # optional: realistic impact decoys
plasma canary token create --kind dns --domain assets.internal
plasma canary sysmon --apply  # narrow Sysmon EID 22 include
plasma canary token create --kind http --base-url http://collector:8088
plasma canary serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8088

A node deployed by MSI runs the same install path as the exe, so its config.json, health verdict and update behavior are identical.

docs.title: Rollout pattern that works
docs.text:
1. Pilot: one node, interactive install, plasma watch once for a day.
  2. Ring 1: MSI via GPO on a small OU; check plasma health centrally with plasma fleet pull/correlate.
  3. Ring 2: remaining OUs. Keep --skip-whids transforms for hosts where WHIDS is known to be unstable; the node records MINIMAL mode and health reports it, and the rest of the stack is unaffected. The installer also registers the PlasmaWhidsWatchdog scheduled task (SYSTEM, every 2 minutes), which runs plasma whids ensure to force-stop a hung StartPending and restart the sensor. Its actions are appended to C:\ProgramData\Plasma\logs\whids-watchdog.log.

docs.title: Note on signing
docs.text: The exe inside the MSI is Authenticode-signed from 1.2.0 onward. From 1.19.2 the release workflow also signs the MSI with the same PFX and timestamp, and SHA256SUMS covers the signed MSI. The current certificate is self-signed, so a fresh host reports UnknownError until the certificate is trusted; distribute the MSI over a trusted internal share and verify both signatures with Get-AuthenticodeSignature.

docs.title: Detection
docs.text:
Detection in Plasma is written rules and written sequences — nothing is learned in the detection path. Every statement carries a fixed score and an ATT&CK technique where one applies.

Detection feeds three consumers: watch (operator sweep), chain (story matching) and enforce (policy-gated containment). Only the last can change a host, and only when you have enabled it. See Prevention and blocking.

docs.title: Scores and verdicts
docs.text:
Score Meaning Typical source 10 act now canary tripped, health down 9 act now lateral hop, persistence-after-privilege, phish chain 8 act now shared hash, blind host, office-spawn, brute-force success 7 investigate shared domain/IP, unusual service paths 5–6 investigate drift changes, new alert growth, encoded command 0 clean nothing crossing a threshold

watch maps the top score to clean / investigate / act now and only delivers alerts when the score crosses min_score (default 7) in notify.json.

docs.title: Gene rules (always-on, WHIDS)
docs.text:
Twenty-five baseline rules with ATT&CK tags, criticality 6–9. See Sensors for the table. They run on every Sysmon event, cost almost nothing, and produce alert rows with a criticality that becomes the event score.

Adding a rule is a one-line JSON object in sensors/plasma-baseline.gen (schema 1.0.0) followed by a reinstall; regexes are validated by tests that compile every expression and assert positive/negative behavior.

docs.title: Tap rules (live windows)
docs.text: 31 rules for PowerShell script blocks, WMI persistence, DNS tunnels, .NET assembly loads and more. They only exist while plasma tap run is alive. Rules are rendered into the 7-field pipe format the C++ tap consumes, with fields validated against pipes and newlines.

docs.title: Detector plugins
docs.text:
A detector plugin runs over a bounded event tail and prints findings:

plasma plugin run acme-detector --since 1h --max-rows 5000

Findings become kind=alert rows with alert_id=plugin:<name>, a clamped score, the technique and bounded evidence. The runner enforces a timeout and the manifest's max_score. Declarative gene/Sigma packs are validated with the existing harness:

plasma detect validate --rules C:\plugins\acme\rules\pack.gen

Plugin findings enter the same store, so chains, query and the anomaly scorer see them without a second pipeline. They do not drive automatic containment.

docs.title: Identity — standing pulls
docs.text:
The shipped product registers a SYSTEM task (PlasmaIdentityPull) that runs the bounded Security-log pull every 15 minutes, so authentication and process-lineage events reach the store between operator sweeps: 4624/4625 logons, 4648 explicit credentials, 4720/4722/4724 account lifecycle, 4728/4732/4756 group membership, 4768/4769/4770/4771 Kerberos, 4776 NTLM and 4688 process creation with parent PID. Directory-service access (4662) and special privileges (4672) are supported but excluded from the default pull because they are high-volume; ask for them explicitly with --ids. Kerberos events exist only on a KDC, so a member server reports zero of them — that is data, not an error. Manage the task explicitly with:

plasma identity schedule --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma --every 15
plasma identity schedule-status
plasma identity unschedule

The task is registered by install/update and is independent of watch.

docs.title: DTrace — on-demand syscall evidence
docs.text: plasma trace run <script> --for 10s opens a bounded DTrace window (kernel syscalls, process creation, ETW) and normalizes matches into the same store (kind: "trace"). It is surgical evidence, not always-on coverage, so it is deliberately not counted in the ATT&CK breadth number. See DTrace.

docs.title: Chains — stories, not events
docs.text:
A single alert says "something happened". A chain says "this, then this, then this". Chains are ordered matchers over the events tail with a gap window between adjacent steps, plus optional count steps.

Chain Score Story (in time order) phish_spawn_chain 9 Office app → script host (powershell/wscript/cscript/mshta) → encoded command or egress, all within 15 min brute_force_success 8 ≥5 failed logons for one user, then a success, within 60 min persistence_after_privilege 9 account/group change → persistence-shaped command (schtasks, service, run key, WMI), within 60 min account_creation_privilege 9 a new account (4720) → privileged group membership (4728/4732/4756), within 30 min 
plasma chain score --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl
plasma chain score --events ... --window 1800 --max-rows 5000

Semantics worth knowing:

  • Matching is on timestamps, not file order; input order is irrelevant.
  • The matcher backtracks: a dead-end candidate does not hide a later match.
  • Each built-in chain carries its own gap_seconds; the --window flag is the default for chains that do not specify one.
  • Every match reports the span, the users involved and the matched rows.
  • Chains also run inside every watch sweep.

docs.title: Drift — what changed since I last looked
docs.text:
plasma drift record attest    # snapshot today's truth
plasma drift score  attest    # diff now vs baseline, 0-10
plasma drift list

attest compares the observatory's self-view (sensor states, blind spots, identity/privilege surface). Score 0 means "nothing changed"; every change is a finding with its own score. Drift refuses to baseline on a failed collection — a broken baseline is worse than none.

docs.title: Detection engineering — validate, diff, replay
docs.text:
plasma detect validate --rules sensors/plasma-baseline.gen
plasma detect test
plasma detect diff --old old.gen --new candidate.gen
plasma detect replay --events captured.jsonl

validate compiles every ~= regex, checks condition variables and names duplicates. test runs a built-in suite of positive and negative chain cases (phishing, brute force, Kerberos spray, privilege-to-persistence, account creation, injection) and exits 2 if any case breaks. diff compares rule sets by name and canonical hash, so an added, removed or silently changed rule is visible before promotion. replay runs the chain engine and a bounded summary over a captured store; the model is not involved. Promotion stays on the install/WHIDS path.

docs.title: Coverage — knowing your holes
docs.text:
plasma coverage

Diffs the shipped rules (tap + gene baseline + IOC feed + the 259-rule Sigma corpus) against a curated list of 37 core on-box ATT&CK techniques. It reports:

  • coverage_pct — 94.6% (35/37) with ATT&CK parent rollup (a parent counts when any sub-technique is covered);
  • coverage_exact_pct — 89.2% (33/37) counting only exact tags;
  • weighted_pct — 85.9%, discounting low/medium-fidelity rules (weights 1.0 / 0.7 / 0.4), halving purely keyword-only evidence, and counting only rules whose event IDs the shipped Sysmon config enables;
  • weighted_all_pct — the same number without the telemetry filter, for comparison;
  • telemetry_breakdown — techniques by live / partial / dormant / unknown, derived from each rule's Meta.EventIDs against the config;
  • dormant_techniques — techniques backed only by rules that cannot fire;
  • covered — technique → rules + per-rule fidelity + evidence + via_subtechnique;
  • keyword_only — the 4 techniques still backed solely by literal string matches; they count for breadth but not full weight. The label is derived from the rule shape (a rule whose only match key is substr), never hand-set, so it cannot drift from the rules themselves;
  • blind — the two honest gaps: T1056 / T1056.001 (input capture — needs kernel hooks). T1486 is covered by the canary capability (canary:verify), reported with its own provenance. A rule you cannot fire is inventory, not coverage: the telemetry axis makes that explicit;
  • extra_coverage — techniques watched outside the core list.

Breadth is deliberately reported alongside fidelity: a report cannot reach 100% by adding a weak rule, because the weighted number would fall, not rise.

This is the anti-marketing page: a product that cannot list its blind spots is not measuring anything.

docs.title: What the always-on plane now reads
docs.text:
Beyond process creation and registry events, the gene baseline consumes three Sysmon events that were previously ignored:

Event Rule Technique 10 ProcessAccess LSASS opened with credential-dump access rights T1003.001 6 DriverLoad unsigned driver loaded from a user-writable path T1014 17/18 PipeCreated named pipe shaped like PsExec/Cobalt/Beacon T1021, T1090

Sigma rules can be converted mechanically into the same gene format; see Sigma conversion. Critical-file integrity is covered by FIM.

docs.title: Canaries — impact and access tripwires
docs.text:
plasma canary deploy [--dir D:\Finance]   # realistic decoys + hash manifest
plasma canary verify                        # exit 2 when a canary is touched
plasma canary status
plasma canary token create --kind dns --domain assets.internal
plasma canary sysmon --apply                # narrow Sysmon EID 22 include
plasma canary token create --kind http --base-url http://collector:8088
plasma canary serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8088
plasma canary collect
plasma canary hits

File canaries are valid xlsx/csv/docx/pdf documents with random subdirectories and names. The body never says "canary"; the manifest is the only marker. watch verifies them on every sweep: a missing or modified canary is a score-10 finding (canary_tripped) — the honest detector for destructive impact that does not depend on guessing at encryption bursts. Deploy them to user-data shares as well as the default Documents folder.

DNS tokens are unique hostnames. Give the suffix a matching internal DNS record (usually a wildcard/sinkhole) so the query reaches a resolver. A query is observed through a narrow Sysmon EID 22 include (only the configured token suffixes) or any normalized event carrying dns_query; watch emits canary_dns_tripped at score 8. HTTP tokens are Windows .url shortcuts pointing at plasma canary serve; the hit is recorded locally and becomes canary_http_tripped at score 8. No Docker, cloud service or external callback is involved.

Registry canaries are decoy keys under Software\PlasmaDecoy. The active shield (plasma canary shield install) adds only the recorded file basenames and registry fragments to a narrow Sysmon FileCreate/FileDelete/RegistryEvent include and runs a one-minute SYSTEM sweep. It verifies the live PID and image, refuses protected/trusted processes, then kills a process that creates, deletes or registry-writes a canary. Reads do not trigger; an in-place overwrite is still caught by canary verify as a hash change, without process attribution.

Configured canary accounts are queried on every watch sweep: config.json:

{"canary": {"accounts": ["svc-print-archive"]}}

A 4624/4625/4771/4776 for that account becomes canary_account_tripped at score 10. A canary hit is evidence, not an automatic kill: the response policy still requires approval for host isolation.

docs.title: Memory scanning
docs.text:
plasma memory scan --pid 4832
plasma memory scan --pname powershell.exe,rundll32.exe --deep

HollowsHunter/PE-sieve looks inside running processes for hollowing, implanted PEs, shellcode, code patches and IAT hooks. It is on-demand and bounded; the scanner is hash-pinned. Findings are source="memory" alerts with T1055/T1055.012/T1620 as appropriate. No dumps by default.

docs.title: IOC push
docs.text:
plasma whids pull --events store.jsonl                  # alerts → store
plasma whids push --events store.jsonl --min-confidence 8
plasma whids push --events store.jsonl --min-confidence 8 --apply --reason "..."

push extracts high-confidence indicators (SHA-256 file hashes, public destinations, DNS queries, excluding private and benign domains) and regenerates plasma-iocs.gen. Dry-run first; --apply replaces the live rule file atomically. The default threshold matches the gene 0–10 scale.

docs.title: Event-level scoring
docs.text: Raw Plasma rows carry 0–1 scores; _row_score maps them to the 0–10 criticality WHIDS expects (score * 10, severity fallback). At the finding layer everything is 0–10. The scale conversion is unit-tested — a mismatch here once caused a default push to extract zero indicators.

docs.title: Enterprise deployment in an Active Directory domain
docs.text:
This guide is for a Windows estate joined to an Active Directory domain: servers, domain controllers, and managed workstations. It covers design, prerequisites, installation, configuration, domain rollout, canary-shield deployment, validation, operations and rollback.

Plasma is per-endpoint software with a desk-side correlation tool. It does not require a central server, a database or an internet-facing service. The “desk” is a hardened jump host or management workstation that pulls bounded event tails from endpoints only when asked.

docs.title: Reference architecture
docs.text:
Plasma in an Active Directory domain: local detection, pull-based management, no required central lake.

Domain controllers are supported as endpoints, but Kerberos events (4768/4769/4770/4771) exist only on a KDC. A member server reporting zero Kerberos events is not broken; it is not a KDC.

docs.title: 1. Design decisions
docs.text: Decision Recommended default Why Installation mode MSI, FULL (Sysmon + WHIDS) Detection-first; MINIMAL is a deliberate exception Management transport WinRM over HTTPS (5986) NTLM over HTTP is relay-prone; Plasma refuses insecure WinRM by default Desk placement Hardened jump host in the management VLAN No inbound listener on endpoints Update ring canary pilot OU, then broad Limits a bad release to the pilot Event retention 7–30 days, size-capped Bounded local store, not a lake Canary placement User-data shares and Documents Impact detection where ransomware acts Canary shield Pilot OU first, audit/dry-run before arm Active kill needs a controlled pilot Pipe canaries One per user/server ring, pilot first A connecting client is a strong signal, but scanners need allowlisting Prevention Audit first, then enforce per control A bad AppLocker/CFA policy can break a business app Central SIEM Optional forwarding of local JSONL Plasma does not require one

docs.title: Active Directory
docs.text:
• Domain-joined Windows 10/11 or Windows Server 2019/2022/2025.
  • An OU for pilot hosts and an OU for broad rollout.
  • A security group for Plasma administrators and a separate group for the desk/fleet operators.
  • Time synchronization (Kerberos and event correlation depend on it).
  • DNS resolution for management names and any canary token suffix.
  • If using the fleet desk over WinRM, a service account or gMSA with local administrator rights on the managed hosts. The password is supplied via an environment variable (password_env); never in fleet.json.

docs.title: Windows host
docs.text:
• PowerShell 5.1 or later.
  • Sysmon installed and logging. WHIDS makes the Sysmon service dependent on the WHIDS service at install.
  • WHIDS 1.7.0 payload for FULL mode.
  • Local administrator (or SYSTEM) for install, services, Sysmon config and scheduled tasks.
  • Windows Firewall:
  • inbound WinRM 5986 from the management VLAN only;
  • inbound RDP 3389 from the operator jump host only;
  • no inbound Plasma service is required.
  • Outbound HTTPS 443 for updates and Sysmon acquisition, or an internal mirror.
  • Event log sizing: Security and Sysmon at least 512 MB each on servers, 256 MB on workstations.

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
Source Destination Port Purpose Jump host endpoint TCP 5986 WinRM HTTPS Operator jump host TCP 3389 RDP to the desk Endpoint update/GitHub TCP 443 Signed self-update Endpoint DNS UDP/TCP 53 Name resolution, DNS canary tokens Endpoint SIEM/collector TCP 443/6514 Optional forwarding Canary collector endpoint/browser TCP 8088 Optional HTTP token collector

Do not expose plasma serve directly to user networks. Bind it to loopback or the management VLAN and use TLS with a certificate from the enterprise PKI.

docs.title: Manual install (pilot)
docs.text:
# 1. Download the release assets and verify them
Get-FileHash .\plasma-1.25.0-windows-x64.exe -Algorithm SHA256
Get-Content .\SHA256SUMS
Get-AuthenticodeSignature .\plasma-1.25.0-windows-x64.exe | Format-List

# 2. Dry-run the install plan
.\plasma-1.25.0-windows-x64.exe install --dry-run

# 3. Install
.\plasma-1.25.0-windows-x64.exe install

# 4. Verify
plasma --version
plasma health
plasma status
plasma whids status

The MSI equivalent:

msiexec /i plasma-1.25.0-windows-x64.msi /qn /norestart /l*v C:\Windows\Temp\plasma-msi.log

The installer:

  • verifies the embedded manifest and payload hashes;
  • chooses FULL or MINIMAL;
  • stages the instance, WHIDS payload and Sysmon baseline;
  • writes C:\ProgramData\Plasma\config.json;
  • registers PlasmaWatch, PlasmaUpdate, the WHIDS watchdog and the identity-pull task;
  • adds AtStartup and StartWhenAvailable to PlasmaWatch, PlasmaWhidsWatchdog and, when armed, PlasmaCanaryShield, so protection resumes immediately after reboot;
  • flips the current junction.

docs.title: Domain rollout with Group Policy
docs.text:
Use a computer startup script or a GPO-delivered scheduled task. Do not use a user logon script: the install needs SYSTEM.

  1. Put the signed MSI and SHA256SUMS on a read-only DFS share.
  2. Create a startup script that verifies the SHA-256 before running MSI.
  3. Target the pilot OU first.
  4. Use a WMI filter or security-group filter for the pilot ring.
  5. After the pilot window, link the same GPO to the broad OU.

Example startup script:

$src = '\\dfs\software\plasma\plasma-1.25.0-windows-x64.msi'
$sum = '\\dfs\software\plasma\SHA256SUMS'
$expected = (Get-Content $sum | Select-String 'plasma-1.25.0-windows-x64.msi').Line.Split()[0]
$actual = (Get-FileHash $src -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower()
if ($actual -ne $expected.ToLower()) { throw 'Plasma MSI hash mismatch' }
Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i `"$src`" /qn /norestart" -Wait

docs.title: SCCM / Intune
docs.text:
• Detection method: file C:\ProgramData\Plasma\bin\plasma.exe exists and plasma --version returns the expected version.
  • Install command: msiexec /i plasma-1.25.0-windows-x64.msi /qn /norestart
  • Return codes: 0 and 3010 success; 1641 reboot initiated.
  • Requirement: 64-bit Windows, PowerShell 5.1, local administrator.
  • Deploy to a pilot collection first; use the same ring tags as the GPO path.

docs.title: MINIMAL mode
docs.text:
Use MINIMAL only where Sysmon/WHIDS cannot be installed:

.\plasma-1.25.0-windows-x64.exe install --skip-whids

MINIMAL still provides identity events, the ETW tap, DTrace (where present), canaries, memory scanning and the investigation/case tools. It does not provide the always-on gene-rule detection plane. health and coverage will name the gap.

docs.title: 4. Configure
docs.text:
The primary file is:

C:\ProgramData\Plasma\config.json

A production-oriented example:

{
  "version": "1.25.0",
  "events_path": "C:\\ProgramData\\Plasma\\data\\events.jsonl",
  "sensors": {
    "whids": {"status": "active", "min_version": "1.7.0"},
    "sysmon": {"status": "active"}
  },
  "retention": {"max_mb": 512, "keep_files": 4},
  "response": {
    "enabled": true,
    "mode": "enforce",
    "min_score": 9,
    "max_actions_per_run": 2,
    "cooldown_seconds": 1800
  },
  "canary": {
    "accounts": ["svc-print-archive"]
  },
  "update": {"ring": "broad"},
  "serve": {"bind": "127.0.0.1", "port": 9999}
}

Rules:

  • Keep events_path on a local disk, not a network share.
  • Protect the root with SYSTEM + Administrators only; the installer does this.
  • response.mode: enforce still uses the policy allowlist, score floor, action cap, cooldown, approval queue and kill switch.
  • canary.accounts must be accounts that no legitimate process uses.
  • update.ring is one of canary, broad, rollback.
  • Secrets do not belong in config files. Use environment variables named by token_env / password_env.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Purpose PLASMA_EVENTS Override the event store for probes PLASMA_SERVE_API_KEY HTTP API key PLASMA_SCOPES MCP scopes PLASMA_TENANT MCP tenant PLASMA_GITHUB_TOKEN Private release repository PLASMA_TG_TOKEN Telegram notification token PLASMA_SIGNER_THUMBPRINTS Allowed update signers

docs.title: 5. Domain GPO baseline
docs.text:
Policy Setting WinRM Allow WinRM; HTTPS listener with enterprise PKI certificate; firewall scope management VLAN RDP Enabled, NLA required, TLS security layer, restricted source Audit Logon/logoff success+failure, account management, process creation, object access as required PowerShell Script block logging, module logging, constrained language where compatible Defender Real-time on, ASR audit first, CFA audit then block, Network Protection audit then block AppLocker/WDAC Audit first; pilot OU before broad Event logs Security and Sysmon size/retention per host role Time Domain hierarchy; reliable external source on the PDC Firewall Outbound 443 to update/SIEM only; inbound management only

Do not apply CFA block or WDAC enforce to the whole domain in one step. plasma prevent posture and the pilot ring exist to prevent exactly that.

docs.title: 6. Deploy the fleet desk
docs.text:
On a hardened jump host:

pip install 'plasma-edr[desk]'
# or use the signed plasma.exe and the desk-side extras

$env:WS1PW = Read-Host -AsSecureString | ConvertFrom-SecureString -AsPlainText
plasma fleet scan --inventory C:\PlasmaDesk\fleet.json --case incident-42 --window 3600
plasma fleet report --case incident-42

fleet.json:

{
  "hosts": [
    {
      "name": "WS1",
      "transport": "winrm",
      "endpoint": "https://ws1.corp.example:5986/wsman",
      "username": "CORP\\svc-plasma-ro",
      "password_env": "WS1PW",
      "events_path": "C:\\ProgramData\\Plasma\\data\\events.jsonl"
    },
    {
      "name": "WS2",
      "transport": "file",
      "events_path": "D:\\Exports\\WS2\\events.jsonl"
    }
  ]
}

The desk pulls a capped tail, correlates deterministic joins and writes a case dossier. Credentials stay in the environment, never in the inventory or the case directory.

docs.title: 7. Deploy the active canary shield
docs.text: The shield turns file and registry canaries into a narrow active defence: a process that creates, deletes or registry-writes a canary is identified from Sysmon and killed after verification. Named-pipe canaries add a local listener: a client that connects to the decoy pipe is identified by PID and killed after the same verification. A pure in-place overwrite with no create/delete has no Sysmon write event; canary verify still records the hash change, but without process attribution. Plan the shield around ransomware behaviour (create encrypted copy, delete original) and registry tamper, not around every possible file edit.

docs.title: 7.1 Deploy canaries
docs.text:
plasma canary deploy --dir D:\Shares\Finance --dir D:\Shares\HR
plasma canary registry deploy --hive HKCU --count 1
plasma canary registry deploy --hive HKLM --count 1
plasma canary pipe deploy --count 1
plasma canary verify

Use realistic user-data shares. A canary in an empty folder called “Canaries” is not a canary; it is a signpost.

docs.title: 7.2 Preview the shield
docs.text:
plasma canary shield status
plasma canary shield install

The preview shows the file and registry conditions added to the Sysmon config and the SYSTEM task that will be registered. It does not write.

docs.title: 7.3 Arm in the pilot OU
docs.text:
plasma canary shield install --apply --plan 4 --reason "IR-2026-042 pilot"
plasma canary shield status
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName PlasmaCanaryShield

The task runs every minute as SYSTEM. Each sweep:

  1. reads Sysmon FileCreate/FileDelete and RegistryEvent rows in the window;
  2. matches only the recorded canary basenames and registry fragments;
  3. refuses PID 0/4, protected processes, Plasma itself, Explorer and common backup/AV/system processes;
  4. verifies the PID still exists and still has the recorded image;
  5. kills the process, journals the decision and caps kills per sweep.

docs.title: 7.4 Prove it in a maintenance window
docs.text:
# start a benign child process that writes the canary, then sleeps
$canary = (Get-Content C:\ProgramData\Plasma\canaries.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).canaries[0].path
$p = Start-Process powershell -PassThru -ArgumentList @(
  '-NoProfile','-Command',"Set-Content -LiteralPath '$canary' -Value test; Start-Sleep 120")
Start-Sleep 2
plasma canary shield sweep --since-minutes 5 --apply --reason "shield drill"
Get-Process -Id $p.Id -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

The process should be gone and canary-shield-journal.jsonl should contain the kill with the canary path, PID, image and verification result. A read (Get-Content $canary) must produce no kill; an Explorer delete must be skipped as trusted.

docs.title: 7.5 Named-pipe canary
docs.text:
plasma canary pipe deploy --count 1
plasma canary pipe install
plasma canary pipe install --apply --plan 6 --reason "IR-2026-042 pipe pilot"
plasma canary pipe status

The listener runs at boot as SYSTEM and restarts on failure. A client that connects to the decoy pipe is identified with GetNamedPipeClientProcessId; a scanner that only enumerates pipes is not touched. Protected processes are refused, Plasma/Defender/backup/system are trusted, and a dry-run listener records without killing. Each decision is written to canary-pipe-journal.jsonl; canary pipe status reports the live connection and kill counters, so you do not have to wait for the task to stop.

A pipe is a stronger trigger than a file canary in one respect — the client must actively connect — but it also carries a higher operational risk: security scanners and some management agents probe pipes. Pilot it in a small ring, watch the journal for skips, and allowlist your own tooling before arming broadly.

docs.title: 7.6 Disarm
docs.text:
plasma canary shield uninstall --apply --plan 5 --reason "change window"
plasma canary pipe uninstall --apply --plan 7 --reason "change window"

This unregisters the tasks and restores the previous Sysmon config.

docs.title: 8. Post-install validation
docs.text:
plasma health
plasma status
plasma whids status
plasma watch once
plasma coverage
plasma query --kind alert --since 24h --count-by process
plasma detect test
plasma prevent posture
plasma canary shield status

Expected on a healthy FULL node:

  • health.status = ok;
  • whids_service = Running, sysmon_service = Running;
  • sensor_heartbeat within the store window;
  • coverage rollup reported, with named blind spots;
  • detect test 10/10;
  • prevent posture names gaps rather than inventing success.

docs.title: 9. SIEM and evidence
docs.text:
• Forward events.jsonl and WHIDS alerts to the SIEM if required; the local store remains the source of truth for the endpoint.
  • Forward Security/Sysmon channels with Windows Event Forwarding if the estate already has it.
  • Use plasma case for investigations; case seal + case verify produces tamper-evident evidence.
  • Use plasma assurance sbom, safety-case, support-bundle and evidence export for audit packages. Support bundles are redacted.

docs.title: 10. Operations
docs.text:
Task Command Daily health plasma health, plasma watch once Store hygiene plasma store stats, store rotate, store compact Update rings plasma ring status, update auto --check-only Rollback plasma rollback Prevention drift plasma prevent posture, prevent status Canary integrity plasma canary verify, canary shield status Case review plasma case list, case timeline, case report Fleet sweep plasma fleet scan --inventory fleet.json --case ...

Keep the kill switch tested. A kill switch that has never been exercised is a hope, not a control.

docs.title: 11. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check WHIDS service hangs at StartPending plasma whids diagnose; prune the dump tree No Sysmon events Get-Service Sysmon64; plasma health; Sysmon config WinRM login fails HTTPS listener, certificate trust, firewall, password_env Fleet pull returns 0 rows endpoint events_path, service heartbeat Canary shield never fires Sysmon config includes, canary shield status, task state Shield skips a process journal reason: trusted, protected, stale PID, max kills Prevention apply fails policy-managed host or tamper protection; prevent posture Update fails signer pin, SHA256SUMS, ring, kill switch, update-journal.jsonl Disk growth store stats; retention; WHIDS dump prune

docs.title: 12. Enterprise checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Pilot OU and broad OU defined.
  • [ ] Signed MSI verified by SHA-256 and Authenticode.
  • [ ] WinRM HTTPS with enterprise PKI; no HTTP WinRM outside a controlled lab.
  • [ ] Sysmon and WHIDS running on FULL nodes.
  • [ ] Root ACL SYSTEM + Administrators only.
  • [ ] Event store on local disk, retention set.
  • [ ] Response policy reviewed; kill switch tested.
  • [ ] Prevention controls piloted in audit mode.
  • [ ] Canaries deployed to user-data shares.
  • [ ] Canary shield previewed, armed in pilot, and drill-proven.
  • [ ] Fleet inventory uses password_env, never inline secrets.
  • [ ] SIEM forwarding, if used, tested.
  • [ ] Case seal/verify tested.
  • [ ] Update ring and rollback tested.
  • [ ] Blind spots accepted and documented.

docs.title: 13. Plugin distribution
docs.text:
Treat plugins like any other signed software:

  1. Build and sign in a controlled pipeline; keep the private key offline.
  2. Publish the payload plus plugin.json, SIGNATURE and the publisher's public key.
  3. Install with plasma plugin install ... --pubkey publisher.pem --enable from the same GPO/SCCM/Intune workflow that installs Plasma.
  4. Pin the publisher key in the deployment script; do not accept an embedded key without a pinned expectation.
  5. Roll out to the pilot OU first. plugin verify and plugin health are the post-install checks.
  6. Disable a misbehaving plugin with plasma plugin disable; remove it with plasma plugin remove.

Responder plugins add actions; they do not bypass the plan/approval gate. Review each action's argv and permissions.filesystem before enabling it.

docs.title: 14. Limits
docs.text:
• No kernel driver: kernel malware, malicious drivers and direct syscalls are outside the claim.
  • Canary shield is near-real-time (one-minute task), not in-kernel.
  • No central console; the desk is pull-based by design.
  • WDAC remains read-only in Plasma.
  • Independent MITRE/red-team validation and large-scale soak testing are not included.

docs.title: Estate edge ledger
docs.text:
The estate ledger answers the questions a single endpoint cannot — one account on fifty machines in an hour, one source address across a subnet, a host that went quiet — without moving raw events and without a central log lake.

Each host reduces a bounded window of its own store into a small, hash-sealed identity ledger. The desk pulls those ledgers, replaces the previous copy for that host, and merges them into one continuously updated estate view.

host store (events.jsonl)                 desk
┌────────────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ last 60 min, ≤ 20k rows│        │ pull one ledger per host     │
│ who / from where /     │  ───▶  │ replace → merge → correlate  │
│ which process and hash │ counts │ estate.json + findings.json  │
└────────────────────────┘        └──────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: What a host ledger contains
docs.text:
The ledger is deliberately lossy. It stores counts, never command lines, file paths, raw descriptions, or the event diary itself.

Field Meaning host, role stable host name and estate role generated_at when this reduction ran window minutes covered, start and end n rows considered inside the window users per account: count, first, last, bounded sources, logon_types processes user>process counts, capped at 200 hashes file hash counts, capped at 100 truncated how many identities were dropped by the caps integrity SHA-256 over the ledger body

Caps are absolute: 200 users, 10 source addresses per user, 200 process pairs, 100 hashes and a 256 KiB ledger. If the blob still exceeds the byte cap, hashes are dropped and process pairs are trimmed to 50, and size_after_trim records the result. A host ledger is normally a few kilobytes.

Machine and service accounts (HOST$, SYSTEM, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE) are excluded, and DOMAIN\user and UPN forms collapse to the same account name.

docs.title: Build a ledger
docs.text:
plasma estate build `
  --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl `
  --window 60 --max-rows 20000 `
  --host WS1 --role member `
  --out C:\ProgramData\Plasma\estate\WS1.json

Local and remote builds use the same code. sync runs exactly this command on each Windows host over WinRM and reads the result back byte-exact (base64), so the console code page cannot corrupt it, then deletes the temporary file.

docs.title: Merge and correlate
docs.text:
plasma estate merge --dir .\estate\hosts --out .\estate\estate.json
plasma estate findings --ledger .\estate\estate.json --threshold 5
plasma estate status --ledger .\estate\estate.json

merge keeps the newest ledger per host, so a re-run replaces that host's previous view instead of double-counting it. Merging the same set twice produces the same estate ledger. Per-host state survives a desk restart: the ledger files under hosts/ are the state.

--max-age (default 180 minutes) marks a host ledger stale when it has not been refreshed; stale is a finding, not a silent gap.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
Finding Score Rule estate_user_fanout 9 one account on ≥ threshold hosts with a source address shared across ≥ 2 of them estate_user_fanout 7 same-name pattern on ≥ threshold hosts, no shared source — verify before acting estate_source_fanout 9 one source address touching ≥ threshold hosts estate_hash_fanout 8 the same file hash on ≥ threshold hosts estate_stale_host 8 ledger older than --max-age estate_new_host_edge 7 a user/host pair absent from --baseline, for users seen on 2+ hosts

The score split matters. A name appearing in many places is not proof of one identity: Administrator, admin and svc-backup are reused across estates by design. The ledger therefore only raises a fan-out to 9 when the same source address links at least two of those appearances. Otherwise it reports 7 and says same-name pattern; verify.

--baseline points at a previous estate.json. New user/host edges are the drift signal — an account that has never been on a host before.

docs.title: Continuous sync
docs.text:
plasma estate sync --inventory inventory.json --out-dir C:\PlasmaEstate `
  --window 60 --workers 8 --threshold 5 --max-age 180 --interval 300 --loop

sync pulls one ledger per host in parallel, saves hosts/<name>.json, merges to estate.json, writes findings.json, and returns one JSON summary. With --loop it prints one summary line per cycle and sleeps for --interval seconds (minimum 10). A failed host is recorded in failures and the cycle continues; a cycle only fails when no host ledger could be built.

Inventory is the same file used by plasma fleet:

{
  "hosts": [
    {"name": "WS1", "endpoint": "44.197.31.152:5985", "transport": "winrm",
     "username": "Administrator", "password_env": "WS1PW",
     "events_path": "C:\\ProgramData\\Plasma\\data\\events.jsonl"},
    {"name": "WS2", "endpoint": "52.3.242.251:5985", "transport": "winrm",
     "username": "Administrator", "password_env": "WS2PW",
     "events_path": "C:\\ProgramData\\Plasma\\data\\events.jsonl"}
  ]
}

Passwords stay in environment variables. HTTPS WinRM is recommended for a real domain (see Fleet); a controlled lab may set "allow_insecure_winrm": true. transport: "file" accepts either events_path (reduce a local store) or ledger_path (read a ledger produced elsewhere), which makes air-gapped and test environments first-class.

docs.title: Scale
docs.text:
The work is linear in hosts and bounded in memory:

  • Each host sends one small ledger, not an event tail. There is no growing central index and no per-event insert on the desk.
  • merge and findings are single passes over the ledgers. A 1,000-host estate with 10,000 distinct accounts merges and correlates in a couple of seconds on a laptop; the resulting estate ledger stays in the low megabytes.
  • Estate caps (5,000 users, 5,000 process pairs, 5,000 hashes, 20,000 hash/host pairs) and the truncated counters keep a pathological domain from exhausting memory.
  • Pulls are parallel but capped at 32 workers. Old copies are replaced, so disk use is proportional to the number of hosts, not to time.

A 300-second cadence over 1,000 hosts is roughly 3.3 ledger pulls per second — well inside a desk-side process. For larger estates, shard the inventory by site and merge the shard ledgers with plasma estate merge --ledgers.

docs.title: Integrity and residency
docs.text:
• Every ledger carries a SHA-256 over its canonical body. load, merge --dir and status recompute it and refuse a modified ledger. This detects corruption and casual edits; it is not a signature. The trust boundary is the desk's filesystem ACL and the WinRM channel.
  • The desk receives identities, counts and source/destination addresses — not command lines, file paths, event descriptions or full event rows.
  • Old ledgers are replaced in place, so the estate view is a current snapshot, not a history. Keeping history is an explicit choice: copy estate.json into a case directory if you need it.
  • Findings are ordinary JSON and can be fed to plasma export webhook|syslog or any SIEM without shipping the store.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The ledger correlates what sensors record. A host that is blind produces a small ledger, not an error — pair it with plasma fleet attestation.
  • Counts cannot explain why. When a fan-out finding matters, pull the bounded event tail for those hosts with plasma fleet pull and read it.
  • Same-name accounts are common. Treat score 7 as a question, not a verdict.
  • The ledger is not a substitute for a SIEM's long retention; it is the estate-wide view that a lake-less design can honestly maintain.

docs.title: Is Plasma an EDR?
docs.text: Functionally yes — endpoint detection and response with sensors, scoring, correlation and containment. Architecturally it deliberately drops the central lake and the always-on vendor console, and it refuses to put the model in the action path.

docs.title: Why no central log lake?
docs.text: Because the questions teams actually ask are about recent, bounded history ("what happened on this box in the last hour?"), and shipping every event to a central store is a large standing cost and a large standing target. Plasma keeps a bounded local diary and pulls only what a case needs. When you do need estate-wide correlation, fleet joins bounded tails on the desk.

docs.title: What is actually different from SIEM/SOAR?
docs.text: SIEM SOAR Plasma Data central lake orchestrates other tools bounded local diary per box Detection correlation rules in the lake playbooks trigger on alerts written rules + chains over local events Response tickets automation with credentials named, dry-run-first, journaled, undoable actions Model vendor AI in the cloud n/a 121M on-device router over a closed probe menu

docs.title: Can it block or kill automatically?
docs.text:
Yes. There are two tiers. Containment is armed by default but narrow; prevention is audit-first and opt-in.

  • Containment (plasma enforce) reacts to findings in seconds: injection findings first write a host snapshot, then kill the accessing process at score 9+, with a 2-action per-run cap and a 30-minute cooldown. A tripped canary queues host isolation for approval, as do quarantine, disabling users, removing admins, stopping services, credential rotation, task/Run-key/WMI removal and IP blocking. The installer registers PlasmaWatch, which runs the sweep every 5 minutes; plasma protect disarm turns automatic containment off.
  • Enforcement points (plasma prevent) stop behaviour before it runs by configuring AppLocker, firewall egress, Defender ASR and LSA protection. AppLocker starts in audit; every control is dry-run first, plan-gated, verified and rollbackable by journal id.

docs.title: How is memory scanning different from Sysmon/ETW?
docs.text: Sysmon and ETW tell you what a process did. HollowsHunter/PE-sieve looks at what is inside the process now: replaced images, implanted PEs, shellcode, patches and IAT hooks. It is an on-demand, hash-pinned user-mode probe, not a standing monitor. Scan a PID or a small name set; --all is explicit. No dumps are written by default.

docs.title: Does interception require a kernel driver?
docs.text: No. plasma intercept brokers typed rules into NTFS ACLs, Windows Firewall and the MCP tool-call boundary. It does not ship a minifilter, WFP callout or API hook. Kernel-mode malware, malicious drivers and direct syscalls are outside the claim; AppLocker/ASR remain under plasma prevent.

docs.title: Do canary tokens need Docker or a cloud service?
docs.text:
No. File canaries are local documents. DNS tokens are read from the local Sysmon channel through a narrow EID 22 include. HTTP tokens are served by plasma canary serve, which binds loopback by default and refuses a non-loopback bind without an explicit flag. There is no container, no external callback and no telemetry endpoint.

Every apply still passes a dry-run + plan gate, and the kill switch blocks all containment. Plasma does not ship its own kernel driver.

docs.title: Does the AI decide anything?
docs.text: It selects a probe from a fixed menu and fills arguments; it cannot invent tools, read raw logs, or run commands. Detection and correlation are deterministic code.

docs.title: Can it run fully offline?
docs.text: Yes. With internet, the installer provisions Sysmon automatically. Without it, the install degrades to MINIMAL mode (identity + tap) and everything else works from local data.

docs.title: Does it phone home?
docs.text: No. There is no Plasma cloud service. The only outbound update traffic is the release check against GitHub: PlasmaUpdate once a day by default, or an explicit plasma update check / plasma update auto. Nothing else is sent.

docs.title: Does Plasma self-update?
docs.text: Yes, by default. The installer registers PlasmaUpdate, a daily SYSTEM task with a random minute inside the 02:00–05:00 maintenance window. It applies signed releases only, through the same SHA256 + Authenticode + install + rotate path as plasma update apply. broad hosts wait 24 hours after publication; canary hosts update first; rollback hosts never auto-update. The kill switch pauses updates, and the previous binary is kept for plasma rollback. --no-autoupdate disables it; plasma update auto --check-only reports availability without installing.

docs.title: How many hosts can a desk manage?
docs.text: fleet is bounded by your WinRM reachability and the desk's patience, not by a license. Each pull takes a capped tail per host (default 300 rows).

docs.title: What about Linux/macOS hosts?
docs.text: Plasma targets Windows endpoints. The fleet desk runs on macOS/Linux (WinRM client). A Linux sensor is a separate roadmap item.

docs.title: Where are credentials stored?
docs.text: Never in Plasma configs. Inventory uses password_env; notify uses token_env; inline secrets are refused. The desk environment (or your secret manager) holds the values.

docs.title: Is the model fine-tunable for my estate?
docs.text: The supported adaptation is the probe menu, not the weights: add a probe, run the gap loop, re-export the menu, redeploy the same bundle. Weight fine-tuning of the tiny router is not shipped as a supported path.

docs.title: Is Plasma signed?
docs.text: Releases are Authenticode-signed by the project certificate, and update applies are verified against pinned signer thumbprints. Publicly trusted signing (SignPath Foundation) is applied for; SmartScreen reputation builds after approval.

docs.title: Is it open source?
docs.text: MIT. Repository: DrOlu/plasma.

docs.title: How do I report a security issue?
docs.text: Open a GitHub issue for non-sensitive reports. For sensitive ones, contact the maintainer through the address on the repository profile rather than posting details publicly.

docs.title: Can I extend Plasma with my own sensor or action?
docs.text: Yes. Plugins are bounded external processes with a signed manifest: sensor, detector, responder, and the reserved exporter kind. Write one in any language, sign it with plasma plugin keygen and plugin sign, install it with a pinned public key, and enable it explicitly. The core still validates every record, owns the event store and gates response actions. See Plugins.

docs.title: File integrity monitoring (FIM)
docs.text:
Canaries answer "did something destroy a decoy?" — impact. FIM answers the compliance question: did a critical file change? Plasma records (path, sha256, size) for a configurable set of paths and diffs it on demand or during every watch sweep.

This is the control PCI DSS 11.5.1 asks for; it is deliberately separate from the canary machinery because the two answer different questions.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
plasma fim baseline --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma
plasma fim verify   --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma   # exit 2 when changed
plasma fim status   --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma

Add your own critical paths (files or globs):

plasma fim baseline --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma `
  --path "C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\*" `
  --path "D:\Apps\gateway\config\*.yaml"

The baseline is stored at <root>\fim.json. Re-run baseline after an approved change; otherwise the change is reported, which is the point.

docs.title: Default paths
docs.text:
Path Why C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts name resolution tampering ...\etc\services, ...\etc\networks service/port tampering C:\ProgramData\Plasma\config.json sensor configuration C:\Program Files\Whids\config.toml detection configuration

Bounds: 5,000 files and 32 MB per file. Paths are expanded as globs and de-duplicated by resolved path.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
Change Type Score Hash changed fim_modified 8 File removed fim_removed 8 New file matched a monitored glob fim_added 6

watch lifts these into its finding list, so a modified critical file makes the verdict act now (score ≥ 8). A missing baseline is not an error storm: verify returns a hint to run plasma fim baseline, and watch ignores the collector until a baseline exists.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: FIM watches content of named paths, not every file on the disk. It is not a replacement for AIDE/Tripwire on a Linux estate; on Windows it covers the high-value configuration and boot-adjacent files an operator can name.

docs.title: Fleet — one desk, many computers
docs.text: Cross-host correlation is where a per-box tool becomes an estate tool. The desk pulls a bounded event tail from each host, then joins them locally.

docs.title: Inventory
docs.text:
{
  "hosts": [
    {
      "name": "WS1",
      "endpoint": "44.197.31.152:5985",
      "transport": "winrm",
      "username": "Administrator",
      "password_env": "WS1PW",
      "events_path": "C:\\ProgramData\\Plasma\\data\\events.jsonl"
    },
    {
      "name": "WS2",
      "endpoint": "52.3.242.251:5985",
      "transport": "winrm",
      "username": "Administrator",
      "password_env": "WS2PW",
      "events_path": "C:\\ProgramData\\Plasma\\data\\events.jsonl"
    }
  ]
}

Rules:

  • transport: "winrm" pulls over WinRM/NTLM. HTTPS is required (https://host:5986) because NTLM over plain HTTP is relay-prone. A controlled lab may set "allow_insecure_winrm": true to opt into HTTP. Omit the transport (or use "file") to read a local copy.
  • Passwords are never in the file — password_env names an environment variable on the desk.
  • Both transports produce the same rows; the WinRM path reads the file byte-exact via base64 (PS text output re-encodes through the console codepage and can corrupt JSON), with a -Tail fallback for locked files.

docs.title: Pull → correlate → report
docs.text:
plasma fleet pull      --inventory inventory.json --case incident-42 --cap 300 --window 21600
plasma fleet correlate --case incident-42 --window 21600
plasma fleet report    --case incident-42

State lives under <root>/fleet-cases/<case>/:

case.json                    window, canaries, created
answers/WS1.events.jsonl     pulled tails
answers/*.attest.json        optional observatory answers per host
report.md                    rendered dossier

docs.title: Correlation scores
docs.text:
Finding Score Rule canary_tripped 10 a canary account appears on any host canary_token_hit 9 a DNS/HTTP canary token fired on a host lateral_hop 9 the same user on 2+ hosts within the window shared_hash 8 the same file hash on 2+ hosts blind_host 8 a host's self-check reports blindness or an unhealthy sensor shared_domain 7 the same DNS query on 2+ hosts shared_ip 7 the same destination IP on 2+ hosts

Notes:

  • Window is in seconds (default 1800; a 6-hour incident review uses 21600).
  • Timestamps are normalized to UTC; naive rows are treated as UTC so mixed formats correlate instead of crashing.
  • --canary alice --canary bob (or config in the existing case) marks accounts that must never appear; --window and --canary on an existing case update it rather than being silently ignored.
  • The report is Markdown, deterministic, and sized for pasting into a ticket.

docs.title: Continuous estate ledger
docs.text:
fleet answers an incident question from a bounded event tail. The estate edge ledger answers the standing question — who is touching how many hosts right now? — at a cadence, from counts only.

plasma estate sync --inventory inventory.json --out-dir C:\PlasmaEstate `
  --window 60 --workers 8 --threshold 5 --interval 300 --loop
plasma estate findings --ledger C:\PlasmaEstate\estate.json
plasma estate status   --ledger C:\PlasmaEstate\estate.json

Each host reduces its own store to a small hash-sealed ledger (users, sources, user>process counts and hashes). The desk replaces that host's previous ledger, merges everything and raises:

Finding Score Meaning estate_user_fanout 9 / 7 one account on many hosts; 9 only when a source address links at least two estate_source_fanout 9 one source address across many hosts estate_stale_host 8 a host stopped refreshing its ledger estate_hash_fanout 8 the same file hash on many hosts estate_new_host_edge 7 a user/host pair absent from --baseline

The event diary never leaves the box; only the counts do. See Estate edge ledger for the schema, caps, scale and residency model.

docs.title: Plugin events
docs.text: Plugin sensor events and detector findings are ordinary rows in the local store, so fleet pull carries them like any other event. A plugin finding is an alert row with alert_id=plugin:<name>; fleet correlation does not need to know the plugin existed.

docs.title: Example finding
docs.text:
[9/10] lateral_hop
  user 'administrator' on 2 hosts within 85 min: WS2 -> WS1

That is a genuine correlation from a two-host estate: the ordering comes from first-seen timestamps, so the report tells you the direction of travel.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Requirement Notes Windows Server 2016+ or Windows 10/11, x64. PowerShell 5.1 is assumed. Privileges Administrator (sensors, services, ETW, firewall). Network Optional. With internet, the installer provisions Sysmon automatically; without it, Plasma runs a reduced mode. Disk ~200 MB for the app plus bounded event stores. Python None at runtime — the release is a single self-contained exe.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
.\plasma-<version>-windows-x64.exe install

The installer is intelligent — it inspects the box and picks a mode:

Observed state Decision Result No WHIDS, no Sysmon, internet full Sysmon downloaded (EULA accepted), WHIDS registered and started WHIDS service present, Sysmon missing full + repair Sysmon installed, WHIDS (re)started — the broken-install case No internet / --skip-whids skipped (MINIMAL, degraded) Identity + ETW tap carry detection Both present already_present Installer verifies and leaves services alone

Always preview first:

.\plasma-<version>-windows-x64.exe install --dry-run

Useful flags:

plasma install --force                 # replace the current install
plasma install --root D:\Plasma        # custom root
plasma install --skip-whids            # force MINIMAL mode
plasma install --skip-sysmon-check     # do not attempt the Sysmon download
plasma install --require-whids         # fail (exit 3) instead of degrading

The installer:

  1. verifies the embedded payload against its SHA-256 manifest;
  2. decides FULL or MINIMAL from the box's actual state;
  3. installs Sysmon when needed (official package, EULA accepted non-interactively);
  4. provisions WHIDS in detect-only mode and registers the service (containment ships armed but narrow; prevention is audit-first);
  5. writes config.json (sensors, paths, install mode);
  6. flips instances\current to the new version atomically;
  7. reports the whole decision as JSON.

docs.title: First checks
docs.text:
plasma health          # verdict: ok | degraded | down, with per-check detail
plasma status --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl

Healthy output (FULL node):

{"status": "ok", "failed": [], "checks": [
  {"check": "events_store", "ok": true},
  {"check": "whids_service", "ok": true, "detail": "service Running"},
  {"check": "sysmon_feed", "ok": true, "detail": "newest Sysmon event 0.0 min old"},
  {"check": "sysmon_service", "ok": true, "detail": "service Running"},
  {"check": "tap_sidecar", "ok": true},
  {"check": "sensor_heartbeat", "ok": true, "detail": "newest event 2 min old"}
]}

A MINIMAL node reports "install_mode": "MINIMAL mode — expected reduced coverage" and is not penalized for lacking WHIDS.

docs.title: Collect something real
docs.text:
# logons from the Security channel into the store
plasma identity pull --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl --since 60

# alerts WHIDS already wrote — normalize them into the same store
plasma whids pull --root "C:\Program Files\Whids" --out C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl

# a bounded live ETW window (no service, no persistence)
plasma tap run --providers powershell,dns --for 10s --max-matches 200

# every auto-start location, with signature status
plasma deep persistence --json-out C:\ProgramData\Plasma\deep-persistence.json

docs.title: Ask questions
docs.text:
plasma ask --prompt "critical alerts" --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl
plasma probe --tool plasma_recent --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl
plasma observe attest      # can this box even see itself?
plasma drift record attest # record today's truth as the baseline

docs.title: Schedule the watchman
docs.text:
plasma watch once     # health + drift + new alerts + chains → verdict

Exit codes: 0 clean, non-zero when findings exist — ideal for Task Scheduler. Configure Telegram/webhook delivery in C:\ProgramData\Plasma\notify.json (see Operations).

docs.title: Protection
docs.text:
Containment is armed by default but narrow: snapshot + kill_process at score 9+, 2 actions per run, 30-minute cooldown; isolation and every other action require approval. Prevention is audit-first and opt-in. Start with the posture, then a plan:

plasma enforce status                 # policy, journal, kill switch
