plasma enforce run                    # proposals only (dry-run)
plasma prevent status                 # AppLocker / Defender / firewall posture
plasma prevent applocker --mode audit # generate a plan; nothing applied yet

To arm containment, set enforcement.enabled and mode: "enforce" in config.json, then run plasma watch once --enforce. Start with allowed_actions: ["kill_process"] and leave isolation behind approval. The full safety model is in Prevention and blocking.

docs.title: Install a plugin (optional)
docs.text:
Plugins are not required for normal operation. To try the signed flow:

plasma plugin new acme --kind sensor --out C:\build
plasma plugin keygen --out C:\build\keys
plasma plugin sign --plugin C:\build\acme --key C:\build\keys\plugin-private.pem
plasma plugin install C:\build\acme --pubkey C:\build\keys\plugin-public.pem --enable
plasma plugin run acme --max-events 5

The sample sensor writes five normalised events to the store. plugin list shows the enabled state; plugin disable acme stops it. See Plugins before installing third-party code.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
plasma update check     # anonymous; exit 0 = current, 2 = update available
plasma update apply     # downloads, verifies SHA-256 *and* the signer, installs

From 1.2.0 onward the downloaded exe must be signed by a pinned certificate or the update is refused before execution.

docs.title: Interception
docs.text:
Interception is the layer between a sensor and a responder: it sees an attempt at the boundary and can allow, deny, or record a would-be denial.

Plasma does not ship a kernel driver. It brokers typed rules into gates Windows already owns:

Point Native gate Enforced by File write / delete NTFS deny ACE Windows file system Network connect Windows Firewall Windows Filtering Platform Agent tool call MCP boundary Plasma gateway Process exec AppLocker / WDAC plasma prevent Credential access Defender ASR plasma prevent

The model may propose a rule. It cannot apply one without the plan gate.

docs.title: Phase 0 — shadow evaluation
docs.text:
plasma intercept rules add --file rules.json
plasma intercept evaluate --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl

Reads a bounded tail of the event store and reports would_block decisions without touching the host. Use this to tune rules before enforcement.

docs.title: Phase 1 — canary protection
docs.text:
plasma intercept protect-canary
plasma intercept protect-canary --apply --plan 7 --reason "canary protection"

Adds a deny ACE for write/delete by Everyone to every file in the canary manifest. The canary becomes both a tripwire and a small safe: a destructive writer is denied and the attempt is still evidence. The prior SDDL is saved for rollback.

If the operator token lacks SeSecurityPrivilege, the audit rule is skipped and the deny ACE is still applied. Enable File System auditing separately to receive failure events in the Security log.

docs.title: Phase 2 — agent tool-call gateway
docs.text:
The MCP tools/call path evaluates intercept rules before policy, handlers or mutations:

{
  "id": "no-isolate",
  "point": "agent_tool_call",
  "action": "deny",
  "backend": "gateway",
  "mode": "enforce",
  "match": {"tool": "isolate_host"}
}

A denied call returns INTERCEPTED with the rule id and an audit ledger entry. A mode: "shadow" rule is audited but does not block.

docs.title: Phase 3 — native policy broker
docs.text:
plasma intercept rules add --file rules.json
plasma intercept apply block-test-net            # dry-run
plasma intercept apply block-test-net --apply --plan 12 --reason "IR-42"
plasma intercept rollback --id 12                # dry-run
plasma intercept rollback --id 12 --apply --plan 15 --reason "test complete"

Enforcing backends:

  • acl — canary file deny/audit ACL.
  • firewall — outbound Windows Firewall block for one IPv4 destination.
  • gateway — MCP boundary; no host mutation.

AppLocker and ASR remain available through plasma prevent with the same dry-run, plan, journal and rollback discipline.

docs.title: Rule shape
docs.text:
{
  "id": "protect-finance-canary",
  "point": "file_write",
  "action": "deny",
  "backend": "acl",
  "mode": "enforce",
  "match": {"path_prefix": "D:\\Finance"},
  "priority": 10,
  "ttl_seconds": 3600,
  "reason": "canary protection"
}

Supported points: file_write, file_delete, file_read, process_exec, network_connect, dns_query, credential_access, agent_tool_call.

Supported match fields: path_prefix, process, user, host, dest_ip, dest_port, technique, event_id, tool, tenant.

The highest priority wins; ties resolve deny > require_approval > allow > audit.

docs.title: Safety model
docs.text:
• Dry-run first. Apply requires the plan id from a seen dry-run with the same payload digest.
  • Single-use plan. A plan cannot be applied twice.
  • Kill switch. Blocks ACL, firewall and rollback execution; dry-runs remain available.
  • Bounded. The shadow evaluator reads a capped tail; no raw stream.
  • Reversible. ACL rollback restores the exact prior SDDL; firewall rollback removes the named rule.
  • No arbitrary shell. Paths, IPs and rule fields are validated; the only PowerShell is generated from typed fields.
  • No kernel driver. The broker owns policy, not the kernel.

docs.title: What it will not do
docs.text:
• It will not stop kernel-mode malware, malicious drivers or direct syscalls; that would require a driver.
  • It will not stop an administrator from disabling it.
  • It will not inspect encrypted C2 without a TLS proxy.
  • It will not replace backups, least privilege or detection.

docs.title: Estate evidence
docs.text:
On WS1 and WS2 (Windows Server 2022):

  • shadow rules matched the synthetic event store;
  • the canary ACL denied a write and rollback restored write access;
  • a 203.0.113.9 outbound firewall rule appeared and was removed;
  • the MCP gateway returned INTERCEPTED for a denied get_health call.

docs.title: Investigation
docs.text: Plasma is lake-less, but an investigation still needs to answer precise questions, follow lineage, keep the evidence and hand over a sealed artifact. Four local surfaces cover that loop: query, tree, summarize and case. They read the same bounded JSONL store and never send it anywhere.

docs.title: Typed query
docs.text:
plasma query --process powershell.exe --since 1h
plasma query --kind alert --min-score 0.7 --count-by process
plasma query --host WS1 --user CORP\olu --since 24h
plasma query --spec incident-42-query.json

The query language is closed. A typo in a field name is an error, not a silent widening of the search:

Field Meaning host, user, kind, source, action, severity exact match event_id, pid integer match process, parent, image basename match, case-insensitive, */? globs technique ATT&CK ID, e.g. T1055 contains case-insensitive substring across description, command line, image, path, DNS and alert ID regex explicit regular expression over the same fields since, until ISO timestamp or duration (15m, 1h, 2d) min_score, max_score 0–1 event score count_by aggregate over host, user, kind, process, event_id and more limit, max_rows, order bound the result and the tail read

The reader is bounded to the last --max-rows (default 5000) within an 8 MiB tail. --out writes the full result locally.

docs.title: Process lineage
docs.text:
plasma tree --pid 4832
plasma tree --process powershell.exe --depth 2

tree builds parent/child edges only from explicit pid/ppid pairs. Sysmon EID 1 and Security 4688 both populate ppid when the audit policy records it. A missing parent is reported as an orphan root; Plasma does not guess lineage from a process name.

Depth is capped at 10 and the result at 500 nodes. Truncation is explicit.

docs.title: A bounded digest
docs.text:
plasma summarize --since 1h
plasma summarize --since 24h --limit 50 --rare-max 1

summarize is the orientation step before a query or a case: process first/last seen, parent→child frequencies, top users and hosts, score bands, event sources and rare command lines. It is a map, not the territory, and every section is capped.

docs.title: Case workspace
docs.text:
A case is a directory under <root>/cases/<name>:

case.json          metadata and counts
events.jsonl       selected event rows
findings.jsonl     selected findings
notes.md           operator notes
report.md          rendered Markdown report
manifest.json      sealed per-file hashes + chain hash

plasma case open IR-2026-042 --host WS1 --title "LSASS access"
plasma case add IR-2026-042 --process lsass.exe --since 2h
plasma case add IR-2026-042 --technique T1055 --min-score 0.7
plasma case note IR-2026-042 "Confirmed with the user"
plasma case timeline IR-2026-042
plasma case report IR-2026-042
plasma case seal IR-2026-042
plasma case verify IR-2026-042

case add refuses to run without a filter: a case is a selection, not a copy of the diary. Duplicate rows are not appended twice. Reopening a case never clears evidence.

case seal hashes every artifact and writes a chain hash. case verify recomputes it and exits 2 on any changed or missing file. Sealing is tamper evidence, not encryption.

docs.title: Detection engineering
docs.text:
plasma detect validate --rules sensors/plasma-baseline.gen
plasma detect test
plasma detect diff --old old.gen --new candidate.gen
plasma detect replay --events captured.jsonl

validate compiles every regex expression and checks condition variables; test runs deterministic hit/miss chain cases; diff reports rules added, removed and changed by name and content hash; replay runs the chain engine and a bounded summary over a captured store. Promotion stays on the existing install/WHIDS path, so a rule cannot reach a live sensor without passing that gate.

docs.title: What this does not do
docs.text:
• It does not create a database or index. Every read is a bounded tail.
  • It does not infer lineage from process names.
  • It does not sign or encrypt a case; it seals it with SHA-256 hashes.
  • It does not call a model. All four surfaces are deterministic.

docs.title: Memory scanning
docs.text:
File and process telemetry can tell you that a process started. It cannot tell you what was later written into that process. plasma memory scan covers that gap with HollowsHunter, the PE-sieve-based user-mode scanner for hollowed or replaced PEs, reflective DLLs, shellcode, inline hooks and in-memory patches.

It is an on-demand probe, not a standing service. No driver, no cloud and no automatic memory lake.

docs.title: Scan targets
docs.text:
plasma memory scan --pid 4832
plasma memory scan --pname powershell.exe,rundll32.exe
plasma memory scan --pid 4832 --deep
plasma memory scan --all --timeout 120

--all is explicit. Prefer a PID or a small name set: a full scan is slow, noisy and can be evaded between scans.

--deep adds --shellc and thread-stack scanning. The default scan is targeted and bounded by --timeout (default 300s).

docs.title: Reports and events
docs.text:
Each scan gets a directory under <root>/memory/<timestamp>/ containing:

stdout.txt       scanner output
stderr.txt       scanner errors
report.json      normalized JSON payload when present
meta.json        argv, target, elapsed time, counts

Findings become normal Plasma events:

{
  "ts": "2026-11-20T10:00:00Z",
  "host": "WS1",
  "source": "memory",
  "kind": "alert",
  "event_id": 9100,
  "severity": "critical",
  "score": 0.95,
  "action": "logged",
  "technique": "T1055.012",
  "alert_id": "memory:hollowing:684:notepad.exe",
  "process": "notepad.exe",
  "pid": 684,
  "file_path": "C:\\Windows\\notepad.exe",
  "description": "HollowsHunter hollowing: notepad.exe"
}

watch, chain, fleet and the response policy consume these rows like any other alert. The event store never contains raw memory images.

docs.title: Dumps
docs.text:
The scanner does not write files by default. --dump is explicit:

plasma memory scan --pid 4832 --dump

Dumps can contain credentials, tokens and customer data. They are written under <root>/memory/, governed by the Plasma root ACL, and refused with --all. Treat them as evidence and apply your retention policy.

docs.title: JIT noise
docs.text: The scanner can classify managed .NET JIT regions as shellcode. Plasma suppresses those observations from the alert stream and reports the count in suppressed_managed_jit. A PowerShell deep scan can therefore show suspicious_count: 1 with findings: []; that is intentional.

docs.title: Pinned payload
docs.text:
The Windows release bundles:

sensors/memory/hollows_hunter64.exe
sensors/memory/hollows_hunter32.exe
sensors/memory/LICENSE
sensors/memory/VERSION

Both binaries are SHA-256 pinned. A mismatched binary is refused rather than executed. The scanner is BSD-2-Clause; its notice travels with the payload and is included in plasma assurance sbom.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• User-mode only: kernel-mode malware, malicious drivers and direct syscalls remain outside the claim.
  • Point-in-time: a short-lived implant can execute and vanish between scans.
  • Protected processes may be unreadable.
  • Full scans are expensive; targeted scans are the default.
  • The scanner may be flagged by other security products; allowlist it deliberately.

docs.title: Triggered triage
docs.text:
plasma memory triage
plasma memory triage --since-minutes 240 --max-targets 10 --min-score 0.9

triage reads the recent event tail and selects only PIDs justified by an injection- or credential-shaped signal: a T1055/T1620/T1003 technique, a memory finding, or language such as shellcode, hollowing, injection or LSASS. A high score alone (for example a ransomware alert) does not become a memory scan. The default window is 60 minutes and the default cap is five targets. No target returns NO_TARGETS, not an error.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
plasma memory status     # resolver, hash, last scan
plasma memory list       # archived scan metadata

docs.title: neuralOSd orchestrator
docs.text:
neuralOSd is an optional, local orchestrator that sits in front of Plasma. It turns a natural-language question into a closed list of typed probes, refuses when no probe matches, and returns a signed envelope. The model never sees a host credential or a shell; the bridge runs allowlisted Plasma CLI verbs over WinRM.

Plasma's built-in MCP server remains the zero-dependency agent surface. neuralOSd is for teams that want a local model, a refusal gate and a probe menu in front of the same typed tools.

docs.title: What it adds
docs.text: Layer Plasma alone With neuralOSd Question routing MCP client chooses a tool 121M on-device model chooses from a closed probe menu Refusal Tool errors and policy denials Typed refusal reasons (no_probe_matches, action_intent, dropped_filter, low_coverage) Response CLI plan → apply → undo Model mints the plan; operator applies and undoes Evidence Hash-chained ledger Signed envelope with menu and gate versions Deployment Single exe, no Python Separate instance on a desk; WinRM to the estate

docs.title: The plasma-estate instance
docs.text:
The reference instance lives at ~/neuralos-instances/plasma-estate/ and has 20 probes:

Group Probes Estate health, coverage, events (kind/severity filters), estate report Response plans block IP, isolate, snapshot, disable user, quarantine file, remove admin, stop service, delete task, disable task, remove run key, disable WMI subscription, kill process Observatory attest, sketch, edges, explain, flowstats, pslogs, attackmap, regedges, canary, sysmon health Security checks chain, WHIDS, canary, FIM, prevention, audit, playbook, enforcement, deep, eval, evidence, SBOM, policy, approvals, kill switch, tenants, drift, store stats, trace, tap, identity Advanced trace list/selftest/run, prevention dry-runs, playbook dry-runs, kill switch on/off, identity pull Fleet cross-host pull, correlate and report from the desk

docs.title: Safety boundary
docs.text:
The model can propose; the operator disposes.

  1. The model selects a probe and fills typed arguments.
  2. The bridge runs an allowlisted Plasma CLI verb over WinRM.
  3. A response probe returns a Plasma dry-run plan id; nothing is applied.
  4. The operator reviews the plan and runs orchestrate.py apply <id>.
  5. orchestrate.py undo <id> reverses it.

The model cannot widen its scopes, run an arbitrary command, or hide a request from the ledger. Protected paths, accounts, services and processes are refused by Plasma before the plan is minted.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
neuralosd ask --instance-dir ~/neuralos-instances/plasma-estate \
  "is the estate healthy"

neuralosd ask --instance-dir ~/neuralos-instances/plasma-estate \
  "propose a block plan for 192.0.2.2 on WS1"

python orchestrate.py apply <plan>
python orchestrate.py undo <plan>

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
The 1.15.9 drill ran the instance against WS1 and WS2:

  • health, coverage, chain, attack map, PowerShell logs, canary, FIM, deep persistence, DTrace selftest, ETW tap selftest, identity pull, eval, evidence, SBOM, policy, approvals, kill switch, tenants, drift, store stats and fleet;
  • response plans for block, disable, quarantine, remove-admin, task, service, Run key and snapshot were applied and reversed;
  • protected targets were refused;
  • both hosts parse 100% of the event store.

See DEEP_TEST_1.15.9.md in the instance directory for the full matrix.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A Python desk with neuralosd installed and the instance directory.
  • WinRM reachable on the estate (5985 with allow_insecure_winrm in a lab, or 5986 HTTPS in production).
  • Host credentials in the bridge, or a secret store; never in the model menu.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
plasma health
Check Fails when Verdict impact events_store store is not writable degraded whids_service expected but not Running down sysmon_feed no Sysmon event within 60 min down sysmon_service Sysmon expected but stopped down tap_sidecar tap binary missing degraded sensor_heartbeat newest store row older than 24 h degraded rdp_hardening_drift RDP disabled or security layer drifted degraded canary_integrity a deployed canary is missing or modified degraded blind_spot_accounting never — it names known gaps informational install_mode never — it documents MINIMAL mode informational

MINIMAL-mode nodes are not penalized for lacking WHIDS: the sensor list comes from the install decision recorded in config.json.

The verdict now includes a blind_spots[] list: skipped sensors, disabled Sysmon event IDs, failed feeds, an undeployed canary, and the coverage engine's named ATT&CK gaps. A blind spot is not a service failure, but it is never silent either.

docs.title: Enforcement posture
docs.text:
plasma prevent posture

Inventory of the signed Windows controls behind prevention: active WDAC policy files, Controlled Folder Access, Network Protection, the vulnerable driver blocklist, ASR rule counts, real-time protection and tamper protection. Each row says whether Plasma can apply it and gives the preview command. WDAC stays read-only; CFA, Network Protection and the driver blocklist are opt-in and plan-gated with rollback.

docs.title: Watch — the scheduled sweep
docs.text:
plasma watch once                 # one sweep, JSON + exit code
plasma watch loop --every 3600    # long-running; or schedule `watch once`

A sweep gathers:

  1. the health verdict,
  2. drift against the attest baseline,
  3. new WHIDS alert rows since the last sweep (growth-based, so pulled rows never re-fire),
  4. chain matches over the events tail,
  5. canary-file integrity (missing/modified = score 10).

Output: findings[], top_score, and a verdict of clean / investigate / act now. watch-state.json records each run; watch-alerts-state.json tracks the alert-row watermark.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
<root>/notify.json:

{
  "channels": [
    {"type": "telegram", "token_env": "PLASMA_TG_TOKEN", "chat_id": "123456789"},
    {"type": "webhook",  "url": "https://hooks.example.com/plasma"}
  ],
  "min_score": 7
}
  • Secrets are only via token_env; inline token fields are refused.
  • Delivery is gated by min_score (default 7).
  • Alerts are throttled by the loudest finding's type: at most one message per finding type per hour, and the throttle window only burns when a channel actually accepted the message. A broken webhook retries next sweep.
  • plasma notify show validates the file; plasma notify test sends one.

docs.title: Enforcement and prevention
docs.text:
plasma protect status                  # armed? containment + prevention + protected
plasma protect protected               # what the response layer refuses to touch
plasma protect disarm --reason "change window"
plasma protect arm
plasma enforce status                  # policy, journal counts, kill switch
plasma enforce run                     # dry-run proposals
plasma enforce run --apply             # policy still gates every action
plasma enforce pending
plasma enforce approve --id 4 --apply
plasma prevent status                  # read-only posture
plasma prevent rollback --id 7 --apply # undo an applied prevention control

Containment ships armed but narrow: snapshot + kill_process at score 9+, 2 actions per run, 30-minute cooldown. Isolation and every other action require approval. The installer registers PlasmaWatch, which runs watch once --enforce at boot and every 5 minutes; --no-autoprotect removes it and installs the old dry-run posture. PlasmaWatch, PlasmaWhidsWatchdog and PlasmaCanaryShield carry both an AtStartup trigger and StartWhenAvailable, so a reboot or a missed timer run is picked up immediately. PlasmaUpdate deliberately keeps its daily maintenance-window trigger and does not run at boot.

enforce-journal.jsonl records every decision (including refusals and cooldowns); prevent-journal.jsonl records every control change with its undo recipe. Prevention backups live in prevent-backups/. Neither file is rotated automatically — they are audit records.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
Plugins are installed once, verified, enabled explicitly and then run on a cadence or on demand.

plasma plugin list
plasma plugin verify acme --pubkey acme.pem
plasma plugin health acme
plasma plugin run acme --max-events 100
plasma plugin run acme-detector --since 1h
plasma plugin disable acme

install verifies the manifest, entrypoint, payload digest and Ed25519 signature, then copies the payload under <root>\plugins\<name>; it does not enable it. disable is the quick containment. Sensor runs enforce the manifest's max_events, max_line_bytes and timeout_seconds, log stderr to <root>\logs\plugin-<name>.log, and quarantine a plugin after ten invalid records.

Ingest and export are bounded adapters, not collectors:

plasma ingest jsonl .\events.jsonl --max-events 500
plasma ingest evtx --channel System --since 15 --max-events 200
plasma ingest webhook --port 8787 --secret-env PLASMA_INGEST_SECRET --once
plasma export webhook --url https://siem.example/ingest --since 1h
plasma export syslog --host 192.0.2.10 --port 514 --protocol udp

A failed export spools the unsent tail under <root>\export-spool with a 5,000-line cap. Drain and retry; do not raise the cap indefinitely.

Responder actions stay plan-gated:

plasma plugin actions
plasma plugin act acme.restart_agent --args-file args.json
plasma plugin act acme.restart_agent --args-file args.json --apply --plan <id> --reason "change window"
plasma plugin undo <journal-id> --reason "rollback"

Apply checks the kill switch and the enabled flag, runs only the declared argv, verifies and journals the rollback. Paths must sit under the plugin's declared filesystem roots.

docs.title: Estate ledger
docs.text:
The estate ledger is the scheduled, estate-wide counterpart to fleet pull. Each host reduces its recent store to a hash-sealed count ledger; the desk merges the newest ledger per host and correlates identity fan-out and stale hosts.

plasma estate sync --inventory inventory.json --out-dir C:\PlasmaEstate --interval 300 --loop
plasma estate findings --ledger C:\PlasmaEstate\estate.json --threshold 5
plasma estate status   --ledger C:\PlasmaEstate\estate.json

Run it on the same cadence as watch (typically 5–15 minutes). Check failures in each sync summary: a host that cannot build a ledger is a coverage problem, not a quiet host. A stale_host finding means the desk has not refreshed that host inside --max-age. A score-7 user fan-out is a same-name pattern until a shared source address proves otherwise; escalate to plasma fleet pull for the hosts involved before acting.

Keep estate.json and hosts/ on the desk, not on endpoints. Replace-in-place means the view is current, not historical — copy a snapshot into a case directory if it must be retained. See Estate edge ledger.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
plasma update auto --check-only   # exit 2 when an update is available
plasma update auto                # apply if due
plasma update auto --force        # reinstall even if the version matches
plasma update auto --ring canary  # override the configured ring
plasma update check
plasma update apply
plasma rollback

The installer registers PlasmaUpdate, a daily SYSTEM task with a random minute inside the 02:00–05:00 maintenance window. It applies signed releases only, through the same SHA256 + Authenticode + install + rotate path as update apply. broad hosts wait 24 hours after publication; canary hosts update first; rollback hosts never auto-update. The kill switch pauses updates. A host's explicit ring assignment wins over the configured default. Around the swap Plasma stops the tasks that hold the binary (PlasmaServe, PlasmaWatch, PlasmaWhidsWatchdog, PlasmaIdentityPull), stops every other plasma* process so no child can keep the old image on port 9999, retries a locked image, preserves a stale .old backup, restores the previous binary if the swap fails, and restarts the tasks afterwards — so PlasmaServe serves the new version. A serve-launched update skips PlasmaServe to avoid killing its own process tree. The previous binary is kept, so plasma rollback still restores it. update-journal.jsonl and update-state.json record every attempt.

--no-autoupdate on install removes the task and disables automatic updates. See Updates and signing.

docs.title: Store hygiene
docs.text:
plasma store stats   --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl
plasma store rotate  --events ... --max-mb 50 --keep 3
plasma store compact --events ...
  • rotate renames the live file to .1, shifts .k → .k+1, and drops the oldest beyond --keep. Runs are no-ops below the size limit.
  • compact drops exact duplicate rows (key-order-insensitive), preserves torn/noise lines, and swaps atomically via a temp file.
  • stats reports row count, size, kind histogram and time span.

The store stays a plain JSONL file — rotation never changes the contract.

docs.title: Identity pulls
docs.text:
plasma identity pull --events <store> --since 60 [--host NAME] \
                    [--ids 4624,4625,4688,4768,4769,4776] [--max-events 2000]

Reads the Security channel from the local host, normalizes auth and process records onto the event contract, and appends with dedupe. --host labels the rows when the store is shared. Kerberos IDs are only meaningful on a domain controller; on a member server they return zero rows by design.

docs.title: Drift baselines
docs.text:
plasma drift record attest
plasma drift score  attest     # exit 0 clean / 2 drift / 1 collection error
plasma drift list

Baselines live under <root>/drift/. Score refuses to overwrite a good baseline with a failed collection.

docs.title: Asking questions
docs.text:
plasma ask --prompt "critical alerts" --events <store>
plasma ask --prompt "network connections to 203.0.113.9" --events <store>
plasma probe --tool plasma_persistence --events <store>
plasma status --events <store>

status shows the bundle identity and the probe menu; probe runs one named probe; ask lets the on-device model choose the probe. Every answer is JSON; refusals are structured (GATE_VERSION 1), never guesses.

docs.title: Observatory (self-knowledge)
docs.text:
plasma observe attest
plasma observe sketch
plasma observe edges
plasma observe attackmap
plasma observe pslogs

These are read-only witness questions: can the box see its own logons, its services, its network edges? attest includes a blind check — a box that cannot see itself reports that honestly, and fleet correlation turns it into a blind_host finding.

docs.title: Canaries and tokens
docs.text:
plasma canary deploy --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma [--dir D:\Finance]
plasma canary verify --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma   # exit 2 when tripped
plasma canary status --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma
plasma canary token create --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma --kind dns --domain assets.internal
plasma canary sysmon --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma --apply
plasma canary token create --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma --kind http --base-url http://collector:8088
plasma canary serve --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8088
plasma canary collect --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma
plasma canary hits --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma

Deploy file canaries once per node (and on data shares with --dir). The default layout is randomized and the content is a valid document, so the decoy does not announce itself. watch verifies them from then on.

DNS tokens need a narrow Sysmon include: run canary sysmon --apply after creating them. It writes Plasma's baseline plus the token include and replaces the current Sysmon config, so review a custom config first. It logs only queries ending in a registered token suffix; ordinary DNS traffic stays out of the channel. HTTP tokens point at one local collector; bind it to loopback or a management VLAN, never the internet. Hits are appended to the event store by watch or canary collect, and deduplicated across sweeps.

Add canary accounts to config.json:

{"canary": {"accounts": ["svc-print-archive"]}}

A tripped canary is evidence. Snapshot and isolate before investigating; the enforcement policy keeps isolate_host behind approval.

docs.title: Memory scanning
docs.text:
plasma memory status
plasma memory scan --pid 4832
plasma memory scan --pname powershell.exe,rundll32.exe --deep
plasma memory scan --all --timeout 120
plasma memory list

HollowsHunter/PE-sieve is a pinned, on-demand probe for in-memory implants. Target a PID or a small name set; --all is explicit. No dumps are written by default. --dump is local, explicit and refused with --all. Findings land in the event store as source="memory" alerts; a clean scan is a point-in-time result, not proof of innocence.

docs.title: Interception
docs.text:
plasma intercept status
plasma intercept rules add --file rules.json
plasma intercept evaluate --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl
plasma intercept protect-canary
plasma intercept protect-canary --apply --plan 7 --reason "canary protection"
plasma intercept apply block-test-net --apply --plan 12 --reason "IR-42"
plasma intercept rollback --id 12 --apply --plan 15 --reason "test complete"

Shadow evaluation reports would-block decisions without changing the host. Canary protection adds an NTFS deny ACE; normal Administrator tokens may not hold SeSecurityPrivilege, so the audit rule can be skipped while the deny still applies. Firewall rules are outbound blocks by destination. Every apply is dry-run first, single-use plan-bound, journaled and reversible.

docs.title: Scheduling
docs.text:
Task Scheduler (or cron on a desk) runs, at minimum:

*/15 * * * *   plasma whids pull --root "C:\Program Files\Whids" --out <store>
0 * * * *      plasma identity pull --events <store> --since 70
0 */6 * * *    plasma watch once

After every watch, re-arm the alert watermark by pulling; otherwise the watchman will (correctly) keep reporting growth.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
Plasma plugins are processes with a manifest, not Python imports. Sysmon, WHIDS, the ETW tap and DTrace already work this way: an external component runs, emits a bounded record stream, and Plasma validates and normalises it. The plugin ABI makes that pattern available to anything you write or buy.

A plugin may contribute one of four things:

Kind Emits Runs sensor PlasmaEvents plasma plugin run <name> on a cadence detector findings over a bounded event tail plasma plugin run <name> responder named actions with preview/apply/rollback plasma plugin act exporter nothing (outbound) reserved for the export adapters

They can be written in any language: a native binary, Python, or PowerShell. The wire format is newline-delimited JSON.

docs.title: Install and run
docs.text:
plasma plugin new acme-bridge --kind sensor --out C:\build
plasma plugin keygen --out keys
plasma plugin sign --plugin C:\build\acme-bridge --key keys\plugin-private.pem
plasma plugin install C:\build\acme-bridge `
  --pubkey keys\plugin-public.pem --enable
plasma plugin run acme-bridge --max-events 100
plasma plugin verify acme-bridge --pubkey keys\plugin-public.pem

Nothing is auto-enabled. install verifies the manifest, entrypoint, payload digest and Ed25519 signature (unless --allow-unsigned is explicitly used), copies the payload to <root>\plugins\<name> and records it in <root>\plugins\registry.json.

docs.title: Manifest
docs.text:
plugin.json follows schemas/plugin-manifest.schema.json:

{
  "api_version": "1.0",
  "name": "acme-bridge",
  "version": "0.3.1",
  "kind": "sensor",
  "description": "Acme agent events",
  "entrypoint": "acme-bridge.exe",
  "runtime": "native",
  "protocol": "ndjson-stdio",
  "capabilities": ["event.process", "event.network"],
  "permissions": {
    "filesystem": ["C:\\ProgramData\\Acme\\**"],
    "network": ["https://acme.example/*"]
  },
  "limits": {
    "max_events": 1000,
    "max_line_bytes": 65536,
    "timeout_seconds": 60
  },
  "health": { "command": ["acme-bridge.exe", "--health"] },
  "min_core": "1.28.0"
}

entrypoint must stay inside the plugin directory. limits are enforced by the host, not trusted from the plugin.

docs.title: Records
docs.text:
One JSON object per line:

{"v":1,"type":"event","plugin":"acme-bridge","seq":1,"event":{
  "ts":"2026-11-22T15:00:00Z","kind":"process","process":"cmd.exe",
  "parent":"explorer.exe","pid":1234,"score":0.2
}}
{"v":1,"type":"finding","plugin":"acme-detector","finding":{
  "description":"encoded PowerShell","score":0.8,
  "technique":"T1059.001","evidence":["2026-11-22T15:00:00Z"]
}}
{"v":1,"type":"health","status":"ok"}

The core:

  • rejects records over max_line_bytes, unknown envelope versions and unknown types;
  • maps known fields onto the strict PlasmaEvent contract and puts unknown fields in a bounded attributes map;
  • stamps source=plugin:<name>, plugin=<name>@<version> and the host;
  • clamps scores to 0–1 and validates technique IDs;
  • dedupes against the tail and appends only fresh records;
  • quarantines invalid lines and stops a run after ten bad records.

Plugins never write events.jsonl directly. That is what stops a plugin from forging another source or corrupting the diary.

docs.title: Detectors
docs.text:
A detector is a process invoked with:

<entrypoint> --events <store> --max-rows <n> [--since <iso>]

It prints finding envelopes. Findings become kind=alert rows with alert_id=plugin:<name>, the technique, a clamped score and bounded evidence. The runner enforces a timeout and rejects over-scoring.

Rule packs can be validated with the existing harness:

plasma detect validate --rules C:\plugins\acme\rules\pack.gen

docs.title: Responders
docs.text:
A responder declares actions in actions.json:

{"actions":[{
  "name": "acme.restart_agent",
  "description": "restart the Acme agent",
  "args_schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"service":{"type":"string"}},"required":["service"]},
  "preview": ["acme-cli","restart","--dry-run","{{service}}"],
  "apply":   ["acme-cli","restart","{{service}}"],
  "verify":  ["acme-cli","status","{{service}}"],
  "rollback":["acme-cli","start","{{service}}"],
  "reversible": true
}]}

plasma plugin act without --apply renders the exact argv and returns a plan id. Applying requires that id and a reason, checks the kill switch and the plugin's enabled state, runs only the declared argv (no shell), verifies, and journals the result with its rollback argv. plasma plugin undo replays that rollback.

Path arguments are checked against permissions.filesystem. A plugin cannot write outside the roots it declared.

docs.title: Ingest and export
docs.text:
Inbound adapters:

plasma ingest jsonl .\events.jsonl --max-events 500
plasma ingest evtx --channel Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational --since 15
plasma ingest webhook --port 8787 --secret-env PLASMA_INGEST_SECRET --once

The webhook receiver requires X-Plasma-Signature: sha256=<hmac> when a secret is configured, caps bodies at 2 MiB and validates every record.

Outbound:

plasma export webhook --url https://siem.example/ingest --secret-env PLASMA_EXPORT_SECRET --since 1h
plasma export syslog --host 192.0.2.10 --port 514 --protocol udp --since 1h

Exports are batched and bounded. A failed sink spools the unsent tail under <root>\export-spool with a hard line cap — never an unbounded queue.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text:
• Signed manifests and payloads; pin the publisher key with --pubkey.
  • Install is explicit; enable is separate; plugin disable is the quick containment.
  • Plugins cannot modify config, rules, baselines or services; the registry and store are core-owned.
  • Responder actions are plan-gated, reason-bearing, kill-switch aware and reversible when declared.
  • Runtime limits: line size, event cap, timeout, output cap; process isolation is a child process with its own working directory.
  • Secrets are injected as environment variables at start and never written to the manifest or logs.

The remaining hardening step is stronger OS isolation (Job Objects and AppContainer) for untrusted plugins; the current release enforces process separation, limits and signature verification.

docs.title: Samples
docs.text: examples/plugins/ contains a sensor, a detector and a responder scaffolded by plasma plugin new, used by the unit tests and the estate drill.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
State Meaning How it changes installed verified and copied, not enabled plugin install enabled may run plugin enable disabled plugin run refuses unless --force plugin disable running a bounded run is in flight plugin run ok last run completed inside its caps registry last_result quarantined ten invalid records stopped the run fix the emitter, then run again timeout the manifest deadline was reached bound the plugin or raise the limit broken manifest or entrypoint no longer validates reinstall or remove removed payload and registry entry deleted plugin remove

plugin list reports the state, signature, digest, last run and last result. plugin health runs the manifest health command; a plugin without one reports its registry state.

docs.title: Manifest reference
docs.text: Field Required Meaning api_version yes 1.0; unknown majors are refused name yes lowercase id, 1–64 chars version yes semver-like kind yes sensor, detector, responder, exporter entrypoint yes relative path inside the plugin directory runtime yes native, python, powershell protocol yes ndjson-stdio description no shown by plugin list capabilities no declared event families permissions no filesystem, registry, network lists limits no max_events, max_line_bytes (≤ 65536), timeout_seconds, max_score health no { "command": [...] } actions responders path to actions.json rules detectors path to a declarative pack min_core no refuse an older core

docs.title: Record reference
docs.text:
Type Required Notes event event object with a timestamp or a usable signal mapped onto the strict PlasmaEvent contract finding description, score (0–1) becomes a plugin alert; technique and evidence optional health status surfaced in the run summary log any ignored; stderr is the log

Every record needs v: 1 and type. A record larger than max_line_bytes, an unknown version or an unknown type is rejected and counted.

docs.title: Responder reference
docs.text:
Actions are argv arrays with {{placeholder}} substitution:

  • preview — required; rendered and returned by a dry-run.
  • apply — required; runs only after a matching plan id and reason.
  • verify — optional; runs after apply and must exit 0.
  • rollback — optional; required for reversible: true.
  • args_schema — JSON Schema subset: object, string/integer/boolean, required, no unknown keys.
  • permissions.filesystem — path arguments must resolve under one of these roots; ${root} expands to the Plasma root.

--args-file is the reliable way to pass JSON on Windows. Plans expire after 24 hours. Every apply and undo is a JSONL journal entry with the argv, result, verify result and rollback argv.

docs.title: Ingest and export reference
docs.text:
Adapter Direction Caps ingest jsonl inbound file --max-events, validation, dedupe ingest evtx inbound channel --since minutes, --max-events ingest webhook inbound HTTP 2 MiB body, HMAC, --max-events, --seconds/--once export webhook outbound batches, retries, 5,000-line spool export syslog outbound UDP/TCP --max-events, 8 KiB line cap

Export URLs must be http or https; other schemes are refused before any request.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix install: refusing unsigned no SIGNATURE or wrong key sign it, or --allow-unsigned in a lab verify exits 2 payload changed after install review, then install --force run: quarantined ten invalid records read <root>\logs\plugin-<name>.log run: timeout manifest deadline raise limits.timeout_seconds or bound the plugin act: outside permitted roots path escaped permissions use a declared root act: kill switch is engaged switch on plasma control killswitch status webhook 401 bad HMAC sign the body with the configured secret webhook 413 body over 2 MiB batch smaller

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: api_version is a major.minor contract. The core supports the current major and refuses unknown ones; min_core lets a plugin require a newer Plasma. Record fields are additive: unknown event keys land in attributes, unknown top-level record types are rejected. Plugin-defined kind values are not consumed by chains or profiles until registered in core.

docs.title: Testing a plugin
docs.text:
plasma plugin new acme-test --kind sensor --out C:\build
# implement, then:
plasma plugin sign --plugin C:\build\acme-test --key keys\plugin-private.pem
plasma plugin install C:\build\acme-test --pubkey keys\plugin-public.pem --enable
plasma plugin run acme-test --events C:\temp\events.jsonl --max-events 3
plasma query --events C:\temp\events.jsonl --source plugin:acme-test

For responders, preview first and inspect the exact argv; apply against a disposable target; undo and confirm the journal. For detectors, seed a store with a known row and check alert_id=plugin:<name>.

docs.title: Distribution
docs.text: Ship the plugin directory, its SIGNATURE, and the publisher's public key. Install with a pinned key from the same GPO/SCCM/Intune workflow that installs Plasma. Keep the private key offline. Treat a plugin update as a new signed artifact: verify, install, then enable.

docs.title: Prevention and blocking
docs.text:
Plasma has two prevention tiers, and they are deliberately different things.

Tier Mechanism Blocks first execution? Latency 0 — Containment plasma enforce turns findings into allowlisted, reversible actions No seconds to minutes 1 — Enforcement points plasma prevent configures AppLocker, Windows Firewall, Defender ASR, LSA, Controlled Folder Access, Network Protection and the driver blocklist Yes at execution / connection

Plasma does not ship a kernel driver. Inline blocking at the file, process and network boundary belongs to Microsoft's signed components; Plasma generates, applies, verifies and rolls back their policy. That is a deliberate trade: policy you can roll back beats a driver you cannot crash-test.

docs.title: Measured default (1.17.0+)
docs.text:
Containment is armed by default, but narrow:

  • automatic actions: snapshot, then kill_process;
  • score floor: 9;
  • per-run cap: 2;
  • per-target cooldown: 30 minutes;
  • everything else — isolation, quarantine, disabling users, removing admins, stopping services, credential rotation, task/Run-key/WMI removal and IP blocking — requires human approval;
  • the installer registers PlasmaWatch, a SYSTEM task that runs watch once --enforce every 5 minutes.
plasma protect status
plasma protect protected
plasma protect disarm --reason "change window"
plasma protect arm
plasma protect arm --apply-prevention --reason "pilot AppLocker audit"

--no-autoprotect installs the old dry-run posture and removes the PlasmaWatch task. Upgrades replace exactly the pre-1.17 enabled: false block; a custom operator block is preserved.

docs.title: Tier 0 — policy-gated containment
docs.text:
plasma protect status
plasma enforce status
plasma enforce run                 # dry-run: proposals only
plasma enforce run --apply         # policy still gates each action
plasma enforce pending
plasma enforce approve --id 4      # dry-run of the stored request
plasma enforce approve --id 4 --apply
plasma enforce run --findings findings.json   # evaluate supplied findings

Findings map to actions:

Finding Action Default injection technique (T1055 family) with a PID snapshot, then kill_process automatic when armed chain_injection_chain / chain_injection_apc_chain snapshot, then kill_process on the image PID automatic when armed canary_tripped, canary_dns_tripped, canary_http_tripped, canary_account_tripped isolate_host approval required intercept ACL/firewall rule native deny + journal plan-gated; dry-run first

Policy lives in config.json:

{
  "enforcement": {
    "enabled": true,
    "mode": "enforce",
    "min_score": 9,
    "allowed_actions": ["snapshot", "kill_process"],
    "require_approval": [
      "isolate_host", "quarantine_file", "disable_user", "remove_admin",
      "stop_service", "rotate_credential", "delete_task", "disable_task",
      "remove_run_key", "disable_wmi_sub", "block_ip"
    ],
    "cooldown_minutes": 30,
    "max_actions_per_run": 2,
    "watch_task": "PlasmaWatch",
    "watch_every_minutes": 5
  }
}

Evidence before containment. A kill destroys the in-memory artifact the injection detection exists to surface. Before the first automatic kill in a run, Plasma writes one host-state snapshot through the same dry-run + plan gate. The snapshot is a read-only export (users, admins, services, tasks, firewall, audit policy) — it does not capture process memory. If the snapshot fails, containment still proceeds and the journal records capture: failed.

Operators who want forensics ahead of speed can either:

  • remove "snapshot" from allowed_actions to skip the capture, or
  • move "kill_process" into require_approval so every kill is human-gated and the capture can be examined first.

Guardrails are code, not convention:

  • Armed by default, narrow — only snapshot + kill_process at score 9+, with a per-run cap and cooldown.
  • Allowlist — a finding cannot select an action outside the policy lists.
  • Approval gate — high/critical actions queue as pending; nothing runs until a human approves.
  • Blast radius — score floor, per-run cap, per-action+target cooldown.
  • Kill switch — actuate's kill switch still blocks every apply.
  • Journal — enforce-journal.jsonl records the finding digest, decision, reasons, plan id and verification.

Every apply still goes through actuate: dry-run first, plan id required, undo recipe recorded. The installer registers PlasmaWatch, which runs plasma watch once --enforce every 5 minutes as SYSTEM. Run it manually with plasma watch once --enforce, or remove the task with --no-autoprotect and use plasma protect disarm.

docs.title: Tier 1 — Windows enforcement points
docs.text:
plasma prevent status
plasma prevent applocker --mode audit                     # plan only
plasma prevent applocker --mode audit --apply --plan 3 --reason "pilot"
plasma prevent egress --allow 10.0.0.0/8 --allow 1.2.3.4:443
plasma prevent asr --ids <GUID> --action Audit
plasma prevent lsa
plasma prevent rollback --id 7 --apply

All controls are dry-run first and plan-gated: the apply requires the id of a dry-run whose rendered payload digest still matches, plus a reason.

docs.title: AppLocker
docs.text:
Generates an Exe policy with allow rules for %WINDIR%, Program Files (both), optional --allow-path entries, and a permanent Administrators path rule so an enforcement mistake cannot lock the operator out of their own tooling. Default mode is audit; --mode enforce turns it into blocking. Rollback restores the previous effective policy, or clears the local SrpV2 policy when there was none.

AppLocker controls execution, not scripts; pair it with PowerShell logging and constrained language mode where appropriate.

docs.title: Firewall egress
docs.text:
Creates PlasmaPrevent-Egress-* rules: one allow per destination, then a default-block outbound rule (Windows gives explicit allows precedence). An an allowlist is mandatory — blocking all egress without DNS and update destinations locks the host out of patching. Plasma warns when no port-53 destination is present, but it does not guess your DNS servers; add them explicitly. Rollback removes the prefix rules.

Blocking outbound does not affect inbound WinRM/RDP, but it will break anything that needs the internet; pilot it and keep the allowlist current.

docs.title: Defender ASR
docs.text: Applies attack-surface-reduction rule GUIDs in Audit, Enabled (block) or Disabled mode. Requires Defender to be present and not fully managed by policy that overrides local settings. Rollback restores each rule's previous action.

docs.title: LSA protection
docs.text: Sets RunAsPPL=1 under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa. Takes effect after a reboot. Rollback removes the value. Check third-party LSA plugins before enabling it in production.

docs.title: What this is not
docs.text:
• Not a driver. Plasma has no kernel component. File-write and network blocking are delegated to Defender's Controlled Folder Access and Network Protection; execution blocking is AppLocker. There is no Plasma-owned pre-execution veto or packet filter.
  • Not agentless prevention. AppLocker, ASR, CFA and Network Protection are endpoint-local controls; a host that is offline from management still enforces its own policy.
  • Not a substitute for backups. Every control here is reversible, and the journal is the audit trail that proves what changed.

docs.title: Posture and Defender controls
docs.text:
plasma prevent posture

Inventory of the signed enforcement points Plasma delegates to: active WDAC policy files, Defender Controlled Folder Access, Network Protection, the Microsoft vulnerable driver blocklist, ASR rule counts, real-time protection and tamper protection. Each row says whether Plasma can apply it and names the preview command. Gaps come with recommendations.

WDAC stays read-only: a bad code-integrity policy can stop a host booting, and recovery may need offline action. CFA, Network Protection and the driver blocklist are opt-in, plan-gated and reversible.

docs.title: Controlled Folder Access
docs.text:
plasma prevent cfa --mode audit
plasma prevent cfa --mode audit --apply --plan 7 --reason "pilot"
plasma prevent cfa --mode block --apply --plan 8 --reason "enforce"
plasma prevent rollback --id 8

Modes are off, audit and block; the default is audit. Apply captures the current value before writing, verifies the resulting value, and journals the previous value for rollback. A policy-managed host may ignore the local setting; that is reported as a failed apply, not a false success.

docs.title: Network Protection
docs.text:
plasma prevent network --mode audit
plasma prevent network --mode audit --apply --plan 9 --reason "pilot"
plasma prevent network --mode block --apply --plan 10 --reason "enforce"
plasma prevent rollback --id 10

Same discipline as CFA. Network Protection can affect browsers, updaters and telemetry endpoints; pilot in audit first.

docs.title: Vulnerable driver blocklist
docs.text:
plasma prevent driver-blocklist
plasma prevent driver-blocklist --apply --plan 11 --reason "baseline"
plasma prevent driver-blocklist --off
plasma prevent rollback --id 11

Writes VulnerableDriverBlocklistEnable under the Code Integrity config key and captures the previous value. A reboot may be required before the change is fully effective. Plasma never reboots the host.

docs.title: Posture and rollback safety
docs.text:
• Every apply is dry-run first, single-use, payload-bound and reason-gated.
  • The kill switch blocks applies while leaving previews available.
  • Rollback verifies the restored value, not just that PowerShell returned.
  • The journal records the control, mode, previous value, plan, reason and verification result.

This is deliberately an inventory first: a control that is off is reported as off. CFA and Network Protection can be changed through Plasma, but only as an explicit, previewed, plan-gated action. Both can break line-of-business applications if applied without a pilot, so audit mode is the default.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
plasma prevent status
plasma prevent posture
plasma enforce status
Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'PlasmaPrevent-*'
Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective | Select-Object -ExpandProperty RuleCollections

docs.title: Behavioural profiles and anomaly scores
docs.text: Plasma's detection has always been deterministic: gene rules, chains, drift checks and fleet joins. Profiles add the missing baseline layer without adding a log lake.

docs.title: The two tiers
docs.text:
Tier 1 — the host. plasma profile build reduces a bounded tail of the local JSONL store into counts: images, parent→child edges, identity→image pairs, destination families, registry and file families, command-line shapes, and robust hourly volume per entity. The result is tens of kilobytes. It never contains event rows, full command lines, file paths or URLs.

Tier 2 — the estate. plasma fleet profiles asks each host to build its own profile and brings back only that profile. Host profiles merge into one estate profile, so a desk can ask "rare here" and "rare in the estate" separately. A thousand hosts is megabytes, not a lake.

docs.title: What a profile holds
docs.text:
Table Key example Why image chrome.exe which programs this host runs parent_child explorer.exe>cmd.exe the strongest Windows behaviour edge user_image corp\olu>powershell.exe identity-to-program shape dest chrome.exe>p:443 port, else a /24 family — never a raw address registry currentversion\run\evil persistence-shaped key families file documents.ps1 sensitive-path families shape powershell -enc <b64> behaviour, not literals hourly image:chrome.exe, hour 9 median/MAD per day, per hour

Command lines are reduced before they are counted. Paths, URLs, addresses, GUIDs, long hex blobs, quoted strings and numbers collapse to placeholders; net user bob <pw> becomes net user bob <cred>. A profile is a behaviour label, not a transcript.

Profiles carry a SHA-256 over their body. plasma profile verify recomputes it, so a tampered baseline is visible rather than trusted.

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
plasma anomaly score compares recent rows with a profile and returns a 0–10 score built from named components:

Component Weight Signal edge 1.5 parent→child rarity image 1.0 program rarity user_image 0.8 identity/program rarity dest 0.7 destination family rarity registry 0.8 registry family rarity file 0.4 file family rarity shape 0.8 command-shape rarity volume 1.2 robust z of the day's hourly count estate 1.5 rarity in the merged estate profile

Each component reports count/total, first_seen, and the key that produced it. The score is the weighted mean of the components that could be computed. Nothing is learned online and no opaque model sits in the path.

Routine Windows servicing (services.exe, svchost.exe, wuauclt.exe and similar) is damped by 0.55. A rare child of a service host still appears, at triage level, instead of turning a patched server red. Only the shipped Plasma binaries are skipped by default (--include-self shows them), so an upgrade cannot dominate its own ranking while a look-alike name is still scored. Bands are critical at 9.0+, high at 7.5+, medium at 6.0+.

Cold start is explicit. Below 50 observations, or when no table has data, the score is null with cold_start: true. Plasma would rather say "I do not know yet" than manufacture confidence.

docs.title: Traces
docs.text:
plasma anomaly trace joins process spans into trees using PID/PPID within one host. A parent link is the most recent earlier span with that PID on that host, which handles PID reuse. Traces never cross hosts: an RDP or SMB hop creates a new logon and therefore a new tree. Cross-host identity joins belong to fleet.

With --profile, each trace is scored by the rarity of its parent→child edges. First-seen edges are listed explicitly.

docs.title: Learning lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Observe. Run the identity pull and WHIDS for at least a week.
  2. Learn. plasma profile build --since 7d --out profile.json.
  3. Freeze. Diff against the previous profile; investigate new edges before accepting them.
  4. Detect. plasma anomaly score --profile profile.json --since 1h.
  5. Re-learn deliberately after a role change or a long patch window. A stale baseline is worse than a cold one.

docs.title: What this is not
docs.text:
• Not an auto-containment trigger. Scores are for triage. Response stays plan-gated and explicit.
  • Not a replacement for rules or chains. A signature still catches the obvious intrusion faster than a baseline notices the shape.
  • Not poison-proof by itself. Sign profiles, and re-baseline through a change window rather than during one. An attacker who can rewrite the baseline can normalise themselves.
  • Not a log shipper. Only counts cross the wire.

docs.title: Related commands
docs.text:
plasma profile build   --events events.jsonl --role member --out profile.json
plasma profile show    --profile profile.json
plasma profile diff    --old last-week.json --new profile.json
plasma profile merge   --profiles ws1.json ws2.json --out estate.json
plasma profile verify  --profile estate.json
plasma anomaly score   --events events.jsonl --profile profile.json --estate estate.json
plasma anomaly explain --events events.jsonl --profile profile.json --contains powershell
plasma anomaly trace   --events events.jsonl --profile profile.json --min-spans 3
plasma fleet profiles  --inventory hosts.json --out-dir estate

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Plasma's response layer follows one promise: a human decides, a machine executes carefully — and everything is reversible or visibly not.

There are three ways to act, and they are deliberately separate:

Plane Command Gate Manual response plasma actuate / playbook --apply --plan <seen dry-run> Automatic containment plasma enforce policy + approval queue + actuate plan gate Inline prevention plasma prevent dry-run plan + payload digest + rollback id

See Prevention and blocking for the latter two.

docs.title: The gate
docs.text:
# 1. render the exact payload (nothing runs)
plasma actuate apply block_ip --target 203.0.113.9 --reason "C2" --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma

# 2. the dry-run is journaled with an id (say, 7). Apply THAT plan:
plasma actuate apply block_ip --target 203.0.113.9 --reason "C2" --apply --plan 7

# 3. if it was wrong:
plasma actuate undo --id 8 --apply

Rules enforced by code, not documentation:

  • --apply without --plan is refused. The plan id must reference a seen dry-run of the same action and target, and the rendered payload digest must still match (state moved on → re-run the dry-run).
  • Allowlisted actions only. There is no run_command.
  • Protected targets (WinRM, TermService, Winlogon, csrss, lsass, Sysmon, WHIDS, Administrator, …) are refused before any payload runs.
  • Journal first. Every dry-run, apply, failure and undo is appended to actuate-journal.jsonl. A torn line cannot brick the journal.
  • Undo where possible. Each action carries an undo payload or a structured recipe; actions that cannot be undone are marked undoable: false and the CLI says so.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Action Target What it does Undo block_ip IPv4 Inbound + outbound firewall block (two named rules) remove rules isolate_host — Block all traffic after creating RDP-3389 and WinRM-5985 allow rules remove rules disable_user local user Disable-LocalUser enable remove_admin local user remove from Administrators re-add kill_process PID capture identity, then Stop-Process -Force none (by design) quarantine_file absolute path move to C:\ProgramData\Plasma\Quarantine move back stop_service service Stop-Service -Force start disable_task task name back up XML, disable the task enable delete_task task name back up XML, unregister re-register from XML remove_run_key HKLM:\…\Run|Name capture the value, delete it (string values only, allowlisted keys) restore value disable_wmi_sub — remove filter-to-consumer bindings; definitions kept re-bind rotate_credential local user new random password, printed once, never journaled none snapshot — users, admins, services, tasks, firewall, audit policy → JSON none (it is the backup)

isolate_host is deliberately lockout-proof: Windows evaluates more-specific allow rules first, so management access survives full isolation. That ordering is tested.

docs.title: Playbooks
docs.text:
A playbook is a fixed sequence of the actions above, applied as one plan-gated unit:

Playbook Steps contain-user <user> disable_user → snapshot isolate-box isolate_host → snapshot 
plasma playbook apply contain-user --target bob --reason "lateral hop, no ticket"
# → journals one dry-run per step + a playbook dry-run; returns its id

plasma playbook apply contain-user --target bob --reason "lateral hop, no ticket" --apply --plan 12

# reverse the succeeded steps, last-first (non-undoable steps are skipped, visibly)
plasma playbook undo --id 13 --apply

Behavior: abort on the first failing step (the journal records exactly how far it got), and reversal walks backward so dependent steps are undone in the right order.

docs.title: Journal
docs.text:
plasma actuate journal --last 20

Each entry: id, ts, action, target, reason, mode (dry-run/applied), payload_sha256, result (rc + bounded output), verification, undo, and for playbooks steps[] / aborted_at.

docs.title: Plugin actions
docs.text:
Responder plugins contribute named actions to the same gate. They do not get a shell and they do not bypass the plan:

plasma plugin actions
plasma plugin act acme.restart_agent --args-file args.json
plasma plugin act acme.restart_agent --args-file args.json --apply --plan <id> --reason "change window"
plasma plugin undo <journal-id> --reason "rollback"

Preview renders the exact argv and stores a plan id. Apply requires that id and a reason, checks the kill switch and the plugin's enabled state, runs only the declared argv, verifies and journals the rollback. Path arguments must resolve under the plugin's permissions.filesystem roots. See Plugins.

docs.title: Safety rules of thumb
docs.text:
1. Snapshot before containment. plasma actuate apply snapshot costs seconds and gives you the pre-change world.
  2. Isolate, don't kill. isolate_host keeps the management channel; kill_process cannot be undone.
  3. Verify, don't assume. Every apply runs a verification payload; a failed verification exits non-zero.
  4. Read the payload. The dry-run is the contract. If you would not type that PowerShell yourself, do not apply it.

docs.title: Security audit — 1.24.0
docs.text: Scope: the Python package, CLI, MCP server, HTTP API, prevention controls and release path at tag v1.24.0. This is an engineering self-audit, not an independent penetration test or certification.

docs.title: Checks run
docs.text: Check Result pytest -q -W error pass ruff check plasma tests pass bandit -r plasma 0 high / 0 medium; 107 low (subprocess by design) pip-audit no known vulnerable dependencies Estate install WS1 and WS2 on 1.24.0; release hash matches SHA256SUMS

docs.title: Findings fixed
docs.text: Finding Fix SHA-1 used for bounded file-change heads was flagged as a security hash Marked usedforsecurity=False; it is a change detector, not a signature urllib accepted file: and plain-HTTP URLs New netguard.require_https; all four download paths now refuse non-HTTPS, embedded credentials and control characters Sysmon XML parser accepted DTD/entity input Size cap plus explicit <!DOCTYPE / <!ENTITY refusal before parsing Query regex had no length bound 256-character cap, still compiled before use Detection case files had no size/count bound 4 MiB and 500-case caps MCP get_case was marked read but wrote report.md Report rendering is now in-memory for MCP; only CLI case report writes Memory triage had no target cap Hard cap of 50 targets

docs.title: Residual risks
docs.text:
• subprocess is used deliberately to drive fixed PowerShell payloads. The allowlisted action model, literal quoting and plan gate are the control; arbitrary shell is never exposed through MCP.
  • A local administrator can tamper with the event store, policy files or journal. Plasma detects case/report tampering and anchors the ledger, but it does not claim to defeat a hostile administrator.
  • CFA, Network Protection and the driver blocklist can be overridden by policy. Apply verifies the resulting value and fails rather than claiming success.
  • WDAC remains read-only by design.
  • The estate test covers two Windows Server 2022 hosts, not every Windows 10/11 build, domain-controller topology or high-load profile.
  • No independent MITRE ATT&CK evaluation or third-party penetration test has been performed.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: Treat 1.24.0 as a hardened field release, not a certified product. Run the prevention controls in audit mode first, keep the kill switch tested, and review the journal after every apply/rollback drill.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text: This page states what Plasma guarantees, what it explicitly does not, and where the trust anchors are. It is written to be useful to a reviewer, not to a marketing page.

docs.title: Guarantees
docs.text:
1. Read-only collectors; measured mutations. Collectors and probes read. Mutations happen only in two measured planes:
  2. Containment (actuate, driven by plasma enforce) — named, reversible actions behind a plan gate and a policy. Automatic containment ships armed but narrow: snapshot + kill_process at score 9+, with isolation and every other action behind approval.
  3. Enforcement points (plasma prevent) — AppLocker, firewall, Defender ASR and LSA controls, audit-first, plan-gated on the rendered payload and rollbackable by journal id.
  4. Gate is enforced in code. Manual applies require --plan <dry-run id> matching the action, target and payload digest. Automatic containment still runs through actuate's dry-run + plan gate, and only after a written policy allows the action and a human approves high/critical actions.
  5. Allowlisted actions only. No arbitrary shell. Targets are validated against strict patterns; protected services, processes and accounts are refused before any payload runs.
  6. Lockout-resistant.
  7. isolate_host creates RDP-3389 and WinRM-5985 allow rules before any block rule (Windows gives specific allows precedence).
  8. The installer never disables remote management.
  9. stop_service/kill_process/disable_user refuse the management and security stack.
  10. Health permanently checks fDenyTSConnections and SecurityLayer.
  11. Everything is journaled. Dry-runs, applies, failures, verifications and undos land in actuate-journal.jsonl; a torn line cannot brick it.
  12. Undoable where claimed. Actions that cannot be undone are marked undoable: false up front (kill_process, rotate_credential).
  13. Local by default. Events stay on the host. The desk pulls bounded tails over the existing management channel; nothing phones home.
  14. Deterministic detection. Detection is written rules and sequences; the on-device model never decides guilt and never executes anything.
  15. Bounded. Every collector has a time window, a row cap and a size cap.

docs.title: Trust anchors
docs.text: Anchor Where it lives Protects Payload manifest (SHA-256 per file) inside the installed bundle tampered sensor payloads Release SHA256SUMS published with each release corrupted downloads Pinned Authenticode signer baked into the installed exe (update.py) a compromised release page/repository WHIDS detect-only config config.toml (all action bands report) the sensor acting destructively Enforcement policy + journal config.json, enforce-journal.jsonl unattended actions exceeding policy Capture-before-containment host snapshot written before the first automatic kill losing host state to its own response Prevention journal + backups prevent-journal.jsonl, prevent-backups/ unrecoverable policy changes Sigma corpus provenance sigma-sources.json, SIGMA-DRL-1.1.md untraceable or mislicensed detection content Telemetry provenance sysmon-config.xml → coverage telemetry claiming coverage from rules that cannot fire Refusal gate (GATE_VERSION 1) frozen instance the model guessing instead of refusing

docs.title: Plugin trust model
docs.text:
A plugin is code you chose to run. Plasma reduces the blast radius but does not make an untrusted plugin safe.

  • Signature and digest. Install verifies the payload digest and an Ed25519 signature against an embedded key; pass --pubkey to pin a publisher. plugin verify recomputes the digest and exits 2 on any change. Unsigned installs require --allow-unsigned.
  • No store write. Plugins emit records; the host validates, stamps the source, dedupes and appends. A plugin cannot forge another sensor.
  • No shell. Responders declare argv arrays. Plasma owns the plan id, the reason requirement, the kill switch, the journal and the rollback.
  • Declared roots. Path arguments in responder actions are confined to permissions.filesystem.
  • Resource caps. Line size, event count, timeout and stderr size are enforced; ten invalid records quarantine the run.
  • Process isolation. A plugin runs as a child process with its own working directory. Job Objects/AppContainer isolation is the next hardening step.
  • Secrets. Injected as environment variables at start; never written to the manifest, registry or logs.
  • No core mutation. Plugins cannot change config, rules, baselines or services. A compromised plugin can emit false data; it cannot disable Plasma.

docs.title: Threat model boundaries
docs.text:
In scope for detection:

  • commodity post-exploitation, living-off-the-land, credential access, persistence, lateral movement, logon abuse, data-staging indicators;
  • persistence inventory and signature anomalies (deep probe);
  • image/process-level events (Sysmon), script-block content (tap), identity events (Security channel).

Explicitly out of scope (today):

  • Inline blocking from a Plasma driver. Plasma ships no minifilter, WFP callout or process-veto driver. Prevention is delivered through Windows enforcement points (AppLocker, firewall, Defender ASR, LSA protection) configured by plasma prevent, plus containment actions. A process can therefore execute once before containment.
  • Kernel-level self-protection. There is no Plasma driver; a local administrator can stop the services. (Sysmon and WHIDS can be protected by their own mechanisms, but Plasma does not claim tamper-proof operation against a determined admin.)
  • Full memory forensics. No LSASS/host memory acquisition. The deep probe and syscall-level evidence are as far as it goes; DTrace integration is a roadmap item, not a claim.
  • Ransomware impact (T1486). Detected through canary files (plasma canary deploy, verified on every watch): a missing or modified decoy is a score-10 finding. This is deliberately not an "encryption burst" heuristic; the coverage report attributes the technique to canary:verify. DNS and HTTP tokens add access/recon tripwires without cloud callbacks; HTTP tokens use a loopback-first local collector.
  • Endpoint DLP / content inspection. Not attempted.
  • Memory scanning is point-in-time. HollowsHunter/PE-sieve is a user-mode probe, not a kernel monitor. It can miss a short-lived implant between scans, cannot read every protected process and may produce managed-JIT noise; Plasma suppresses that specific class. Dumps are opt-in, local and sensitive.
  • Kernel interception. Plasma compiles policy into NTFS ACLs, Windows Firewall and the MCP boundary. It does not ship a minifilter, WFP callout or API hook; kernel-mode malware and direct syscalls remain outside the claim.

docs.title: Data handling
docs.text:
• Events: JSONL on the endpoint, rotation/compaction under operator control.
  • Identity: SIDs/usernames as Windows reports them; machine accounts dropped.
  • Alerts: Telegram/webhook payloads include finding text — no raw event bodies by default; paths/usernames may appear in descriptions.
  • Fleet: passwords only via environment variables (password_env); inline secrets in inventory or notify configs are refused.
  • Response: rotate_credential prints the new password once and never writes it to the journal.

docs.title: Estate ledger data handling
docs.text:
plasma estate build runs on the endpoint and reduces a bounded window to counts. The ledger contains account names, first/last timestamps, bounded source addresses, logon types, user>process pairs and file hashes. It does not contain command lines, file paths, event descriptions or the event rows themselves. Machine and service accounts are excluded.

Every ledger carries a SHA-256 over its canonical body. plasma estate load, merge --dir and status recompute it and refuse a modified ledger. This is an integrity check, not a signature: it detects corruption and casual edits, while the trust boundary remains the desk's filesystem ACL and the WinRM channel. The desk stores one current ledger per host under hosts/ and replaces it on each pull; retention is an explicit copy, not an implicit history. Transport to the desk is WinRM (HTTPS recommended) or a local file for air-gapped estates.

docs.title: Update integrity
docs.text: From 1.2.0 the update path verifies two independent anchors: the published SHA-256 and the pinned signer thumbprint. A release that is not signed by a pinned certificate is refused before execution. The default pin is the project's self-signed certificate; the SignPath Foundation thumbprint will be added when that application is approved.

docs.title: Verification posture
docs.text:
• 264 automated tests, including detection-content tests that require every gene rule to compile and behave on positive/negative cases.
  • CI runs the test matrix on Linux and Windows, compiles the ETW tap and self-tests it, builds the single-file exe and smoke-tests it.
  • Golden gates verify the frozen instance's probe answers before release.

If you find a defect, open an issue on GitHub with the command, the output and the expected behavior.

docs.title: Secure defaults (1.9.0)
docs.text:
• The Plasma root is restricted to SYSTEM and Administrators at install (well-known SIDs, so it works on non-English Windows). Policy, kill-switch state, approvals, ledger and events are not readable by standard users.
  • Credential-bearing command lines are redacted at WHIDS normalization; plasma store redact --events <path> migrates an older store.
  • MCP tenant and scopes come from PLASMA_TENANT / PLASMA_SCOPES, not from the caller's _meta; client claims require PLASMA_TRUST_CLIENT_META=1. Read tools are tenant-filtered.
  • WinRM fleet transport requires HTTPS unless allow_insecure_winrm: true is set for a controlled lab.
  • The DTrace MSI is executed only after a valid Microsoft Authenticode signature check.
  • HTTP webhook notification URLs are refused; Telegram tokens are redacted from error strings.

docs.title: Sensors
docs.text: Sensors detect. They do not act: containment is a separate, measured plane and prevention is audit-first, described in Prevention and blocking.

docs.title: Sysmon — the kernel flight recorder
docs.text:
The foundation. Plasma provisions the official Sysmon build with a baseline configuration and depends on its Event Log channel for process, network, DNS and file telemetry.

  • Install: downloaded by the intelligent installer, EULA accepted non-interactively (-accepteula).
  • Health: sysmon_service (service running), sysmon_feed (newest Sysmon event within 60 minutes) and sysmon_config (the installed config enables every event ID the rules need) are part of plasma health.
  • Read: via Event Log API and WHIDS; never by loading a driver of our own.
  • Baseline config enables: ProcessCreate (1), NetworkConnect (3), DriverLoad (6), ImageLoad (7, unsigned only), ProcessAccess (10, LSASS only), FileCreate (11), RegistryEvent (12/13/14), PipeEvent (17/18, CreatePipe only), DnsQuery (22) and FileDelete (23, executable/archive extensions only). The bounded filters keep volume down without making the rules dormant. On a node where Sysmon already runs, apply the updated config with Sysmon64.exe -c C:\ProgramData\Plasma\tools\plasma-sysmon-baseline.xml.

docs.title: WHIDS — written suspicion rules
docs.text:
WHIDS 1.7.0 reads Sysmon and applies gene rules — written expressions with an ATT&CK technique and a criticality of 0–10. Plasma ships twenty-five baseline rules:

Rule Score Looks for LOLBin Certutil 7 certutil -urlcache / -decode Office Spawning Shell 8 winword/excel/outlook → cmd/powershell/wscript/cscript/mshta SAM Hive Dump 9 reg save hklm\sam / hklm\system Bitsadmin Transfer 7 bitsadmin /transfer, /create Mshta Network 8 mshta with an HTTP(S) or UNC target (local paths excluded) Rundll32 JS 8 rundll32 javascript: / url.dll / RunHTMLApplication Net Account Add 8 net user … /add, net localgroup … /add Encoded Cmd 6 -enc, -ec, -EncodedCommand Scheduled Task Create 6 schtasks /create Wmic Process Call 7 wmic process call create File Delete by LOLBin 6 cmd/powershell/certutil/bitsadmin/wmic/reg deleting .exe/.ps1/archives (Sysmon 23/26) Run Key Persistence 7 CurrentVersion\Run(Once) registry write (Sysmon 12/13) Service Registry Persistence 8 System\CurrentControlSet\Services\ write (Sysmon 12/13) Privileged Group Add 8 net localgroup administrators … /add Execution From User Paths 6 process running from Downloads / Temp / Users\Public LSASS Access 9 Sysmon 10 — a process opening LSASS with credential-dump access Unsigned Driver Load 8 Sysmon 6 — driver from a user-writable path, signature missing/invalid Suspicious Named Pipe 8 Sysmon 17/18 — PsExec/Cobalt-shaped pipe names Masqueraded System Binary 9 svchost/lsass/csrss/… running from outside System32/SysWOW64/WinSxS PowerShell Download 7 4104 script block using WebClient/DownloadFile/Invoke-WebRequest WMI Recon 6 4104 script block querying Win32_ system classes Wmic Recon 6 wmic … get/list/where for os/account/service/disk information

WHIDS runs detect-only: every action band is configured to report. The v1.7.0 engine has no response verbs at all; Plasma keeps it that way on purpose. Alerts land in C:\Program Files\Whids\Logs\Alerts\ and are normalized into the events store by plasma whids pull.

Detect-only describes this sensor, not the whole product. Containment is a separate, measured layer — plasma enforce is armed by default but limited to snapshot + kill at score 9+, with approval for isolation and every other action — and plasma prevent configures Windows enforcement points audit-first.
