See Prevention and blocking.

Pushed IOCs live in Database\Rules\plasma-iocs.gen and are regenerated by plasma whids push --apply from high-confidence events.

docs.title: Plugin sensors
docs.text: plasma plugin runs an external sensor or detector process with a manifest, a signed payload and an NDJSON contract. Records are validated, capped and stamped before they reach the store; responders are plan-gated. See Plugins for the ABI, lifecycle and security model.

docs.title: Identity — the Security channel
docs.text:
Audit events (4624/4625) are written by LSA directly into the Security channel and are not re-emitted to realtime ETW sessions (proven on a live host: a 75-second trace saw zero of them). Plasma therefore reads the channel through the Event Log API:

plasma identity pull --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl --since 60
Events Kind What it adds 4624 / 4625 auth logon success/failure, type, source, workstation 4768 / 4769 / 4770 / 4771 auth Kerberos TGT, service ticket, renewal, pre-auth failure (KDC only) 4776 auth NTLM credential validation 4688 process process creation with creator, parent image and command line

Auth records carry user, dest_ip (source address), logon type, workstation, process basename and a UTC timestamp. Success is info; failure is medium (score 0.5). Duplicates are removed by hash. The PlasmaIdentityPull task runs the same bounded pull every 15 minutes.

docs.title: ETW tap — the on-demand microphone
docs.text:
plasma-tap.exe (krabsetw) opens a trace session for a bounded window, matches events against 31 rules, prints JSONL matches, and exits. No service, no persistence, no standing driver of ours.

plasma tap list                                   # rules
plasma tap selftest                               # compile + self-check
plasma tap run --providers powershell,dns,wmi --for 10s --max-matches 500

Providers: PowerShell (4104 script blocks), WMI activity, DNS client, .NET runtime, Schannel, and Security-Auditing aliases. Rules are case-insensitive substring matches on a named field, with event_id = 0 meaning "any". Notable rules include Invoke-Mimikatz, MiniDumpWriteDump, amsiInitFailed, IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient, Invoke-Shellcode, __EventFilter/ActiveScriptEventConsumer, ngrok and trycloudflare queries.

Tap exit codes are meaningful: 3 means the session could not be started (no admin rights or ETW unavailable) — the tap never pretends.

docs.title: Deep persistence probe
docs.text:
Sysmon sees persistence changes; plasma deep persistence sees the whole picture:

plasma deep persistence --json-out C:\ProgramData\Plasma\deep-persistence.json

It reads, in one bounded pass:

  • registry Run / RunOnce keys (HKLM and HKCU),
  • services with their ImagePath, start mode and account,
  • scheduled-task actions and triggers (Microsoft paths excluded),
  • IFEO Debugger hijacks,
  • Winlogon Shell / Userinit,
  • WMI event filters, consumers and binding count.

Every binary path found gets an Authenticode check (bounded, capped). An item is flagged suspect when it is unsigned and outside C:\Windows. That flag is evidence for a human — never an automatic action.

docs.title: DTrace — the on-demand microscope
docs.text:
The third detection layer. WHIDS and the tap are always-on and cheap; DTrace is surgical: a reviewed script, a bounded window, then gone. It is never installed silently by the installer — plasma trace provision is explicit because it changes a boot setting and needs a restart.

  • Reviewed scripts only (sensors/dtrace/*.d), validated at load time.
  • No destructive mode: -w is never passed and system() is refused.
  • Bounded: wall-clock window, row cap, process killed at the end.
  • Rows normalize to kind: "trace" with technique and score, so chains, watch, drift and fleet consume them unchanged.
  • tid is emitted rather than pid: pid is not portable across the DTrace builds found on Windows Server.

docs.title: WHIDS watchdog
docs.text: WHIDS 1.7.0 can hang in StartPending or stop after a manual restart; SCM failure actions only cover crashes. The installer registers PlasmaWhidsWatchdog (SYSTEM, every two minutes) to run plasma whids ensure, which force-stops a hung service and starts it again. plasma whids diagnose reports the task and its state; actions are logged to C:\ProgramData\Plasma\logs\whids-watchdog.log.

docs.title: Sensor-of-sensors
docs.text:
The health checks that watch the watchers:

Check Meaning sensor_heartbeat the events diary is still being written (newest row < 24h) rdp_hardening_drift fDenyTSConnections=0 and a sane SecurityLayer — the lockout-incident checks tap_sidecar the ETW tap binary is present whids_service / sysmon_feed the detection stack is alive

docs.title: HTTP API (plasma serve)
docs.text:
plasma serve exposes the entire Plasma CLI over an authenticated HTTP API. It is an alternative transport to WinRM or SSH: a jumphost, dashboard or automation calls one endpoint with an argv list, and the host runs the same command it would run locally.

It is not a general shell. The argv is parsed by the real CLI parser before anything runs, every command runs in a child process with a hard timeout, and --read-only refuses every command that changes state.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
plasma serve --port 9999 --api-key-file C:\ProgramData\Plasma\serve.key

The default bind is 127.0.0.1:9999. The default key is plasmaplasma for lab use; production should use --api-key-file or PLASMA_SERVE_API_KEY.

curl -s http://HOST:9999/healthz
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer plasmaplasma" \
  http://HOST:9999/v1/version

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Auth Purpose GET /healthz no liveness only GET /openapi.json no OpenAPI 3.1 description GET /docs no human-readable API docs GET /v1/version yes version, Python, platform, read-only flag GET /v1/commands yes the full CLI command tree with options and positionals POST /v1/exec yes run one CLI argv

docs.title: OpenAPI
docs.text:
The server publishes an OpenAPI 3.1 document at GET /openapi.json (no auth) and a self-contained HTML reference at GET /docs (no auth). The spec covers the four API routes, both auth schemes (bearerAuth and apiKeyAuth), the request/response envelopes and the error responses.

curl -s http://HOST:9999/openapi.json | jq '.info'
curl -s http://HOST:9999/openapi.json | jq '.paths | keys'

POST /v1/exec is deliberately generic: the spec describes the argv envelope, while the full command surface is discoverable at GET /v1/commands (134 commands plus a separate root object, each with options, positionals, argparse types, mutating flags, long-running markers, a summary, description, examples, safety class and related commands). A per-command OpenAPI schema would duplicate the argparse tree and drift; the enriched command tree is the better contract. For the complete catalog as one document, call POST /v1/exec with {"argv": ["help", "--json"]}.

The spec is generated from plasma/openapi.py and its info.version tracks the package version. A unit test asserts that the spec paths and the server routes do not drift apart.

docs.title: POST /v1/exec
docs.text:
{"argv": ["health", "--root", "C:\\ProgramData\\Plasma"]}

or the equivalent:

{"command": "health", "args": ["--root", "C:\\ProgramData\\Plasma"]}

The response is the command's exit code plus its captured output:

{
  "ok": true,
  "exit_code": 0,
  "command": "health",
  "argv": ["health"],
  "stdout": "{ ... }",
  "stderr": "",
  "result": { "...": "parsed JSON when stdout is JSON" },
  "truncated": false,
  "duration_ms": 412.7
}

ok is true only when the command exited 0. A command that ran and returned a non-zero exit code is still an HTTP 200; inspect exit_code. HTTP 4xx means the request was refused before the command ran.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Send either header:

Authorization: Bearer <key>
X-API-Key: <key>

The key is compared in constant time. It is never written to the audit log; only a 12-character SHA-256 prefix is recorded.

Resolution order:

  1. --api-key
  2. PLASMA_SERVE_API_KEY
  3. --api-key-file (first non-empty line)
  4. plasmaplasma

docs.title: Read-only mode
docs.text:
plasma serve --read-only

Every command that changes host or Plasma state is refused with HTTP 403 and code: "read_only". This includes any --apply, install, update apply, control policy set, control killswitch on/off, prevent *, actuate apply/undo, playbook apply/undo, fleet pull/scan, store rotate/compact/redact, identity pull/schedule, trace run, tap run, whids push/ensure/prune, canary deploy, fim baseline, notify test, eval run, drift record, evidence export, assurance sbom, and the ring/rollback commands.

Read-only commands such as health, status, coverage, chain score, actuate actions, control policy show, control approvals list, control audit verify, fleet reports, trace list, tap list and observe remain available.

docs.title: TLS
docs.text:
plasma serve --tls-cert C:\ProgramData\Plasma\serve.crt `
             --tls-key  C:\ProgramData\Plasma\serve.key

Both are required together. Use an internal CA certificate; do not expose the port to the public internet.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
Every call is appended to <root>/serve/audit.jsonl:

{"ts":"2026-11-17T12:00:00Z","remote":"10.0.0.5","key_id":"a1b2c3d4e5f6",
 "argv":["health"],"command":"health","exit_code":0,"duration_ms":412.7,
 "outcome":"ok","read_only":false}

The audit log never contains the API key or the command's stdout/stderr. Disable it with --no-audit only if another audit path covers the host.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Limit Default Flag Request body 1 MiB --max-body stdout/stderr per call 8 MiB --max-output Command timeout 300 s --timeout argv items 64 fixed argv item length 4096 chars fixed

Long-running commands (serve, mcp serve, watch loop, _bridge) are refused with HTTP 400 and code: "long_running"; run them from the CLI.

docs.title: Firewall and cloud security group
docs.text:
On Windows:

New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Plasma Serve 9999" `
  -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 9999 -Action Allow `
  -Profile Domain,Private

In AWS, add an inbound rule to the instance security group for TCP 9999 from the jumphost or management subnet only. Do not open it to 0.0.0.0/0.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
Use plasma serve when:

  • WinRM is disabled or blocked by policy;
  • you want one transport for Windows and Linux hosts;
  • a dashboard or automation needs a typed, auditable command surface;
  • you want a read-only observer endpoint.

Prefer WinRM/SSM when:

  • the host is already managed by those channels;
  • you need Kerberos, JEA or gMSA;
  • you do not want another listening service.

plasma serve is a narrow API, not a general remote shell. It does not replace WinRM for interactive administration, and it does not accept arbitrary commands outside the Plasma CLI.

docs.title: Sigma conversion
docs.text:
Plasma's gene schema and Sigma's detection: block describe the same thing: a log source, one or more selections, and a boolean condition. plasma sigma convert derives a .gen rule from that structure instead of hand-copying rules, and reports every rule it cannot translate.

plasma sigma convert --in .\sigma-rules --out sensors\plasma-sigma.gen
plasma sigma convert --in rule.yml --dry-run

PyYAML is loaded only when this command runs. Every other Plasma command starts and works without it; if it is missing here you get one clear message instead of an import traceback at startup.

Output is JSONL in the WHIDS gene schema, ready to drop into Database\Rules (or plasma whids push for indicators). Duplicate names are refused; the converter prints converted, files and a skipped list with the reason for each refusal.

docs.title: The vendored corpus
docs.text:
Plasma ships 259 converted SigmaHQ rules in sensors/plasma-sigma.gen, selected from the Windows/Sysmon tree at commit 54967d64 (15 November 2026). Selection is mechanical and reproducible:

  • Windows/Sysmon categories only, Sysmon event IDs 1/3/6/7/10/11/12/13/14/17/18;
  • level medium or higher (26 critical, 150 high, 83 medium);
  • one primary ATT&CK technique per rule, deduplicated, at most two per technique, capped at 300;
  • 168 techniques represented; every rule keeps its upstream author and names its source file in Meta.Comment.

The corpus is data under the Detection Rule License (DRL) 1.1, not MIT. The licence text ships as sensors/SIGMA-DRL-1.1.md; provenance and the selection counts are in sensors/sigma-sources.json. Rebuild it with:

git clone https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma /tmp/sigma
python tools/sync_sigma_corpus.py --source /tmp/sigma/rules/windows \
    --commit "$(git -C /tmp/sigma rev-parse HEAD)"

Field check: WHIDS 1.7.0 loaded 278 rules (19 baseline/IOC + 259 Sigma) on WS2 with no compile errors.

docs.title: Supported subset
docs.text: Piece Support Log sources Windows/Sysmon categories: process_creation (1), image_load (7), driver_load (6), file_event/file_create (11), network_connection (3), pipe_created (17/18), process_access (10), registry_event/registry_set (12/13/14) Explicit EventID Wins over the category default Selections maps, and lists of maps (OR) Field modifiers contains, startswith, endswith, re, all, i Conditions selection names with and / or / not and parentheses (emitted as gene !) Metadata title, description, level → criticality, attack.tXXXX tags

docs.title: Refused, with a reason
docs.text:
• non-Windows log sources;
  • 1 of selection* / all of them quantified conditions;
  • selection shapes other than maps or lists of maps;
  • rules with no EventID and no mapped category;
  • unsupported field modifiers (windash, cidr, base64offset, fieldref) — refused rather than silently mistranslated.

Refusals are data: they appear in the skipped list rather than disappearing.

docs.title: Why this shape
docs.text: Adding rules by hand does not scale and quietly drifts from the upstream corpus. A converter keeps the mapping mechanical: every generated rule has a source file, a condition, and a technique tag. It also makes coverage growth honest — a converted rule is real evidence in the always-on plane, not a relabelled keyword.

docs.title: State machines
docs.text:
Several Plasma workflows used to keep their state implicitly — in a file that might exist, a service that might be pending, or a journal row that was never marked used. v1.7.2 makes the risky ones explicit and closes the transitions that could double-execute or leave a half-finished phase.

Machine States Invariant Fix in 1.7.2 Update idle → staged → verified → installing → installed → rotated; failed A host can only be in one phase; a new run resets the phase and keeps history Persisted state/update.json; update check reports it; atomic bin rotation with recovery Approval pending → approved/denied → consumed An approval is single-use and bound to tool + args_sha256 ledger.consume_approval() checks and marks consumption under the ledger lock Actuate plan dry-run → applied A plan runs once; the payload digest must still match Reusing a plan is refused Actuate undo undo dry-run → undo applied Undo is dry-run first, single-use, digest-bound --plan required (or a prior undo dry-run); double undo refused Playbook dry-run → applied / aborted A playbook plan runs once; steps apply in order Reusing a playbook plan is refused Playbook undo undo dry-run → undo applied Each step is undone once, last-first --plan required; double undo refused Tenant ownership unassigned → tenant A host belongs to at most one tenant; unassigned falls back to default tenants.add removes the host from every other tenant Ring membership host → one ring; current ring A host is in one ring; updates check membership assign removes the host from other rings; update apply --ring gate Canary absent → deployed → intact / tripped The manifest is never half-written; duplicate paths are recorded once Atomic manifest write and path dedupe WHIDS service stopped → startpending → running → stopping; hung A hung StartPending is force-stopped then started Watchdog whids ensure; supervised install start DTrace unavailable → installed → enabled(pending reboot) → available Provisioning is idempotent; a reboot is required after enabling Capability-based readiness; explicit reboot_required Ledger append-only hash chain Every decision/action is ordered and tamper-evident Approval consumption is its own approval_use row

docs.title: Inspecting state
docs.text:
plasma update check                     # includes "state"
plasma control approvals list           # pending
plasma control audit verify             # chain integrity
plasma ring status
plasma control tenants list
plasma whids diagnose                   # service phase + watchdog
plasma trace check

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text:
• Update failed mid-phase: update check shows failed; re-run update apply. rotate_bin restores a missing bin from .old if the previous run died between renames.
  • Approval already used: the tool returns APPROVAL_INVALID; create a new dry-run and approve it again.
  • Undo needed: run the undo dry-run, then --apply --plan <id>. A second undo is refused.
  • Host in the wrong tenant: re-add it to the intended tenant; ownership moves atomically.
  • Canary manifest damaged: canary deploy re-hashes existing files and writes a fresh manifest atomically.

docs.title: Design rule
docs.text: A transition that can change a host must have one of: a typed tool and a policy decision, a single-use plan, or a single-use approval. If a step can be repeated by retrying a request, it is a bug.

docs.title: DTrace — the on-demand kernel microscope
docs.text:
Plasma already has two detection layers: WHIDS gene rules (always-on, cheap) and the ETW tap (a bounded live window over selected providers). DTrace is the third, surgical layer: kernel/user function and syscall instrumentation for a specific question, for a bounded time, then gone.

It is integrated the same way as the tap — reviewed scripts, no service, no persistence, same event contract — with one deliberate difference: provisioning is explicit, because DTrace is a kernel tracer that needs a boot-setting change and a restart. It is never installed silently by the EDR installer.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text:
Where How to get it Windows Server 2025 built-in (dtrace.exe) Windows Server 2022 / Windows 10-11 Microsoft DTrace package (Microsoft.DTrace, amd64) 
plasma trace check        # installed? enabled? which build?
plasma trace provision    # download/install the package + bcdedit /set dtrace on

provision reports reboot_required: true; after the restart:

plasma trace check        # enabled: true
plasma trace selftest     # compile every reviewed script with `dtrace -e`

provision installs the official Microsoft MSI directly when winget is absent (the default on Server 2022). It is idempotent: installed + enabled means ready, and only a missing or disabled install triggers action.

Microsoft's Download Center labels the current package 2.0, but the MSI still reports ProductVersion 1.1.0 and the tool prints Sun D 1.13.1. Plasma deliberately does not chase that version string — capability is what matters. Across the Windows Server builds in the estate, pid is readable on some and rejected with "invalid user access" on others, so the shipped scripts emit tid, which is portable and is carried in the normalized event description. DTrace relies on virtualization-based security (VBS) on modern Windows; if tracing fails to start, verify VBS is enabled and give the driver one clean restart after the MSI.

docs.title: Reviewed scripts
docs.text:
plasma trace list
Script Technique Score What it prints syscall-errors T1106 6 NT syscalls returning a non-success status: tid, image, function, status process-create T1059 5 NtCreateUserProcess / NtCreateThreadEx entries: tid, image etw-kernel-process T1057 4 ETW Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Process events (header fields only) inject-rwx T1055 5 / 8 NtProtectVirtualMemory granting RWX (base arg3 & 0xff == 0x40): tid, image, raw protection, self flag. Self-access scores 5; cross-process scores 8 inject-remote-thread T1055 6 NtCreateThreadEx with a target handle other than the caller: tid, image inject-apc T1055 5 (chain 9) NtQueueApcThread, NtQueueApcThreadEx or NtQueueApcThreadEx2: tid, image, syscall inject-hijack T1055 5 (chain 8) NtSetContextThread on a thread other than the caller (NtCurrentThread is -2): tid, image inject-hollow T1055 6 (chain 9) NtUnmapViewOfSection against another process (arg0): tid, image inject-section T1055 5 (chain 9) NtMapViewOfSection into another process (arg1 is the ProcessHandle; arg0 is the SectionHandle): tid, image inject-write T1055 5 (chain 9) NtWriteVirtualMemory into another process (arg0): tid, image

Scripts live in sensors/dtrace/*.d, carry metadata in /* */ block comments, and are validated before use: an allowlisted provider is required, system() and other destructive constructs are refused, and every script must emit lines prefixed plasma|{"…"}.

Adding a script is a review, not a config change: drop a .d file in the directory, keep the plasma| JSON contract, run plasma trace selftest.

docs.title: Bounded runs
docs.text:
plasma trace run syscall-errors --for 10s --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl
plasma trace run process-create --for 30s --max-rows 5000 --out C:\ProgramData\Plasma\trace\capture.jsonl --events <store>
  • Wall-clock window (--for, 1s–5m) — the process is killed at the end.
  • Row cap (--max-rows, default 2000).
  • Raw capture optionally kept (--out); normalized rows appended to the events store with content-hash dedupe.
  • -w (DTrace's destructive mode) is never used.

docs.title: Process-injection evidence (T1055)
docs.text:
A single RWX allocation is not a verdict: JIT compilers and some installers create executable writable pages legitimately. Trace both halves of the story and let the chain decide.

plasma trace run inject-rwx --for 30s --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl
plasma trace run inject-remote-thread --for 30s --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl
plasma chain score --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl

inject-rwx fires on NtProtectVirtualMemory when the base protection is RWX (arg3 & 0xff == 0x40). Matching the low byte is deliberate: 0x140, 0x240 and 0x440 add PAGE_GUARD, PAGE_NOCACHE or PAGE_WRITECOMBINE and are at least as suspicious as plain RWX. arg0 is the target process handle, so the row distinguishes a process flipping its own page (JIT, .NET, V8 — score 5, medium) from one flipping another process's page (injection — score 8, high).

inject-remote-thread fires on NtCreateThreadEx when the target handle is not the caller's pseudo-handle. It compares only the low 32 bits, which is stable across DTrace builds and avoids the untyped 64-bit literal problem.

inject-apc covers the NtQueueApcThread family (including NtQueueApcThreadEx2, which modern QueueUserAPC uses). A thread handle does not reveal its owning process at this boundary, so it is evidence at score 5. It is high-volume: every APC a process queues to its own threads (threadpool dispatch, .NET, routine QueueUserAPC) produces a row. Use short windows and a row cap.

injection_apc_chain escalates only the meaningful shape: a cross-process RWX flip (self=0) followed by an APC from the same image within 30 seconds, score 9. Self-RWX cannot start the chain.

injection_chain requires a cross-process RWX row ("self": 0) followed by remote thread creation, both from the same image, inside 120 seconds. The chain binds on the image name because thread creation in another process is ordinary system activity (System, svchost, the EDR itself); without binding, unrelated events would collide.

False positives: self-RWX is normal in JIT-heavy software, and remote thread creation is normal for system services. Treat the same-image, cross-process chain as the signal, not either single event — that is why the individual scripts stay at 5/6/5.

Coverage of the family: the reviewed set now covers the classic CreateRemoteThread path, RWX permission flips, APC queueing, thread context rewriting, process hollowing, section mapping and remote writes into already-executable memory. Four chains bind each primitive to a remote thread from the same image:

Chain Steps Score injection_chain RWX flip → remote thread 9 injection_apc_chain RWX flip → APC 9 injection_hollow_chain unmap → write → remote thread 9 injection_section_chain section map → remote thread 9 injection_write_chain remote write → remote thread 9 injection_hijack_chain context rewrite → remote thread 8

The write chain is the one that leaves neither an RWX flip nor a new thread on its own; it still requires the remote thread to complete the story.

Volume: inject-section is the noisiest primitive. NtMapViewOfSection is used by every memory-mapped file and .NET assembly load; the predicate requires a remote process handle (arg1), and the chain requires a remote thread, but expect rows on hosts that map sections heavily. The other three scripts are low-volume by comparison.

This is evidence, not prevention. DTrace observes the syscall boundary; it cannot block an injection. raise( remains forbidden in reviewed scripts, so Plasma can witness an injection but never stop it.

Each normalized row has kind: "trace", source: "dtrace", the script's technique and score, and the image/tid. That means chains, drift, fleet and watch consume DTrace evidence exactly like any other event:

chain: office spawn (Sysmon) → encoded PowerShell (tap) →
       syscall error on a finance file (dtrace)  =  one story, one store

docs.title: Why not always-on?
docs.text: Kernel tracing is expensive and, on hosts without VBS, invasive. Plasma's doctrine is the flashlight: tap for a cheap live window, DTrace when a case needs the syscall boundary. Always-on depth belongs to Sysmon/WHIDS, which are tuned for continuous collection.

docs.title: Coverage accounting
docs.text: DTrace scripts are on-demand evidence, so they are not counted in the always-on ATT&CK breadth number. The coverage report stays honest about what runs continuously; trace evidence shows up in findings and chains whenever an operator opens a window.

Diagnostics first:

plasma health
plasma status --events C:\ProgramData\Plasma\data\events.jsonl
plasma watch once
Get-Service Whids, Sysmon64, TermService, WinRM | Format-Table Name, Status

Failed check What it means Fix whids_service service expected but not Running Start-Service Whids; check Logs\whids.log sysmon_service Sysmon missing/stopped reinstall: plasma install --force (repair path) sysmon_feed service runs but no fresh events check the Sysmon channel; the driver may be stopped events_store store unwritable permissions on the root; disk space rdp_hardening_drift RDP disabled or security layer changed see the RDP section below

docs.title: WHIDS stuck in StartPending
docs.text:
Seen in the field on Server 2022 with WHIDS 1.7.0: the service registers, starts, and never reaches Running (deterministic init hang).

v1.4.0 handles it in three layers:

  1. Narrow channel list — channels = [...four explicit logs] instead of "all"; subscribing to every channel on the host is the known trigger.
  2. Supervised start — the installer waits up to PLASMA_WHIDS_START_TIMEOUT (default 60s) for Running; if the service is stuck in StartPending, it is force-stopped and the node is recorded as degraded/skipped instead of leaving a hung service behind.
  3. Diagnosis — plasma whids diagnose reports service state, start mode, binary/config presence, channel readability, recent SCM errors and the tail of whids.log, with the likely cause stated as data.
  4. Watchdog (1.6.0) — the installer registers the PlasmaWhidsWatchdog task (SYSTEM, every two minutes), which runs plasma whids ensure. That command is a no-op while Running; for StartPending it force-stops and starts the service (Start-Service alone cannot recover the hang); for Stopped it starts it. Actions are appended to C:\ProgramData\Plasma\logs\whids-watchdog.log.
plasma whids ensure          # heal now, print what it did
plasma whids diagnose        # includes "watchdog": {"present": true}

Interim posture on an affected node: identity + tap carry detection.

docs.title: WinRM / management access
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Port 5985 closed from outside WinRM listener not configured winrm quickconfig -force (locally) InvalidCredentials account disabled or password mismatch Enable-LocalUser, reset password Logon fails although credentials are right SeNetworkLogonRight stripped restore *S-1-5-11,*S-1-5-32-544,*S-1-5-9 via secedit, reboot RDP client: "NTLM authentication was blocked" (0x3707) hardening set RestrictReceivingNTLMTraffic=2 set to 0 under Lsa\MSV1_0, reboot Fleet pull works locally, not remotely inventory missing transport: "winrm" add it (file transport reads the desk's disk!)

docs.title: RDP
docs.text:
Classic failure chain on a hardened box:

  1. No server certificate — Schannel 36886 "no suitable default server credential". The RDP auto-cert path was broken by hardening.
  2. Key access failure — Schannel 36870 0x8009030D while loading the private key. On a box with LSA protection (RunAsPPL=1), a CNG key created by a tool can be unreadable to LSASS.
  3. Fix that worked in the field:
  4. create a cert with the legacy provider (Microsoft Enhanced Cryptographic Provider v1.0), so the key lives in C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Crypto\RSA\MachineKeys with the machine ACL;
  5. publish it to the Remote Desktop store and bind its SHA-1 thumbprint to HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp\SSLCertificateSHA1Hash;
  6. align RunAsPPL with the estate policy (if RDP must work with a CNG key, PPL off is the proven combination);
  7. full reboot (TermService restart alone may not re-init the listener).
  8. Verify from the desk: X.224 negotiation → TLS handshake completes and the presented certificate thumbprint equals the bound one.

docs.title: Detection looks quiet
docs.text:
• plasma whids status --root "C:\Program Files\Whids" — is WHIDS writing?
  • plasma store stats --events <store> — rows growing? which kinds?
  • plasma coverage — is the technique you expect actually watched?
  • plasma chain score --events <store> — chains need the sequence; a single alert is not a chain.
  • Tap rules need plasma tap run to be alive; it is deliberately on-demand, not a service.

docs.title: Update refused
docs.text:
{"stage": "signature", "ok": false, "error": "signer thumbprint mismatch"}

The downloaded exe is not signed by a pinned certificate. Do not use --allow-unsigned outside development. Check what the release actually carries:

Get-AuthenticodeSignature .\downloaded.exe | Select Status, SignerCertificate

After a legitimate signer rotation, set PLASMA_SIGNER_THUMBPRINTS or ship a build with the new default pin.

docs.title: Fleet correlation errors
docs.text: Message Meaning file not found: C:\... wrong transport — the desk tried to read a Windows path locally winrm failed: ... reachability, credentials, or NTLM policy no such case run fleet pull first odd lateral_hop windows check timestamps have Z/offsets; naive rows are treated as UTC

docs.title: PowerShell 5.1 quirks Plasma works around
docs.text:
• BOM — PowerShell-written JSON can carry a UTF-8 BOM; Plasma reads configs with utf-8-sig.
  • -Raw + -Tail cannot be combined; the fleet transport reads bytes via base64 and falls back to line mode.
  • Codepage mojibake — subprocess output is decoded as UTF-8 with replacement; non-ASCII never crashes an apply.
  • Junctions — PS 5.1 Remove-Item can hang on reparse points; Plasma uses cmd /c rmdir and handles dangling junctions explicitly.

docs.title: DTrace
docs.text:
plasma trace check        # installed? enabled? which build?
plasma trace selftest     # compile-only check of the reviewed scripts
plasma trace provision    # install the Microsoft package (direct download,
                          # no winget needed) + bcdedit /set dtrace on

enabled: false means the boot setting is off — tracing needs bcdedit /set dtrace on and a restart. available: false means the package is missing; provision downloads the official MSI directly when winget is absent (the default on Server 2022) and reports reboot_required: true.

Microsoft's current package is labelled 2.0 on the Download Center, but the MSI still reports ProductVersion 1.1.0 and the tool prints Sun D 1.13.1. That is expected: Plasma treats installed + enabled as ready rather than chasing a version string.

If DTrace refuses to start on a modern host, verify virtualization-based security (VBS) is enabled; Server 2025 ships the built-in build. A driver that is loaded but exposes no providers usually needs one clean restart after the MSI.

docs.text:
Symptom Cause Fix install: refusing unsigned no SIGNATURE or wrong key sign the plugin, or use --allow-unsigned in a lab verify exits 2 payload changed after install review, then reinstall --force run: quarantined ten invalid records read <root>\logs\plugin-<name>.log run: timeout manifest timeout reached bound the plugin or raise limits.timeout_seconds act: outside permitted roots path escaped permissions.filesystem use a declared root or update the manifest act: kill switch is engaged global/host switch on plasma control killswitch status webhook 401 missing or bad HMAC sign the body with the configured secret

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 success / clean 1 data or input error (bad inventory, missing file, collection error) 2 refused / attention (update signer mismatch, drift found, update available) 3 execution failed (actuate payload/verification, required WHIDS missing)

docs.title: Checking and applying updates
docs.text:
plasma update check    # exit 0 = current, 2 = update available
plasma update apply    # download → verify SHA-256 → verify signer → install → rotate

The repository is public, so both commands work anonymously. A token is still accepted (--token-env) for private forks.

What apply does, in order:

  1. fetches the latest release metadata,
  2. downloads the exe and SHA256SUMS,
  3. verifies the SHA-256 of the downloaded bytes,
  4. verifies the Authenticode signer against thumbprints pinned inside the installed binary — mismatch or unsigned aborts with exit 2 and the staged installer is never executed,
  5. runs the new exe's own install --force --root <same root>,
  6. rotates the canonical bin copy (rename-while-running is legal on Windows; overwriting a running exe is not).

--allow-unsigned exists for development only.

docs.title: Automatic updates
docs.text:
The installer registers PlasmaUpdate, a daily SYSTEM task with a random minute inside the 02:00–05:00 local maintenance window. It runs:

plasma update auto --root C:\ProgramData\Plasma

What the automatic path does:

  1. skips if automatic updates are disabled, the kill switch is engaged, the host is outside its ring, or it is outside the maintenance window;
  2. fetches the latest release and compares versions;
  3. on broad, waits for the canary hold (24 hours after publication); on canary, updates immediately; on rollback, never auto-updates;
  4. downloads, verifies SHA-256, and verifies the pinned Authenticode signer;
  5. runs the same install --force path, stops the tasks that hold the binary (PlasmaServe, PlasmaWatch, PlasmaWhidsWatchdog, PlasmaIdentityPull), stops every other plasma* process so PyInstaller's child cannot keep port 9999, rotates the running binary and the canonical plasma.exe, then restarts those tasks. A locked image is retried five times; a stale .old backup is preserved under a unique name; a failed swap restores the previous binary. A serve-launched update skips PlasmaServe so it cannot kill its own process tree; an explicit host ring assignment wins over the configured default;
  6. writes update-journal.jsonl and update-state.json;
  7. keeps the previous binary beside the current one, so plasma rollback still works.
plasma update auto --check-only   # exit 2 when an update is available
plasma update auto                # apply if due
plasma update auto --force        # reinstall even if the version matches
plasma update auto --ring canary  # override the configured ring

Configuration lives in config.json:

{
  "update": {
    "auto": true,
    "repo": "DrOlu/plasma",
    "ring": "broad",
    "every_hours": 24,
    "window_start_hour": 2,
    "window_end_hour": 5,
    "canary_hold_hours": 24,
    "allow_unsigned": false,
    "restart_serve": true,
    "notify": true,
    "task": "PlasmaUpdate"
  }
}

--no-autoupdate on install removes the task and disables the feature. The kill switch pauses updates without disabling the task; the next run after the switch is released picks up the release.

docs.title: The two trust anchors
docs.text:
Anchor What it protects against SHA256SUMS published with the release corrupted download, truncated transfer Pinned signer thumbprint baked into the installed exe a compromised release page / repository: an attacker who can replace both the exe and the sums still cannot forge a signature matching the pin

Default pin (self-signed project certificate, valid to 2036):

BC67B990A783702D0C4761D557A58F9AD4534A68

Rotate or extend the set without rebuilding:

$env:PLASMA_SIGNER_THUMBPRINTS = "BC67...,AB12...,CD34..."
plasma update apply

Verification reports the signer thumbprint and the chain status. Trust-chain status is informational: a lab box may not have the signer's root imported, but the pin is what matters.

docs.title: Release signing in CI
docs.text:
release.yml signs the Windows exe and the MSI with Authenticode before SHA-256 sums are computed, when repository secrets exist:

Secret Purpose SIGNING_PFX_BASE64 the PKCS#12 bundle, base64-encoded SIGNING_PFX_PASSWORD its password

The workflow imports the certificate into the ephemeral runner's trust stores (so signtool verify /pa exercises the real chain), signs with a DigiCert RFC 3161 timestamp, verifies, then hashes the signed files. The MSI is built with -arch x64, so it installs under C:\Program Files\Plasma rather than Program Files (x86). Without secrets, the release proceeds unsigned.

docs.title: Signpath Foundation (publicly trusted signing)
docs.text:
The project has applied to SignPath Foundation for free OSS code signing. Once approved:

  • Plasma's certificate is issued to the Foundation (HSM-held key), the publisher shown by Windows becomes SignPath Foundation, and SmartScreen reputation can accrue;
  • release.yml switches to signpath/github-action-submit-signing-request (the wiring is prepared in docs/SIGNPATH_APPLICATION.md);
  • the Foundation thumbprint is added to the pin set above (or passed via PLASMA_SIGNER_THUMBPRINTS during the overlap).

Note the honest caveat: a publicly trusted certificate removes the "Unknown publisher" warning and lets reputation build — it does not guarantee instant SmartScreen silence for a brand-new publisher.

docs.title: Verifying a build yourself
docs.text:
Windows:

Get-AuthenticodeSignature .\plasma-<version>-windows-x64.exe |
  Select-Object Status, SignerCertificate

Any OS with osslsigncode:

osslsigncode verify -in plasma-<version>-windows-x64.exe

Both should show the Hyperspace (or SignPath Foundation) signer and a verified timestamp.
